nodes.statement:
The statement is trivial when $\zeta > 1/4$, so assume  egin{equation} \zeta \leq 1/4. \end{equation} By ef{prop:simeq-for-measurements}, \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi} A_a \ot B_a \ket{\psi} \geq 1-\zeta. \] Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi} (A_a \ot I)\cdot(I \ot B_a)\ket{\psi} \] to obtain \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi} (A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\zeta)^2 \geq 1-2\zeta. \] Because $A$ is a measurement, this rewrites as  egin{equation} \sum_a  ra{\psi} (A_a-(A_a)^2) \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 2\zeta. \end{equation}  egin{lemma} For any $x \in [0, 1]$,  egin{equation*} (x - \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2 \leq  rac{1}{\delta} \cdot (x - x^2). \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} If $x \geq 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$. Since $\delta \leq 1/2$ below, one also has $x \geq \delta$, so \[ (x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2 = (1-x)^2 \leq (1-x) rac{x}{\delta} =  rac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2). \] If $x < 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=0$, and similarly \[ (x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2 = x^2 \leq x rac{1-x}{\delta} =  rac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2). \] \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[Rounding to projectors] There exists a set of projective matrices $\{R_a\}$ such that  egin{equation*} A_a \ot I \approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta}} R_a \ot I. \end{equation*} and  egin{equation*} R:= \sum_a R_a \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \cdot I. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Write the eigendecomposition of $A_a$ as \[ A_a = \sum_i \lambda_{a,i}\ket{u_{a,i}} ra{u_{a,i}}. \] Choose  egin{equation} 0 < \delta \leq 1/2, \end{equation} define $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta:[0,1] 	o \{0,1\}$ by $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$ when $x \geq 1-\delta$ and $0$ otherwise, and set \[ R_a = \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(A_a) = \sum_i \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(\lambda_{a,i}) \ket{u_{a,i}} ra{u_{a,i}}. \] By ef{lem:trunc-inequality}, \[ (A_a-R_a)^2 \leq  rac{1}{\delta}(A_a-(A_a)^2). \] Summing expectations and using ef{eq:A-looks-projective} gives \[ \sum_a \Vert (A_a-R_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 \leq  rac{2\zeta}{\delta}, \] so $A_a \ot I \approx_{2\zeta/\delta} R_a \ot I$. For every $x \in [0,1]$, one has $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x) \leq x/(1-\delta)$, hence \[ R_a \leq  rac{1}{1-\delta} A_a. \] Summing over $a$ and using that $A$ is a measurement, \[ R = \sum_a R_a \leq  rac{1}{1-\delta} I \leq (1+2\delta)I, \] where the last estimate uses $\delta \leq 1/2$. Setting $\delta=\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives the claim, and ef{eq:assumption-on-zeta} ensures $\delta \leq 1/2$. \end{proof}  egin{remark}[Lean auxiliary declarations for rounding to projectors] The source-facing Lean declarations for Lemma~ef{lem:projective-non-measurement} are the proposition 	exttt{projectiveNonMeasurement} and the construction theorem 	exttt{projectiveNonMeasurement\_of\_sourceAlmostProjective\_full}. The declarations listed here are the endpoint and regime splits, the 	exttt{AlmostProjMeasStatement} witness forms, and the spectral-truncation statement conversions used by later Section~5 arguments. They are not additional hypotheses in the paper statement of Lemma~ef{lem:projective-non-measurement}. \end{remark}  egin{lemma}[Combinatorial averaging for the $r > d$ branch] Let $f : \alpha 	o \mathbb{R}$ be a function on a finite index set $\alpha$ with $|\alpha| = r$, and let $L \subseteq \alpha$ with $|L| = d$ and $d < r$. Write $S = L^\complement$ and assume $f(s) \leq f(l)$ for every $s \in S$ and $l \in L$. Then the pairwise double-counting inequality \[ |L|\, \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\, \sum_{l \in L} f(l) \] holds, and hence also \[ r\, \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\, \sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x). \] If in addition $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})\,d$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1 + 2\sqrt{\zeta}$, and $0 \leq \zeta \leq 1/4$, then \[ \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}. \] \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Choose $L$ to be a set of $d$ indices on which the sum of $f$ is maximal. If some $s \in S$ and $l \in L$ satisfied $f(l) < f(s)$, replacing $l$ by $s$ would increase this sum, so every small index is bounded by every large index. Summing the inequalities $f(s) \leq f(l)$ over all pairs $(s,l) \in S 	imes L$ gives \[ |L|\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{l \in L} f(l). \] Since $\alpha$ is the disjoint union of $L$ and $S$, adding $|S|\sum_{s \in S} f(s)$ to both sides yields \[ r\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x). \] The hypotheses $|L|=d$ and $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d$ imply $|S|/r \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Dividing by $r$ and using $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives \[ \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}). \] Finally, $\zeta \leq 1/4$ implies $\sqrt{\zeta} \leq 1/2$, and hence $2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}$. \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[Rank reduction] There exists a set of projection matrices $\{Q_a\}$ such that  egin{equation*} A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I. \end{equation*} and  egin{equation*} Q:= \sum_a Q_a \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \cdot I. \end{equation*} Furthermore,  egin{equation*} \sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a) \leq d. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Let $\{R_a\}$ be given by ef{lem:projective-non-measurement}. Write $r_a=\mathrm{rank}(R_a)$ and $r=\sum_a r_a$. If $r \leq d$, take $Q_a=R_a$. Otherwise,  egin{equation} r = \sum_a r_a = \sum_a \Tr(R_a) = \Tr(R) \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d. \end{equation} Let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,r_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $R_a$, so \[ R_a = \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} \ket{v_{a,i}} ra{v_{a,i}}. \] Define the overlaps \[ o_{a,i} =  ra{\psi} (\ket{v_{a,i}} ra{v_{a,i}} \ot I)\ket{\psi}. \] Their total satisfies  egin{equation} \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} o_{a,i} =  ra{\psi} R \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}. \end{equation} Let $\mathsf{Large}$ be the set of the $d$ largest overlaps $o_{a,i}$, breaking ties arbitrarily, and let $\mathsf{Small}$ be the complement. Then  egin{equation} |\mathsf{Small}| = r-d \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,d \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,r, \end{equation} by ef{eq:bound-on-r}. Averaging the overlaps over the $r$ indices gives  egin{equation} \sum_{(a,i)\in \mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i} \leq  rac{|\mathsf{Small}|}{r}\sum_{a,i} o_{a,i} \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}, \end{equation} using ef{eq:size-of-small-is-small}, ef{eq:total-overlap}, and ef{eq:assumption-on-zeta}. For each $a$, let $\mathsf{Large}_a=\{i : (a,i)\in \mathsf{Large}\}$ and define \[ Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Large}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}} ra{v_{a,i}}. \] Then $\sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a)=|\mathsf{Large}| \leq d$, and $Q_a \leq R_a$ for every $a$, so \[ Q = \sum_a Q_a \leq \sum_a R_a = R \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I. \] Also, \[ R_a-Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Small}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}} ra{v_{a,i}} \] is a projector, hence \[ \sum_a \Vert (R_a-Q_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 = \sum_{(a,i)\in\mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i} \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta} \] by ef{eq:small-overlaps}. Therefore $R_a \ot I \approx_{4\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I$. Combining this with ef{lem:projective-non-measurement} and the triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ gives \[ A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I. \] \end{proof} Henceforth let $Q=\{Q_a\}$ be the family given by ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}.  egin{lemma}[Completeness of~$Q$]  egin{equation*}  ra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq 1 - 11 \zeta^{1/4}. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Since each $Q_a$ is projective,  egin{equation}  ra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} = \sum_a  ra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{5\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a  ra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} By Cauchy--Schwarz, \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta} \quad	ext{and}\quad \sum_a  ra{\psi} (Q_a-A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 12\sqrt{\zeta} \] from ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}. A second Cauchy--Schwarz estimate yields  egin{equation} \sum_a  ra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{4\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a  ra{\psi} (A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Combining ef{eq:Q-for-an-A} and ef{eq:another-Q-for-A} with ef{eq:A-looks-projective} gives \[  ra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_a  ra{\psi} A_a \ot I \ket{\psi} - 2\zeta - 9\zeta^{1/4} = 1 - 11\zeta^{1/4}, \] since $\zeta \leq \zeta^{1/4}$ under ef{eq:assumption-on-zeta}. \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[Completeness of~$\sqrt{Q}$]  egin{equation*}  ra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq 1 - 12 \zeta^{1/4}. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Diagonalize $Q=\sum_i 
u_i \ket{u_i} ra{u_i}$. Because $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, each $
u_i$ is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Therefore \[ \sqrt{Q} = \sum_i \sqrt{
u_i}\ket{u_i} ra{u_i} \geq  rac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} Q. \] The scalar estimate \[  rac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} \geq 1-\sqrt{\zeta} \] gives $\sqrt{Q} \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})Q$. Hence ef{lem:Q-completeness} implies \[  ra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})(1-11\zeta^{1/4}) \geq 1-12\zeta^{1/4}. \] \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[$Q$ is almost projective]  egin{equation*} \sum_a (Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta} \cdot I. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Since $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum},  egin{align*} \sum_a Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a & \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \sum_a Q_a \cdot I \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a \ & = (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})Q - Q \ & = 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,Q \ & \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I \ & \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}\,I, \end{align*} using ef{eq:assumption-on-zeta} in the last step. \end{proof}  egin{definition}[Matrix decomposition of~$Q_a$] For each $a$, let \[ m_a = \mathrm{rank}(Q_a), \] and let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,m_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $Q_a$, so that \[ Q_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{v_{a,i}} ra{v_{a,i}}. \] Let \[ m = \sum_a m_a, \] and let $\{\ket{a,i}\}$ be an orthonormal basis of $\C^m$, indexed by all $a$ and all $1 \leq i \leq m_a$. For each $a$, define \[ X_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i} ra{v_{a,i}}, \qquad T_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i} ra{a,i}, \] and define  egin{equation} X = \sum_a X_a = \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i} ra{v_{a,i}}. \end{equation} Let $T = \{T_a\}$. Then $T$ is a projective measurement on $\C^m$. \end{definition}  egin{proof} Choose an orthonormal basis of the range of each projector \(Q_a\). The rank-one expansion gives the displayed decomposition, and the orthogonality of the labelled basis vectors makes the family \(T\) a projective measurement. \end{proof}  egin{definition}[SVD of~$X$] The paper presents this step by choosing a singular value decomposition \[ X = U \cdot \Sigma_{m 	imes d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] The formalization has two closely related auxiliary declarations. The reduced datum records the downstream consequences of the choice: the matrices $X$ and $\widehat X$, the identities $X^\dagger X=Q$, $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$, and $X^\dagger\widehat X=\sqrt Q$, together with the $Q_a=X^\dagger T_aX$ restatement. The rectangular-SVD lemmas take explicit matrices $U,V,\Sigma,I_{m	imes d}$ and derive the two stored $\widehat X$ identities from the matrix calculation below. \end{definition}  egin{proof} Apply the finite-dimensional singular value decomposition to \(X\) and record exactly the consequences used later: the identities for \(X^\dagger X\), \(\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger\), \(X^\dagger\widehat X\), and the restatement of the \(Q_a\)'s. The unitary-group constructors are the same rectangular-SVD calculation, with the square factors taken as elements of the relevant unitary groups rather than as matrices accompanied by separate unitarity equations. In the sigma-range specialization, the auxiliary row space is the lifted finite-enumeration carrier associated to the ranks of the \(Q_a\)'s, which is definitionally the carrier of the canonical sigma-range \(Q\)-layer. \end{proof}  egin{remark}[Formalization support for orthogonal projector families] If the family $\{Q_a\}$ were a projective measurement, then the vectors $\ket{v_{a,i}}$, over all $a$ and all $1 \leq i \leq m_a$, would be orthonormal. Then \eqref{eq:looks-like-singular-value-decomposition} would already be a singular value decomposition of $X$, with $\Sigma = I_{m 	imes d}$. Equivalently, \[ X = U \cdot I_{m 	imes d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] This motivates replacing $\Sigma$ by $I$ in the definition of $\widehat X$ and $P$. \end{remark}  egin{definition}[Definition of~$P$] The paper defines \[ \widehat{X} = U \cdot I_{m 	imes d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] We take $\widehat X$ to be the reduced matrix supplied by the stored datum. For each $a$, define \[ \widehat{X}_a = T_a \cdot \widehat{X}, \qquad P_a = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a. \] \end{definition}  egin{proof} The definition is the formal \(Q/X/\widehat X/P\) construction: once \(\widehat X\) is chosen from the stored singular-value data, each \(P_a\) is defined as the positive operator \(\widehat X_a^\dagger\widehat X_a\). \end{proof}  egin{lemma} For each $a$, \[ X_a = T_a \cdot X. \] \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Multiply the definition of $X$ by $T_a$ on the left and use that $T_a$ selects exactly the basis vectors $\ket{a,i}$: \[ T_a \cdot X = \Big(\sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i} ra{a,i}\Big) \Big(\sum_b \sum_{j=1}^{m_b} \ket{b,j} ra{v_{b,j}}\Big) = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i} ra{v_{a,i}} = X_a. \] \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[$Q_a$ restated] For each $a$,  egin{equation*} Q_a = X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a = X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = X_a^\dagger \cdot X. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} The identity $X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$ follows by expanding the basis sums. The remaining equalities come from ef{lem:xa-t} and the projectivity of $T$: \[ X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a = (X^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot X) = X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = X_a^\dagger \cdot X. \] \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[$X$ squared]  egin{equation*} X^\dagger \cdot X = Q. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Use that $T$ is a measurement and then ef{lem:qa-restated}: \[ X^\dagger \cdot X = \sum_a X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = \sum_a Q_a = Q. \] The additional paper identities involving $U,V,\Sigma$ are the usual SVD computations. The Lean development also records the spectral calculation which will identify the mixed positive-Gram-image product with $\sqrt Q$: the positive eigenvalues give the nonzero columns, while the zero eigenspace has zero coefficient in the square-root expansion and is killed by $X$. The conjugate right-eigenvector rows over the positive spectrum are also orthonormal. Equivalently, any row-space vector orthogonal to the positive Gram images is killed by $X^\dagger$. \end{proof}  egin{lemma} For each $a$,  egin{equation*} X_a^\dagger \cdot (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m 	imes m})^2 \cdot X_a = Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Expand the square and apply ef{lem:X-squared} and ef{lem:qa-restated} term by term: \[ X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a = Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a, \] while \[ X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a = (X_a^\dagger \cdot X)(X^\dagger \cdot X_a) = Q_a \cdot Q_a = Q_a, \] and $X_a^\dagger I_{m 	imes m} X_a = X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$. Substituting these identities into \[ (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m 	imes m})^2 = X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger - 2X \cdot X^\dagger + I_{m 	imes m} \] gives the claim. \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[$P_a$ restated] For each $a$,  egin{equation*} P_a = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Since $T$ is projective, \[ P_a = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a = (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot \widehat{X}) = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}. \] \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[$\widehat{X}$ squared]  egin{equation*} \widehat{X} \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger = I_{m 	imes m}. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} The paper proves this by multiplying out $\widehat{X}=U\cdot I_{m	imes d}\cdot V^\dagger$ and using the unitarity of $U$ and $V$. In Lean, the dimension hypothesis $m\leq d$ already gives a rectangular matrix with orthonormal rows on the sigma auxiliary space; the chosen matrix 	exttt{sigmaFinXHatCoisometry} and its specification record this existence result as a hypothesis for the future construction. The formal lemma 	exttt{orthonormal\_normalized\_image\_of\_adjoint\_comp\_eigenvectors} records the singular-vector normalization calculation, while 	exttt{normalized\_matrix\_image\_rows\_mul\_conjTranspose} combines the corresponding row-coisometry identity, and 	exttt{positive\_gram\_spectrum\_image\_rows\_transpose\_mixed} records the adjoint action $X^\dagger(\lambda^{-1/2}Xv)=\lambda^{1/2}v$ on the positive spectral part of the Gram operator. The formal lemma 	exttt{exists\_unitaryGroup\_with\_positive\_gram\_spectrum\_rows} records the next finite-dimensional step: after choosing distinct row positions for the positive spectrum, these normalized image rows extend to a square unitary group element on the row space. The companion lemma 	exttt{exists\_rectangular\_coisometry\_extending\_orthonormal\_rows} records the analogous rectangular completion for prescribed right rows when the dimension bound permits it. The formal lemma 	exttt{unitaryGroup\_mul\_rectangular\_coisometry} and its right-multiplication companion 	exttt{rectangular\_coisometry\_mul\_conjTranspose\_unitaryGroup} record the two unitary-preservation steps in the paper's multiplication. The formal lemma 	exttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_coisometry\_unitaryGroup} applies these preservation steps to the rectangular-SVD expression. The unconditional positive-Gram route is 	exttt{exists\_xHat\_of\_sigmaFinRangeEmbedding\_positiveGram}, which constructs $\widehat X$ from the rank-reduction witness and proves $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$ together with the mixed square-root identity below. \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[$X$ times $\widehat{X}$]  egin{equation*} X \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger = U \cdot \Sigma_{m 	imes m} \cdot U^\dagger, \quad X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} = \sqrt{Q}. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} The paper obtains this from the SVD formula for $X$ and the definition of $\widehat X$. In Lean, the unconditional QXP data first proves that $X\widehat X^\dagger$ is Hermitian and positive. The formal lemma 	exttt{x\_mul\_xHat\_adjoint\_spectral\_theorem} then applies Mathlib's spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, giving the displayed $U\Sigma U^\dagger$ form with the Mathlib eigenvector unitary and the diagonal matrix of real eigenvalues. The auxiliary lemma 	exttt{rectangularSvd\_x\_mul\_xHat\_conjTranspose\_raw} records the same calculation under explicit rectangular-SVD data, where the middle factor \(S I_{m	imes d}^\dagger\) is the formal square matrix \(\Sigma_{m	imes m}\). The formal lemma 	exttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_mixed\_of\_sqrtQ\_unitaryGroup} records the second matrix calculation in the form whose square-root target is the operator $Q$ supplied by the QXP construction. The formal lemma 	exttt{rectangularSvd\_middle\_eq\_sqrt\_of\_square} records the spectral step: a positive middle factor whose square is $Q$ is the positive square root of $Q$. The reduced datum then records this mixed-product identity as a primitive consequence, which is exactly the part needed in ef{lem:squared-difference} and ef{lem:P-Q-approx}. \end{proof}  egin{remark}[Lean status for the QXP algebra] The Lean declarations linked in Lemmas~ef{lem:X-squared}, ef{lem:X-hat-squared}, and~ef{lem:X-times-X-hat} expose the corresponding matrix identities as construction theorems. These declarations prove the identities from the \(Q\)-layer, the sigma-range realization, and the positive-Gram spectral construction, with the rectangular-SVD calculation retained as an auxiliary comparison. Thus the local \(X/\widehat X/P\) algebra is formalized; the remaining chapter-level work is to compose this construction with the preceding orthonormalization step from the paper hypotheses. \end{remark}  egin{lemma}[Squared difference]  egin{equation*} (X - \widehat{X}) \cdot (X - \widehat{X})^\dagger \leq (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m 	imes m})^2. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} The paper diagonalizes the positive operator $X\widehat X^\dagger$ using the SVD notation. The formal proof avoids storing that SVD explicitly: set $Y=X\widehat X^\dagger$. The primitive identities imply that $Y$ is hermitian, nonnegative, and satisfies $Y^2=XX^\dagger$. Hence $(X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger=(Y-I)^2$, and positivity of $Y$ gives $(Y-I)^2\leq(Y^2-I)^2=(XX^\dagger-I)^2$. \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[Projectivity of~$P$] $P = \{P_a\}$ forms a projective sub-measurement. \end{lemma}  egin{proof} For outcomes $a,b$,  egin{align*} P_a \cdot P_b & = (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X}) (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X}) \ & = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot I_{m 	imes m} \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X} \ & = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot  one[a=b] \ & = P_a \cdot  one[a=b], \end{align*} where the second line uses ef{lem:X-hat-squared}, the third uses that $T$ is projective, and the last uses ef{lem:pa-restated}. Summing over $a$ shows $\sum_a P_a \leq I$, so $P$ is a projective sub-measurement. The formalization also records the sharper identity \[ \sum_a P_a=\widehat X^\dagger\widehat X, \] and the resulting total-domination estimates used later in the monotone-total self-improvement route. \end{proof}  egin{lemma}[$P$ is close to~$Q$]  egin{equation*} Q_a \ot I \approx_{30\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I. \end{equation*} \end{lemma}  egin{proof} The formal proof follows this argument directly from the primitive $X$, $\widehat X$, and $P$ identities; the $30\zeta^{1/4}$ estimate is derived here rather than stored as part of the reduced datum. The unitary-group rectangular-SVD lemma combines the same estimate with the positive-square identification of the middle factor from ef{lem:X-times-X-hat}; the square unitary factors are again carried as elements of the relevant unitary groups. The positive-Gram sigma-space lemma also records the coisometry \(X X^\dagger=I\) for the original sigma embedding when the projective \(Q\)-family is subnormalized; this is the construction-level hypothesis later used to obtain the QXP-internal fresh-outcome comparison \(Q_{\mathrm{none}} \leq P_{\mathrm{none}}\). An additional source-to-\(Q\) comparison is still needed for source-facing residual domination. The quantity to bound is  egin{equation} \sum_a  ra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} =  ra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} +  ra{\psi} P \ot I \ket{\psi} - \sum_a  ra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} - \sum_a  ra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi}, \end{equation} using the projectivity of $Q$ and $P$. The first term is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ by ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, and the second is at most $1$ because $P$ is a sub-measurement. For the last two terms,  egin{equation} \sum_a  ra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} + \sum_a  ra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi} = 2 \cdot \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a  ra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big). \end{equation} By ef{lem:qa-restated}, \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} = \sum_a  ra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a) \ot I \ket{\psi}. \] The main estimate is  egin{equation} \sum_a  ra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a  ra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} This follows by Cauchy--Schwarz: \[ \Big|\sum_a  ra{\psi} ((X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)) \ot I)\cdot(P_a \ot I)\ket{\psi}\Big| \] is bounded by the square root of \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi}  ig(X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger \cdot X_a ig)\ot I \ket{\psi}, \] times the square root of $\sum_a  ra{\psi}(P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1$. The first factor is at most $4\sqrt{\zeta}$ by ef{lem:squared-difference}, ef{lem:X-expression-to-Q-expression}, and ef{lem:q-almost-projective}, so the total error is at most $2\zeta^{1/4}$. The right-hand side of ef{eq:add-a-hat} is real, because \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} =  ra{\psi} (X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}) \ot I \ket{\psi} =  ra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi}, \] where the first equality uses ef{lem:xa-t}, ef{lem:pa-restated}, and ef{lem:X-hat-squared} and that $T$ is a measurement, and the second uses ef{lem:X-times-X-hat}. Hence ef{lem:sqrt-Q-completeness} and ef{eq:add-a-hat} imply \[ \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a  ra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big) \geq 1-14\zeta^{1/4}. \] Substituting this into ef{eq:complex-conjugates} and then into ef{eq:P-Q-thing-to-bound} gives \[ \sum_a  ra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) + 1 - 2(1-14\zeta^{1/4}) = 2\sqrt{\zeta} + 28\zeta^{1/4} \leq 30\zeta^{1/4}. \] \end{proof} Finally, ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum} gives \[ A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I, \] and ef{lem:P-Q-approx} gives \[ Q_a \ot I \approx_{30\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I. \] The triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ yields \[ A_a \ot I \approx_{84\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I. \]

nodes.statement_short: Reduce to almost-projectivity, round eigenvalues to projectors, cut rank to $d$, then orthonormalize via an SVD-based $Q/X/\widehat X/P$ construction. The key step bounds $P$ against $Q$ using $\widehat X$ replacing $X$.

nodes.statement: If $x \geq 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$. Since $\delta \leq 1/2$ below, one also has $x \geq \delta$, so \[ (x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2 = (1-x)^2 \leq (1-x)\frac{x}{\delta} = \frac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2). \] If $x < 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=0$, and similarly \[ (x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2 = x^2 \leq x\frac{1-x}{\delta} = \frac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2). \]

nodes.statement: There exists a set of projective matrices $\{R_a\}$ such that \begin{equation*} A_a \ot I \approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta}} R_a \ot I. \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} R:= \sum_a R_a \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \cdot I. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: Rounding to projectors
nodes.statement_short: Round each $A_a$'s eigenvalues to $\{0,1\}$: projectors $R_a$ $2\sqrt\zeta$-close with total $\le(1+2\sqrt\zeta)I$.
nodes.label: lem:projective-non-measurement

nodes.statement: Write the eigendecomposition of $A_a$ as \[ A_a = \sum_i \lambda_{a,i}\ket{u_{a,i}}\bra{u_{a,i}}. \] Choose \begin{equation} 0 < \delta \leq 1/2, \end{equation} define $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta:[0,1] \to \{0,1\}$ by $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$ when $x \geq 1-\delta$ and $0$ otherwise, and set \[ R_a = \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(A_a) = \sum_i \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(\lambda_{a,i}) \ket{u_{a,i}}\bra{u_{a,i}}. \] By \ref{lem:trunc-inequality}, \[ (A_a-R_a)^2 \leq \frac{1}{\delta}(A_a-(A_a)^2). \] Summing expectations and using \ref{eq:A-looks-projective} gives \[ \sum_a \Vert (A_a-R_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 \leq \frac{2\zeta}{\delta}, \] so $A_a \ot I \approx_{2\zeta/\delta} R_a \ot I$. For every $x \in [0,1]$, one has $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x) \leq x/(1-\delta)$, hence \[ R_a \leq \frac{1}{1-\delta} A_a. \] Summing over $a$ and using that $A$ is a measurement, \[ R = \sum_a R_a \leq \frac{1}{1-\delta} I \leq (1+2\delta)I, \] where the last estimate uses $\delta \leq 1/2$. Setting $\delta=\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives the claim, and \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta} ensures $\delta \leq 1/2$.
nodes.name: Truncate eigenvalues at $1-\delta$, bound the error via the truncation inequalit
nodes.statement_short: Truncate eigenvalues at $1-\delta$, bound the error via the truncation inequality, bound $R$ by $A/(1-\delta)$, set $\delta=\sqrt\zeta$.

nodes.statement: 0 < \delta \leq 1/2,
nodes.name: Bound on delta
nodes.label: eq:bound-on-delta

nodes.statement: The source-facing Lean declarations for Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-non-measurement} are the proposition \texttt{projectiveNonMeasurement} and the construction theorem \texttt{projectiveNonMeasurement\_of\_sourceAlmostProjective\_full}. The declarations listed here are the endpoint and regime splits, the \texttt{AlmostProjMeasStatement} witness forms, and the spectral-truncation statement conversions used by later Section~5 arguments. They are not additional hypotheses in the paper statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-non-measurement}.
nodes.name: Lean auxiliary declarations for rounding to projectors
nodes.label: rem:lean-projective-non-measurement-auxiliary

nodes.statement: Let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function on a finite index set $\alpha$ with $|\alpha| = r$, and let $L \subseteq \alpha$ with $|L| = d$ and $d < r$. Write $S = L^\complement$ and assume $f(s) \leq f(l)$ for every $s \in S$ and $l \in L$. Then the pairwise double-counting inequality \[ |L|\, \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\, \sum_{l \in L} f(l) \] holds, and hence also \[ r\, \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\, \sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x). \] If in addition $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})\,d$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1 + 2\sqrt{\zeta}$, and $0 \leq \zeta \leq 1/4$, then \[ \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}. \]
nodes.name: Combinatorial averaging for the $r > d$ branch
nodes.statement_short: If the $d$ largest of $r$ values dominate the rest, the small values sum to at most $4\sqrt\zeta$ when $r\le(1+2\sqrt\zeta)d$.

assumptions: Let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function on a finite index set $\alpha$ with $|\alpha| = r$, and let $L \subseteq \alpha$ with $|L| = d$ and $d < r$.
conclusions: Then the pairwise double-counting inequality

assumptions: $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})\,d$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1 + 2\sqrt{\zeta}$, and $0 \leq \zeta \leq 1/4$
conclusions: \[ \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}. \]

assumptions: Let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function on a finite index set $\alpha$ with $|\alpha| = r$, and let $L \subseteq \alpha$ with $|L| = d$ and $d < r$.
Write $S = L^\complement$ and assume $f(s) \leq f(l)$ for every $s \in S$ and $l \in L$.
$r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})\,d$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1 + 2\sqrt{\zeta}$, and $0 \leq \zeta \leq 1/4$
conclusions: Then the pairwise double-counting inequality
If in addition $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})\,d$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1 + 2\sqrt{\zeta}$, and $0 \leq \zeta \leq 1/4$, then
\[ \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}. \]
nodes.label: lem:small-overlap-averaging

nodes.statement: Choose $L$ to be a set of $d$ indices on which the sum of $f$ is maximal. If some $s \in S$ and $l \in L$ satisfied $f(l) < f(s)$, replacing $l$ by $s$ would increase this sum, so every small index is bounded by every large index. Summing the inequalities $f(s) \leq f(l)$ over all pairs $(s,l) \in S \times L$ gives \[ |L|\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{l \in L} f(l). \] Since $\alpha$ is the disjoint union of $L$ and $S$, adding $|S|\sum_{s \in S} f(s)$ to both sides yields \[ r\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x). \] The hypotheses $|L|=d$ and $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d$ imply $|S|/r \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Dividing by $r$ and using $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives \[ \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}). \] Finally, $\zeta \leq 1/4$ implies $\sqrt{\zeta} \leq 1/2$, and hence $2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}$.
nodes.name: Exchange argument, double counting over $S\times L$, then divide by $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Exchange argument, double counting over $S\times L$, then divide by $r$.

nodes.statement: There exists a set of projection matrices $\{Q_a\}$ such that \begin{equation*} A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I. \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} Q:= \sum_a Q_a \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \cdot I. \end{equation*} Furthermore, \begin{equation*} \sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a) \leq d. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: Rank reduction
nodes.statement_short: Projectors $Q_a$ of total rank $\le d$, $12\sqrt\zeta$-close to $A_a$, with $\sum Q_a\le(1+2\sqrt\zeta)I$.
nodes.label: lem:projective-low-rank-sum

nodes.statement: Let $\{R_a\}$ be given by \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement}. Write $r_a=\mathrm{rank}(R_a)$ and $r=\sum_a r_a$. If $r \leq d$, take $Q_a=R_a$. Otherwise, \begin{equation} r = \sum_a r_a = \sum_a \Tr(R_a) = \Tr(R) \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d. \end{equation} Let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,r_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $R_a$, so \[ R_a = \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}. \] Define the overlaps \[ o_{a,i} = \bra{\psi} (\ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}} \ot I)\ket{\psi}. \] Their total satisfies \begin{equation} \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} o_{a,i} = \bra{\psi} R \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}. \end{equation} Let $\mathsf{Large}$ be the set of the $d$ largest overlaps $o_{a,i}$, breaking ties arbitrarily, and let $\mathsf{Small}$ be the complement. Then \begin{equation} |\mathsf{Small}| = r-d \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,d \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,r, \end{equation} by \ref{eq:bound-on-r}. Averaging the overlaps over the $r$ indices gives \begin{equation} \sum_{(a,i)\in \mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i} \leq \frac{|\mathsf{Small}|}{r}\sum_{a,i} o_{a,i} \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}, \end{equation} using \ref{eq:size-of-small-is-small}, \ref{eq:total-overlap}, and \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta}. For each $a$, let $\mathsf{Large}_a=\{i : (a,i)\in \mathsf{Large}\}$ and define \[ Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Large}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}. \] Then $\sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a)=|\mathsf{Large}| \leq d$, and $Q_a \leq R_a$ for every $a$, so \[ Q = \sum_a Q_a \leq \sum_a R_a = R \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I. \] Also, \[ R_a-Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Small}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}} \] is a projector, hence \[ \sum_a \Vert (R_a-Q_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 = \sum_{(a,i)\in\mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i} \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta} \] by \ref{eq:small-overlaps}. Therefore $R_a \ot I \approx_{4\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I$. Combining this with \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement} and the triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ gives \[ A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I. \]
nodes.name: Keep the $d$ largest-overlap rank-one pieces of the rounded projectors; the disc
nodes.statement_short: Keep the $d$ largest-overlap rank-one pieces of the rounded projectors; the discarded small overlaps total $4\sqrt\zeta$.

nodes.statement: r = \sum_a r_a = \sum_a \Tr(R_a) = \Tr(R) \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d.
nodes.name: Bound on r
nodes.label: eq:bound-on-r

nodes.statement: \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} o_{a,i} = \bra{\psi} R \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}.
nodes.name: Total overlap
nodes.label: eq:total-overlap

nodes.statement: |\mathsf{Small}| = r-d \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,d \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,r,
nodes.name: Size of small is small
nodes.label: eq:size-of-small-is-small

nodes.statement: \sum_{(a,i)\in \mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i} \leq \frac{|\mathsf{Small}|}{r}\sum_{a,i} o_{a,i} \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta},
nodes.name: Small overlaps
nodes.label: eq:small-overlaps

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq 1 - 11 \zeta^{1/4}. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: Completeness of~$Q$
nodes.label: lem:Q-completeness

nodes.statement: Since each $Q_a$ is projective, \begin{equation} \bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} = \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{5\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} By Cauchy--Schwarz, \[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta} \quad\text{and}\quad \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 12\sqrt{\zeta} \] from \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}. A second Cauchy--Schwarz estimate yields \begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{4\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Combining \ref{eq:Q-for-an-A} and \ref{eq:another-Q-for-A} with \ref{eq:A-looks-projective} gives \[ \bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \ot I \ket{\psi} - 2\zeta - 9\zeta^{1/4} = 1 - 11\zeta^{1/4}, \] since $\zeta \leq \zeta^{1/4}$ under \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta}.
nodes.name: Two Cauchy--Schwarz estimates replace $Q_a^2$ by $Q_aA_a$ and then $A_a^2$, comb
nodes.statement_short: Two Cauchy--Schwarz estimates replace $Q_a^2$ by $Q_aA_a$ and then $A_a^2$, combined with almost-projectivity.

nodes.statement: \bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} = \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{5\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Q for an A
nodes.label: eq:Q-for-an-A

nodes.statement: \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{4\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Another Q for A
nodes.label: eq:another-Q-for-A

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq 1 - 12 \zeta^{1/4}. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: Completeness of~$\sqrt{Q}$
nodes.label: lem:sqrt-Q-completeness

nodes.statement:
Diagonalize $Q=\sum_i 
u_i \ket{u_i} ra{u_i}$. Because $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, each $
u_i$ is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Therefore \[ \sqrt{Q} = \sum_i \sqrt{
u_i}\ket{u_i} ra{u_i} \geq  rac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} Q. \] The scalar estimate \[  rac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} \geq 1-\sqrt{\zeta} \] gives $\sqrt{Q} \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})Q$. Hence ef{lem:Q-completeness} implies \[  ra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})(1-11\zeta^{1/4}) \geq 1-12\zeta^{1/4}. \]
nodes.name: Eigenvalues of $Q$ at most $1+2\sqrt\zeta$ give $\sqrt Q\ge(1-\sqrt\zeta)Q$; app
nodes.statement_short: Eigenvalues of $Q$ at most $1+2\sqrt\zeta$ give $\sqrt Q\ge(1-\sqrt\zeta)Q$; apply completeness of $Q$.

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \sum_a (Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta} \cdot I. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $Q$ is almost projective
nodes.label: lem:q-almost-projective

nodes.statement: Since $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, \begin{align*} \sum_a Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a & \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \sum_a Q_a \cdot I \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a \\ & = (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})Q - Q \\ & = 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,Q \\ & \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I \\ & \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}\,I, \end{align*} using \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta} in the last step.
nodes.name: Bound $\sum Q_aQQ_a$ using $Q\le(1+2\sqrt\zeta)I$.

nodes.statement: For each $a$, let \[ m_a = \mathrm{rank}(Q_a), \] and let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,m_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $Q_a$, so that \[ Q_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}. \] Let \[ m = \sum_a m_a, \] and let $\{\ket{a,i}\}$ be an orthonormal basis of $\C^m$, indexed by all $a$ and all $1 \leq i \leq m_a$. For each $a$, define \[ X_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{v_{a,i}}, \qquad T_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{a,i}, \] and define \begin{equation} X = \sum_a X_a = \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{v_{a,i}}. \end{equation} Let $T = \{T_a\}$. Then $T$ is a projective measurement on $\C^m$.
nodes.name: Matrix decomposition of~$Q_a$
nodes.statement_short: Encode each $Q_a$ by an orthonormal basis of its range into matrices $X_a$, $T_a$, $X=\sum X_a$.
nodes.label: def:matrix-decomposition-Q

nodes.statement: X = \sum_a X_a = \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
nodes.name: Looks like singular value decomposition
nodes.label: eq:looks-like-singular-value-decomposition

nodes.statement: Then $T$ is a projective measurement on $\C^m$.
nodes.name: $T$ is a projective measurement

nodes.statement: Choose an orthonormal basis of the range of each projector \(Q_a\). The rank-one expansion gives the displayed decomposition, and the orthogonality of the labelled basis vectors makes the family \(T\) a projective measurement.
nodes.name: Rank-one expansion and orthogonality of the labelled basis.
nodes.statement_short: Rank-one expansion and orthogonality of the labelled basis.

nodes.statement: The paper presents this step by choosing a singular value decomposition \[ X = U \cdot \Sigma_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] The formalization has two closely related auxiliary declarations. The reduced datum records the downstream consequences of the choice: the matrices $X$ and $\widehat X$, the identities $X^\dagger X=Q$, $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$, and $X^\dagger\widehat X=\sqrt Q$, together with the $Q_a=X^\dagger T_aX$ restatement. The rectangular-SVD lemmas take explicit matrices $U,V,\Sigma,I_{m\times d}$ and derive the two stored $\widehat X$ identities from the matrix calculation below.
nodes.name: SVD of~$X$
nodes.statement_short: An SVD $X=U\Sigma V^\dagger$ is chosen, recording $X^\dagger X=Q$, $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$, $X^\dagger\widehat X=\sqrt Q$.
nodes.label: def:svd-of-X

nodes.statement: Apply the finite-dimensional singular value decomposition to \(X\) and record exactly the consequences used later: the identities for \(X^\dagger X\), \(\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger\), \(X^\dagger\widehat X\), and the restatement of the \(Q_a\)'s. The unitary-group constructors are the same rectangular-SVD calculation, with the square factors taken as elements of the relevant unitary groups rather than as matrices accompanied by separate unitarity equations. In the sigma-range specialization, the auxiliary row space is the lifted finite-enumeration carrier associated to the ranks of the \(Q_a\)'s, which is definitionally the carrier of the canonical sigma-range \(Q\)-layer.
nodes.name: Apply the finite-dimensional SVD and record the consequences used later.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the finite-dimensional SVD and record the consequences used later.

nodes.statement: If the family $\{Q_a\}$ were a projective measurement, then the vectors $\ket{v_{a,i}}$, over all $a$ and all $1 \leq i \leq m_a$, would be orthonormal. Then \eqref{eq:looks-like-singular-value-decomposition} would already be a singular value decomposition of $X$, with $\Sigma = I_{m \times d}$. Equivalently, \[ X = U \cdot I_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] This motivates replacing $\Sigma$ by $I$ in the definition of $\widehat X$ and $P$.
nodes.name: Formalization support for orthogonal projector families
nodes.statement_short: If $Q$ were projective, $X$'s decomposition would be an SVD with $\Sigma=I$, motivating $\widehat X$.
nodes.label: rem:motivation-for-P

nodes.statement: The paper defines \[ \widehat{X} = U \cdot I_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] We take $\widehat X$ to be the reduced matrix supplied by the stored datum. For each $a$, define \[ \widehat{X}_a = T_a \cdot \widehat{X}, \qquad P_a = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a. \]
nodes.name: Definition of~$P$
nodes.label: def:projective-P

nodes.statement: The definition is the formal \(Q/X/\widehat X/P\) construction: once \(\widehat X\) is chosen from the stored singular-value data, each \(P_a\) is defined as the positive operator \(\widehat X_a^\dagger\widehat X_a\).
nodes.name: Explains that $P_a=\widehat X_a^\dagger\widehat X_a$ is the formal construction.
nodes.statement_short: Explains that $P_a=\widehat X_a^\dagger\widehat X_a$ is the formal construction.

nodes.statement: For each $a$, \[ X_a = T_a \cdot X. \]
nodes.name: $X_a = T_a X$
nodes.label: lem:xa-t

nodes.statement: Multiply the definition of $X$ by $T_a$ on the left and use that $T_a$ selects exactly the basis vectors $\ket{a,i}$: \[ T_a \cdot X = \Big(\sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{a,i}\Big) \Big(\sum_b \sum_{j=1}^{m_b} \ket{b,j}\bra{v_{b,j}}\Big) = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{v_{a,i}} = X_a. \]
nodes.name: $T_a$ selects the basis vectors $|a,i\rangle$.

nodes.statement: For each $a$, \begin{equation*} Q_a = X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a = X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = X_a^\dagger \cdot X. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $Q_a$ restated
nodes.label: lem:qa-restated

nodes.statement: The identity $X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$ follows by expanding the basis sums. The remaining equalities come from \ref{lem:xa-t} and the projectivity of $T$: \[ X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a = (X^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot X) = X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = X_a^\dagger \cdot X. \]
nodes.name: Expand basis sums, then use $X_a=T_aX$ and projectivity of $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand basis sums, then use $X_a=T_aX$ and projectivity of $T$.

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} X^\dagger \cdot X = Q. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $X$ squared
nodes.label: lem:X-squared

nodes.statement: Use that $T$ is a measurement and then \ref{lem:qa-restated}: \[ X^\dagger \cdot X = \sum_a X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = \sum_a Q_a = Q. \] The additional paper identities involving $U,V,\Sigma$ are the usual SVD computations. The Lean development also records the spectral calculation which will identify the mixed positive-Gram-image product with $\sqrt Q$: the positive eigenvalues give the nonzero columns, while the zero eigenspace has zero coefficient in the square-root expansion and is killed by $X$. The conjugate right-eigenvector rows over the positive spectrum are also orthonormal. Equivalently, any row-space vector orthogonal to the positive Gram images is killed by $X^\dagger$.
nodes.name: Sum $X^\dagger T_aX=Q_a$ over $a$ using that $T$ is a measurement; Lean records
nodes.statement_short: Sum $X^\dagger T_aX=Q_a$ over $a$ using that $T$ is a measurement; Lean records extra spectral facts.

nodes.statement: For each $a$, \begin{equation*} X_a^\dagger \cdot (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2 \cdot X_a = Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $X$-expression to $Q$-expression
nodes.label: lem:X-expression-to-Q-expression

nodes.statement: Expand the square and apply \ref{lem:X-squared} and \ref{lem:qa-restated} term by term: \[ X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a = Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a, \] while \[ X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a = (X_a^\dagger \cdot X)(X^\dagger \cdot X_a) = Q_a \cdot Q_a = Q_a, \] and $X_a^\dagger I_{m \times m} X_a = X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$. Substituting these identities into \[ (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2 = X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger - 2X \cdot X^\dagger + I_{m \times m} \] gives the claim.
nodes.name: Expand the square and substitute term-by-term identities.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the square and substitute term-by-term identities.

nodes.statement: For each $a$, \begin{equation*} P_a = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $P_a$ restated
nodes.label: lem:pa-restated

nodes.statement: Since $T$ is projective, \[ P_a = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a = (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot \widehat{X}) = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}. \]
nodes.name: Projectivity of $T$.

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \widehat{X} \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger = I_{m \times m}. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $\widehat{X}$ squared
nodes.label: lem:X-hat-squared

nodes.statement: The paper proves this by multiplying out $\widehat{X}=U\cdot I_{m\times d}\cdot V^\dagger$ and using the unitarity of $U$ and $V$. In Lean, the dimension hypothesis $m\leq d$ already gives a rectangular matrix with orthonormal rows on the sigma auxiliary space; the chosen matrix \texttt{sigmaFinXHatCoisometry} and its specification record this existence result as a hypothesis for the future construction. The formal lemma \texttt{orthonormal\_normalized\_image\_of\_adjoint\_comp\_eigenvectors} records the singular-vector normalization calculation, while \texttt{normalized\_matrix\_image\_rows\_mul\_conjTranspose} combines the corresponding row-coisometry identity, and \texttt{positive\_gram\_spectrum\_image\_rows\_transpose\_mixed} records the adjoint action $X^\dagger(\lambda^{-1/2}Xv)=\lambda^{1/2}v$ on the positive spectral part of the Gram operator. The formal lemma \texttt{exists\_unitaryGroup\_with\_positive\_gram\_spectrum\_rows} records the next finite-dimensional step: after choosing distinct row positions for the positive spectrum, these normalized image rows extend to a square unitary group element on the row space. The companion lemma \texttt{exists\_rectangular\_coisometry\_extending\_orthonormal\_rows} records the analogous rectangular completion for prescribed right rows when the dimension bound permits it. The formal lemma \texttt{unitaryGroup\_mul\_rectangular\_coisometry} and its right-multiplication companion \texttt{rectangular\_coisometry\_mul\_conjTranspose\_unitaryGroup} record the two unitary-preservation steps in the paper's multiplication. The formal lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_coisometry\_unitaryGroup} applies these preservation steps to the rectangular-SVD expression. The unconditional positive-Gram route is \texttt{exists\_xHat\_of\_sigmaFinRangeEmbedding\_positiveGram}, which constructs $\widehat X$ from the rank-reduction witness and proves $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$ together with the mixed square-root identity below.
nodes.name: Paper: unitarity of $U,V$. Lean: build $\widehat X$ from orthonormal rows of the
nodes.statement_short: Paper: unitarity of $U,V$. Lean: build $\widehat X$ from orthonormal rows of the positive Gram spectrum extended to a unitary.

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} X \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger = U \cdot \Sigma_{m \times m} \cdot U^\dagger, \quad X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} = \sqrt{Q}. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $X$ times $\widehat{X}$
nodes.label: lem:X-times-X-hat

nodes.statement: The paper obtains this from the SVD formula for $X$ and the definition of $\widehat X$. In Lean, the unconditional QXP data first proves that $X\widehat X^\dagger$ is Hermitian and positive. The formal lemma \texttt{x\_mul\_xHat\_adjoint\_spectral\_theorem} then applies Mathlib's spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, giving the displayed $U\Sigma U^\dagger$ form with the Mathlib eigenvector unitary and the diagonal matrix of real eigenvalues. The auxiliary lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_x\_mul\_xHat\_conjTranspose\_raw} records the same calculation under explicit rectangular-SVD data, where the middle factor \(S I_{m\times d}^\dagger\) is the formal square matrix \(\Sigma_{m\times m}\). The formal lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_mixed\_of\_sqrtQ\_unitaryGroup} records the second matrix calculation in the form whose square-root target is the operator $Q$ supplied by the QXP construction. The formal lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_middle\_eq\_sqrt\_of\_square} records the spectral step: a positive middle factor whose square is $Q$ is the positive square root of $Q$. The reduced datum then records this mixed-product identity as a primitive consequence, which is exactly the part needed in \ref{lem:squared-difference} and \ref{lem:P-Q-approx}.
nodes.name: Paper: SVD formula. Lean: spectral theorem for the Hermitian positive $X\widehat
nodes.statement_short: Paper: SVD formula. Lean: spectral theorem for the Hermitian positive $X\widehat X^\dagger$ and positive square-root identification.

nodes.statement: The Lean declarations linked in Lemmas~\ref{lem:X-squared}, \ref{lem:X-hat-squared}, and~\ref{lem:X-times-X-hat} expose the corresponding matrix identities as construction theorems. These declarations prove the identities from the \(Q\)-layer, the sigma-range realization, and the positive-Gram spectral construction, with the rectangular-SVD calculation retained as an auxiliary comparison. Thus the local \(X/\widehat X/P\) algebra is formalized; the remaining chapter-level work is to compose this construction with the preceding orthonormalization step from the paper hypotheses.
nodes.name: Lean status for the QXP algebra
nodes.label: rem:qxp-layer-lean-status

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} (X - \widehat{X}) \cdot (X - \widehat{X})^\dagger \leq (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: Squared difference
nodes.label: lem:squared-difference

nodes.statement: The paper diagonalizes the positive operator $X\widehat X^\dagger$ using the SVD notation. The formal proof avoids storing that SVD explicitly: set $Y=X\widehat X^\dagger$. The primitive identities imply that $Y$ is hermitian, nonnegative, and satisfies $Y^2=XX^\dagger$. Hence $(X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger=(Y-I)^2$, and positivity of $Y$ gives $(Y-I)^2\leq(Y^2-I)^2=(XX^\dagger-I)^2$.
nodes.name: With $Y=X\widehat X^\dagger\ge0$ and $Y^2=XX^\dagger$, $(Y-I)^2\le(Y^2-I)^2$.

nodes.statement: $P = \{P_a\}$ forms a projective sub-measurement.
nodes.name: Projectivity of~$P$
nodes.label: lem:P-projectivity

nodes.statement: For outcomes $a,b$, \begin{align*} P_a \cdot P_b & = (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X}) (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X}) \\ & = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot I_{m \times m} \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X} \\ & = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot \bone[a=b] \\ & = P_a \cdot \bone[a=b], \end{align*} where the second line uses \ref{lem:X-hat-squared}, the third uses that $T$ is projective, and the last uses \ref{lem:pa-restated}. Summing over $a$ shows $\sum_a P_a \leq I$, so $P$ is a projective sub-measurement. The formalization also records the sharper identity \[ \sum_a P_a=\widehat X^\dagger\widehat X, \] and the resulting total-domination estimates used later in the monotone-total self-improvement route.
nodes.name: Compute $P_aP_b$ using $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$ and projectivity of $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $P_aP_b$ using $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$ and projectivity of $T$.

nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} Q_a \ot I \approx_{30\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I. \end{equation*}
nodes.name: $P$ is close to~$Q$
nodes.label: lem:P-Q-approx

nodes.statement: The formal proof follows this argument directly from the primitive $X$, $\widehat X$, and $P$ identities; the $30\zeta^{1/4}$ estimate is derived here rather than stored as part of the reduced datum. The unitary-group rectangular-SVD lemma combines the same estimate with the positive-square identification of the middle factor from \ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}; the square unitary factors are again carried as elements of the relevant unitary groups. The positive-Gram sigma-space lemma also records the coisometry \(X X^\dagger=I\) for the original sigma embedding when the projective \(Q\)-family is subnormalized; this is the construction-level hypothesis later used to obtain the QXP-internal fresh-outcome comparison \(Q_{\mathrm{none}} \leq P_{\mathrm{none}}\). An additional source-to-\(Q\) comparison is still needed for source-facing residual domination. The quantity to bound is \begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} = \bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} + \bra{\psi} P \ot I \ket{\psi} - \sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} - \sum_a \bra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi}, \end{equation} using the projectivity of $Q$ and $P$. The first term is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, and the second is at most $1$ because $P$ is a sub-measurement. For the last two terms, \begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} + \sum_a \bra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi} = 2 \cdot \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big). \end{equation} By \ref{lem:qa-restated}, \[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} = \sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a) \ot I \ket{\psi}. \] The main estimate is \begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} This follows by Cauchy--Schwarz: \[ \Big|\sum_a \bra{\psi} ((X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)) \ot I)\cdot(P_a \ot I)\ket{\psi}\Big| \] is bounded by the square root of \[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} \big(X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger \cdot X_a\big)\ot I \ket{\psi}, \] times the square root of $\sum_a \bra{\psi}(P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1$. The first factor is at most $4\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:squared-difference}, \ref{lem:X-expression-to-Q-expression}, and \ref{lem:q-almost-projective}, so the total error is at most $2\zeta^{1/4}$. The right-hand side of \ref{eq:add-a-hat} is real, because \[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} = \bra{\psi} (X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}) \ot I \ket{\psi} = \bra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi}, \] where the first equality uses \ref{lem:xa-t}, \ref{lem:pa-restated}, and \ref{lem:X-hat-squared} and that $T$ is a measurement, and the second uses \ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}. Hence \ref{lem:sqrt-Q-completeness} and \ref{eq:add-a-hat} imply \[ \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big) \geq 1-14\zeta^{1/4}. \] Substituting this into \ref{eq:complex-conjugates} and then into \ref{eq:P-Q-thing-to-bound} gives \[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) + 1 - 2(1-14\zeta^{1/4}) = 2\sqrt{\zeta} + 28\zeta^{1/4} \leq 30\zeta^{1/4}. \]
nodes.name: Expand $\sum(Q_a-P_a)^2$; the cross term is close (Cauchy--Schwarz) to $\langle\
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\sum(Q_a-P_a)^2$; the cross term is close (Cauchy--Schwarz) to $\langle\sqrt Q\rangle$, bounded by completeness of $\sqrt Q$.

nodes.statement: \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} = \bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi} + \bra{\psi} P \ot I \ket{\psi} - \sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} - \sum_a \bra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi},
nodes.name: P Q thing to bound
nodes.label: eq:P-Q-thing-to-bound

nodes.statement: \sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi} + \sum_a \bra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi} = 2 \cdot \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big).
nodes.name: Complex conjugates
nodes.label: eq:complex-conjugates

nodes.statement: \sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Add a hat
nodes.label: eq:add-a-hat

nodes.statement: For $u \in \F_q^m$, an index $i \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, and $x \in \F_q$, let \[ \operatorname{rerand}_i(u,x) = u + x e_i. \] This is the move obtained by rerandomizing the $i$-th coordinate of $u$ by a uniform additive shift. In Lean, the same edge distribution is represented as the push-forward of the uniform distribution on triples $(u,i,x)$ by the map that replaces the $i$-th coordinate by $x$; since $x$ is uniform, this is the same distribution as the additive-shift presentation. The corresponding weight-sum identity identifies this push-forward distribution with the explicit edge coefficient used in the matrix proof.
nodes.name: Rerandomizing one coordinate
nodes.label: def:rerandomize-coord

nodes.statement: The hypercube graph $C=(V,E)$ has vertex set $V=\F_q^m$, and an edge between $u$ and $v$ whenever they differ in at most one coordinate. A random edge $(u,v) \sim C$ is sampled by drawing $u \sim \F_q^m$, $i \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, and $x \in \F_q$ uniformly and then setting $v=\operatorname{rerand}_i(u,x)$.
nodes.name: Hypercube graph
differentia: an edge between $u$ and $v$ whenever they differ in at most one coordinate
nodes.label: def:hypercube-graph

nodes.statement: Let $M=q^m$. The normalized adjacency matrix of $C$ is \[ K = \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \ket{u}\bra{v}, \] and the Laplacian is \[ L = \frac{1}{M}I-K. \]
nodes.name: Adjacency matrix and Laplacian
nodes.label: def:adjacency-laplacian

nodes.statement: The Laplacian can be written as \[ L = \frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} (\ket{u}-\ket{v})(\bra{u}-\bra{v}). \]
nodes.name: Laplacian rewrite
nodes.statement_short: $L$ is half the average of $(|u\rangle-|v\rangle)(\langle u|-\langle v|)$ over random edges.
nodes.label: prop:laplacian-rewrite

nodes.statement: The two vertex marginals of a random edge are uniform on $\F_q^m$. Expanding the right-hand side yields $(1/M)I-K$.
nodes.name: Uniform edge marginals; expand.

nodes.statement: For $\beta \in \F_q$, \[ \E_{x \sim \F_q} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(\beta x)} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } \beta=0, \\ 0 & \text{if } \beta\ne 0. \end{cases} \]
nodes.name: Average of a nontrivial additive character
assumptions: For $\beta \in \F_q$,
nodes.label: lem:character-average-scalar

nodes.statement: If $\beta=0$ the character is constant. If $\beta\ne 0$, the map $x \mapsto \beta x$ permutes $\F_q$, so the average is the average of a nontrivial additive character, which vanishes.
nodes.name: Trivial for $\beta=0$; otherwise $x\mapsto\beta x$ permutes $\F_q$ and a nontriv
nodes.statement_short: Trivial for $\beta=0$; otherwise $x\mapsto\beta x$ permutes $\F_q$ and a nontrivial character averages to zero.

nodes.statement: For $\alpha,\beta \in \F_q^m$, \[ \frac{1}{q^m}\sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot(\beta-\alpha))} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } \alpha=\beta, \\ 0 & \text{if } \alpha\ne \beta. \end{cases} \]
nodes.name: Orthogonality of finite-field characters
assumptions: For $\alpha,\beta \in \F_q^m$,
nodes.label: lem:character-average-vector

nodes.statement: This is Lemma~\ref{prop:fourier-fact-vector} applied to $v=\beta-\alpha$.
nodes.name: Apply the vector Fourier fact with $v=\beta-\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the vector Fourier fact with $v=\beta-\alpha$.

nodes.statement: For each $\alpha \in \F_q^m$, define \[ \ket{\varphi_\alpha} = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}. \] Then the following two statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$'s form an orthonormal basis of $\C^V$. \item For each $\alpha \in \F_q^m$, $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ is an eigenvector for $K$ with eigenvalue $\frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-|\alpha|}{m}$, where $|\alpha|$ is the number of nonzero coordinates of $\alpha$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.name: Eigenvectors of the hypercube graph
nodes.statement_short: Fourier characters $|\varphi_\alpha\rangle$ form an orthonormal eigenbasis of $K$ with eigenvalue $\frac{m-|\alpha|}{mM}$.
assumptions: For each $\alpha \in \F_q^m$, define
conclusions: The $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$'s form an orthonormal basis of $\C^V$.

For each $\alpha \in \F_q^m$, $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ is an eigenvector for $K$ with eigenvalue $\frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-|\alpha|}{m}$, where $|\alpha|$ is the number of nonzero coordinates of $\alpha$.
nodes.label: prop:eigenvectors

nodes.statement: First we prove \ref{item:orthonormal}. For $\alpha,\beta \in \F_q^m$, \[ \braket{\varphi_\alpha}{\varphi_\beta} = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot(\beta-\alpha))} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } \alpha=\beta, \\ 0 & \text{if } \alpha\ne \beta, \end{cases} \] by Lemma~\ref{lem:character-average-vector}. Thus the $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ form an orthonormal basis of $\C^V$. Next we prove \ref{item:eigenvector}. For $\alpha \in \F_q^m$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} K \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha} & = \left(\E_{(u,v)\sim C} \ket{u}\bra{v}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}\right) \\ & = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(v\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} By the edge-sampling rule from Definition~\ref{def:hypercube-graph}, we may write $v=u+x e_i$, where $i$ is uniformly random in $\{1,\dots,m\}$ and $x$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$. Therefore \[ \eqref{eq:eigenvector-calculation} = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \E_{u,i,x} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}((u+x e_i)\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u} = \left(\E_{i,x}\omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \E_u \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u} = \frac{1}{M}\left(\E_{i,x}\omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right) \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha}. \] Hence $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ is an eigenvector of $K$ with eigenvalue \[ \frac{1}{M} \cdot \E_i \left[\E_x \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \E_i \left[\bone[\alpha_i=0]\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-|\alpha|}{m}, \] by Lemma~\ref{lem:character-average-scalar}.
nodes.name: Orthonormality via character orthogonality; eigenvalue by averaging the characte
nodes.statement_short: Orthonormality via character orthogonality; eigenvalue by averaging the character over the rerandomized coordinate.

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} K \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha} & = \left(\E_{(u,v)\sim C} \ket{u}\bra{v}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}\right) \\ & = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(v\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}. \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Eigenvector calculation
nodes.label: eq:eigenvector-calculation

nodes.statement: If $\lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \le \lambda_{q^m}$ are the eigenvalues of $L$, then \[ \lambda_1=0, \qquad \lambda_2 = \frac{1}{m q^m}. \]
nodes.name: Spectral gap of the Laplacian
assumptions: $\lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \le \lambda_{q^m}$ are the eigenvalues of $L$
nodes.label: cor:laplacian-spectral-gap

nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{prop:eigenvectors} identifies the two largest eigenvalues of $K$, hence the two smallest eigenvalues of $L=(1/q^m)I-K$.
nodes.name: Read off the two largest eigenvalues of $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Read off the two largest eigenvalues of $K$.

nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal H_{\mathrm A} \ot \mathcal H_{\mathrm B}$ and let $0 \le A^u \le I$ be an operator for each $u \in \F_q^m$. The local variance is \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi) = \frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A^v)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}, \] and the global variance is \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi) = \frac12 \E_{u,v\sim \F_q^m} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A^v)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}. \]
nodes.name: Local and global variance
nodes.label: def:local-and-variance

nodes.statement: Define \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \ket{u} \ot A^u \ot I. \] Then \[ \Tr(A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}}) = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.name: Local variance as a Laplacian form
nodes.statement_short: Local variance equals the Laplacian quadratic form of $A_{\mathrm{comb}}$.
nodes.label: lem:local-rewrite

nodes.statement: For $u,v \in \F_q^m$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} ((\bra{u}-\bra{v}) \ot \bra{\psi}) \cdot A_{\mathrm{comb}} & = ((\bra{u}-\bra{v}) \ot \bra{\psi}) \cdot \sum_{w \in \F_q^m} \ket{w} \ot A^w \ot I \\ & = \bra{\psi} \cdot ((A^u-A^v)\ot I). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Therefore \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger \bigl((\ket{u}-\ket{v})(\bra{u}-\bra{v}) \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}\bigr) A_{\mathrm{comb}} \] by Lemma~\ref{prop:laplacian-rewrite}, and hence \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} ((A^u-A^v)\ot I)\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}((A^u-A^v)\ot I) \] by \eqref{eq:edge-difference-action}. Taking the trace gives \[ \Tr(A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}}) = \frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A^v)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.name: Compute the action of edge differences, apply the Laplacian rewrite and take the
nodes.statement_short: Compute the action of edge differences, apply the Laplacian rewrite and take the trace.

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} ((\bra{u}-\bra{v}) \ot \bra{\psi}) \cdot A_{\mathrm{comb}} & = ((\bra{u}-\bra{v}) \ot \bra{\psi}) \cdot \sum_{w \in \F_q^m} \ket{w} \ot A^w \ot I \\ & = \bra{\psi} \cdot ((A^u-A^v)\ot I). \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Edge difference action
nodes.label: eq:edge-difference-action

nodes.statement: Write \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \ket{\varphi_0} \ot A_0 + \ket{\varphi_\perp} \ot A_\perp, \] where $\ket{\varphi_\perp}$ is orthogonal to $\ket{\varphi_0}$. Then \[ \frac{1}{q^m}\Tr((\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(I\ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)) = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.name: Global variance as the orthogonal Fourier mass
nodes.statement_short: Global variance equals the mass of $A_{\mathrm{comb}}$ orthogonal to the constant vector.
assumptions: where $\ket{\varphi_\perp}$ is orthogonal to $\ket{\varphi_0}$
nodes.label: lem:global-rewrite

nodes.statement: We first compute \[ A_0 = (\bra{\varphi_0}\ot I)\cdot A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \left(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \bra{u}\right) \ot I \cdot \left(\sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \ket{u} \ot A^u \ot I\right) = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} A^u \ot I. \] Writing $A_{\mathrm{avg}}=\E_u A^u$, it follows that \[ \ket{\varphi_0}\ot A_0 = \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \ket{u} \ot A_{\mathrm{avg}} \ot I, \qquad \ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp = \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \ket{u} \ot (A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \ot I. \] Hence \begin{equation} \frac{1}{M} \cdot \Tr((\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(I\ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)) = \E_{u \sim \F_q^m} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Moreover, \[ \E_{u \sim \F_q^m}(A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 = \E_{u \sim \F_q^m}\bigl((A^u)^2-(A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2\bigr) = \frac12 \E_{u,v \sim \F_q^m} (A^u-A^v)^2. \] Substituting this identity into \eqref{eq:just-took-trace} yields \[ \frac{1}{M} \cdot \Tr((\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(I\ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)) = \frac12 \E_{u,v \sim \F_q^m} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A^v)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.name: Compute $A_0$ as the average, then the orthogonal part's trace equals the varian
nodes.statement_short: Compute $A_0$ as the average, then the orthogonal part's trace equals the variance.

nodes.statement: \frac{1}{M} \cdot \Tr((\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(I\ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)) = \E_{u \sim \F_q^m} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Just took trace
nodes.label: eq:just-took-trace

nodes.statement: For every family $\{A^u\}$, \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi) \le m\, \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.name: Local-to-global inequality
nodes.statement_short: Global variance is at most $m$ times local variance (spectral gap).

nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}} & = (\bra{\varphi_0}\ot A_0+\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_0}\ot A_0+\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp) \\ & = (\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp) \\ & = \bra{\varphi_\perp}L\ket{\varphi_\perp} \cdot A_\perp \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} A_\perp. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The second step uses that $\ket{\varphi_0}$ is a $0$-eigenvector of $L$. nodes.statement: We want to bound \begin{equation} \E_{u,v \sim \F_q^m} \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \lVert (A^u_{g(u)}-A^v_{g(v)}) \ot (G_g)^{1/2} \ket{\psi} \rVert^2 = \E_{u,v \sim \F_q^m} \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (A^u_{g(u)}-A^v_{g(v)})^2 \ot G_g \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} For each $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, define \[ A(g)^u := A^u_{g(u)}, \qquad \ket{\psi_g} := (I \ot (G_g)^{1/2})\ket{\psi}. \] Then \[ \eqref{eq:global-variance-target} = \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \E_{u,v \sim \F_q^m} \bra{\psi_g} (A(g)^u-A(g)^v)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi_g} = \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} 2\,\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A(g),\psi_g). \] Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:local-to-global} gives \[ \eqref{eq:global-variance-target} \le \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} 2m\,\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A(g),\psi_g) = m \cdot \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \bra{\psi} (A^u_{g(u)}-A^v_{g(v)})^2 \ot G_g \ket{\psi}. \] The last quantity is at most $m \cdot 24\left(\eps+\delta+\frac{md}{q}\right)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:equivalent-local-variance}, which is exactly \ref{eq:global-variance-of-points-equation}.
