Let $T=\{T_g\}$ and $Z$ be the optimal solutions to the SDPs~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} and~\eqref{eq:dual-objective} given by Lemma~ef{lem:sdp}. Then $T$ is a measurement, and  egin{align}  orall g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}: \qquad Z &\geq \left(\E_{u} A^{u}_{g(u)}ight), \ T_g \cdot Z &= T_g \cdot \left(\E_{u} A^{u}_{g(u)}ight). \end{align} For each $u \in \F_q^m$, define $H^u=\{H_h^u\}_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}$ by \[ H_h^u := A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)}, \] and let \[ H_h := \E_{u} H_h^u. \] The pointwise family $H^u$ is a submeasurement because \[ \sum_h H_h^u = \sum_a A_a^u \cdot \Big(\sum_{h:h(u)=a} T_h\Big)\cdot A_a^u \le \sum_a (A_a^u)^2 = I, \] where the inequality uses that~$T$ is a measurement and the last identity uses that~$A$ is projective. Averaging over~$u$ gives \[ \sum_h H_h = \E_{u} \sum_h H_h^u \le I, \] so $H$ is also a submeasurement and therefore lies in~$\polysub{m}{q}{d}$. Set \[ \zeta_{\mathrm{variance}} = 24m\cdot\Big(\eps + \delta +  rac{md}{q}\Big). \] Lemma~ef{lem:add-in-u} below is the technical transfer from the averaged family~$H$ back to the sandwiched operators $A^u_{h(u)}T_hA^u_{h(u)}$. We use it in the completeness, consistency, strong self-consistency, and boundedness estimates that follow. We now verify the four conclusions of Lemma~ef{lem:self-improvement-helper}. \emph{Proof of ef{item:self-improvement-completeness}.} The completeness of~$H$ is  egin{align} \sum_h  ra{\psi} H_h \ot I \ket{\psi} &= \E_{u} \sum_h  ra{\psi} H^{u}_h \ot I \ket{\psi} 
otag\ &= \E_{u} \sum_h  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{align} Grouping the polynomials according to their value at~$u$ gives  egin{equation} \E_{u} \sum_h  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot I \ket{\psi} = \E_{u} \sum_a  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{a} \cdot T_{[h(u) = a]} \cdot A^{u}_{a} igr) \ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} We first move the leftmost copy of~$A^u_a$ across the bipartition:  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:group-by-point-value} \approx_{2\sqrt{\delta}} \E_{u} \sum_a  ra{\psi}  igl(T_{[h(u)=a]} \cdot A^{u}_{a} igr) \ot A^{u}_{a} \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} The difference is bounded by Cauchy--Schwarz as in~\eqref{eq:move-first-point-projector-cauchy-schwarz}; the first factor is at most $\sqrt{2\delta}$ by self-consistency of~$A$, and the second is at most~$1$ because $T_{[h(u)=a]} \le I$. We next remove the remaining copy of~$A^u_a$ on Bob's side:  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:first-point-projector-transport} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \E_{u} \sum_a  ra{\psi}  igl(T_{[h(u)=a]} \cdot A^{u}_{a} igr) \ot I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} The first Cauchy--Schwarz factor is at most~$1$ because the fiber operators form a submeasurement after grouping~$T$ by the value of~$h(u)$. Here the second Cauchy--Schwarz factor is \[ \E_{u} \sum_{a
eq b}  ra{\psi} A^u_a \ot A^u_b \ket{\psi}, \] which is at most~$\delta$ because~$A$ is self-consistent and projective. Reindexing by~$h$ and using~\eqref{eq:swap-Z-for-A}, \[ \eqref{eq:first-moved-completeness} = \sum_h  ra{\psi}  igl(T_h \cdot \E_{u} A^u_{h(u)} igr) \ot I \ket{\psi} = \sum_h  ra{\psi} (T_h \cdot Z) \ot I \ket{\psi} =  ra{\psi} Z \ot I \ket{\psi}. \] Thus  egin{equation} \sum_h  ra{\psi} H_h \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq  ra{\psi} Z \ot I \ket{\psi} - 3\sqrt{\delta}. \end{equation} Since $G$ is a measurement,~\eqref{eq:Z-greater-than-A} and Lemma~ef{prop:simeq-for-measurements} give \[  ra{\psi} Z \ot I \ket{\psi} \ge \E_{u} \sum_a  ra{\psi} A^u_a \ot G_{[g(u)=a]} \ket{\psi} \ge 1-
u. \] Therefore the completeness is at least $1-
u-3\sqrt{\delta}$, which is bounded below by $(1-
u)-\zeta$. \emph{Proof of ef{item:self-improvement-A-consistency}.} The inconsistency of~$H$ with~$A$ is  egin{equation} \E_{u} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} A^{u}_a \ot H_{[h(u) = b]} \ket{\psi} = \E_{u} \sum_{a, h: h(u) 
eq a}  ra{\psi} A^{u}_a \ot H_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} The theorem-side off-diagonal selection used for this `add-in-u` application is , and the corresponding left/right scalar quantities are and . The selected scalar chain for this specialization is recorded by . Apply Lemma~ef{lem:add-in-u} with $\mathcal O=\F_q$, $M=A$, and $S_u=\{(a,h):h(u)
eq a\}$. Then \[ \eqref{eq:point-consistency-expansion} \approx_{4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \E_{u} \sum_{a, h: h(u) 
eq a}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot A^{u}_a \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr)\ot T_h \ket{\psi}, \] and the right-hand side is~$0$ because~$A$ is projective. Hence  egin{equation} \E_{u} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} A^{u}_a \ot H_{[h(u) = b]} \ket{\psi} \leq 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \end{equation} Since \[ 4\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} = 4 \sqrt{24 m \cdot\Big(\eps + \delta +  rac{md}{q}\Big)} \le 20 m \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big) \le \zeta, \] this proves ef{item:self-improvement-A-consistency}. \emph{Proof of ef{item:self-improvement-self}.} From the definition of $H_h^u$ and the projectivity of~$A$,  egin{align} H^u_h &= A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)} = A^u_{h(u)} \cdot H^u_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)}, \ A^u_{h(u)} \cdot H^u_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)} &= H^u_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)} =  igl(A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)} igr)\cdot  one{h(u) = h'(u)}. \end{align} The strong self-consistency expression is  egin{equation} \sum_{h\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H_h \ot H_h \ket{\psi} = \E_{u} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H_h^{u} \ot H_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Apply Lemma~ef{lem:add-in-u} with $\mathcal O=\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, $M=H$, and $S_u=\{(h,h):h\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}\}$. This gives  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:self-consistency-expansion} \approx_{4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \E_{u} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot H_h^{u} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} We next enlarge the sum from $h'=h$ to all pairs $h,h'$:  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:add-point-conditioning} \approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} +  rac{md}{q}} \E_{u} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot H^{u}_{h'} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} The added off-diagonal contribution is  egin{align} \eqref{eq:enlarge-polynomial-sum}-\eqref{eq:add-point-conditioning} &= \E_{u} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot H^{u}_{h'} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi} 
otag\ &= \E_{u} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  one{h(u) = h'(u)}, \end{align} where the second equality is~\eqref{eq:h-blt}. To estimate~\eqref{eq:added-indicator}, first replace the left copy of $A^u_{h(u)}$ by $A^v_{h(v)}$:  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:added-indicator} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  one{h(u) = h'(u)}. \end{equation} The corresponding Cauchy--Schwarz bound is  egin{multline} \Big|\E_{u,v} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl((A^{u}_{h(u)} - A^{v}_{h(v)}) \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  one{h(u) = h'(u)}\Big|\ \leq \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl((A^{u}_{h(u)} - A^{v}_{h(v)}) \cdot T_{h'} \cdot (A^{u}_{h(u)} - A^{v}_{h(v)}) igr) \ot T_h\ket{\psi}}\ \cdot \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h\ket{\psi} \cdot  one{h(u) = h'(u)}}. \end{multline} The first factor is bounded by $\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}$ via Lemma~ef{lem:global-variance-of-points}, and the second by~$1$ because $T$ and $H^u$ are submeasurements. Repeating the same argument for the remaining copy of~$A$ yields  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:swapped-u-for-v} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  one{h(u) = h'(u)}. \end{equation} The same intermediate estimate gives  egin{equation} \E_{u,v} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr)\ot T_h\ket{\psi} \leq 1, \end{equation} so Schwartz--Zippel bounds the indicator average by $md/q$ and proves~\eqref{eq:enlarge-polynomial-sum}. Using~\eqref{eq:h-blt}, the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:enlarge-polynomial-sum} is  egin{equation} \E_{u} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi}  igl(H^{u}_{h'} \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Replace the remaining copy of $A^u_{h(u)}$ by $A^v_{h(v)}$:  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:remove-point-projector} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi}  igl(H^{u}_{h'} \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Here the first Cauchy--Schwarz factor is at most~$1$ because $T$ and $H^u$ are submeasurements, and the second is again bounded by Lemma~ef{lem:global-variance-of-points}. Finally move this last copy of~$A^v_{h(v)}$ to Bob's side:  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:replace-final-point-conditioner} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H^{u}_{h'} \ot  igl(T_h \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Substituting~\eqref{eq:swap-Z-for-A}, then~\eqref{eq:Z-greater-than-A}, and finally the already proved bound~\eqref{eq:explicit-bound-for-A-consistency}, one obtains \[ \eqref{eq:move-over-v} \ge \sum_h  ra{\psi} H_h \ot I \ket{\psi} - 4\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \] Combining~\eqref{eq:add-point-conditioning}, \eqref{eq:enlarge-polynomial-sum}, \eqref{eq:replace-final-point-conditioner}, and~\eqref{eq:move-over-v} gives \[ \sum_h  ra{\psi} H_h \ot H_h \ket{\psi} \ge \sum_h  ra{\psi} H_h \ot I \ket{\psi} - 11 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} - \sqrt{2\delta} -  rac{md}{q}. \] The Lean formalization records this step as named internal bounds, starting with the structure and the exact residual-side expansion and then uses the proved lemma together with to recover the final helper-stage self-consistency conclusion. The theorem-level derivation is therefore not moved into an additional hypothesis. The paper's arithmetic shows that the right-hand error is at most \[ 57m\cdot \Big(\eps^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big) \le \zeta, \] which proves ef{item:self-improvement-self}. \emph{Proof of ef{item:self-improvement-boundedness}.} The helper-stage boundedness quantity is \[  ra{\psi} Z \ot I \ket{\psi} -\E_{u} \sum_a  ra{\psi} A^{u}_{a} \ot H_{[h(u)=a]} \ket{\psi}. \] The reindexing of the sum by~$h$ is the algebraic identity \[ \sum_a A^u_a \ot H_{[h(u)=a]} = \sum_h A^u_{h(u)} \ot H_h, \] whose averaged scalar form reads \[ \E_u \sum_a  ra{\psi}\,A^u_a \ot H_{[h(u)=a]}\,\ket{\psi} = \E_u \sum_h  ra{\psi}\,A^u_{h(u)} \ot H_h\,\ket{\psi}. \] Using $\sum_a A_a^u=I$, the pointwise difference between the right-placed total $I \ot H.\mathrm{total} = \sum_h I \ot H_h$ and the helper-agreement operator at $u$ reindexes as the off-diagonal sum \[ \sum_h I \ot H_h - \sum_a A^u_a \ot H_{[h(u)=a]} = \sum_h \sum_{a 
eq h(u)} A^u_a \ot H_h, \] whose averaged scalar form reads \[ \sum_h  ra{\psi}\,I \ot H_h\,\ket{\psi} - \E_u \sum_a  ra{\psi}\,A^u_a \ot H_{[h(u)=a]}\,\ket{\psi} = \E_u \sum_h \sum_{a 
eq h(u)}  ra{\psi}\,A^u_a \ot H_h\,\ket{\psi}. \] Combined with~\eqref{eq:explicit-bound-for-A-consistency} this gives \[  ra{\psi} Z \ot I \ket{\psi} -\E_{u} \sum_a  ra{\psi} A^{u}_{a} \ot H_{[h(u)=a]} \ket{\psi} \le  ra{\psi} Z \ot I \ket{\psi} - \sum_h  ra{\psi} I \ot H_h \ket{\psi} + 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \] By~\eqref{eq:h-versus-z-lower-bound}, the right-hand side is at most $3\sqrt{\delta}+4\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}$. Substituting the definition of $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$ and collecting terms gives \[ 23m\cdot\Big(\eps^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big) \le \zeta. \] Together with~\eqref{eq:Z-greater-than-A}, this proves ef{item:self-improvement-boundedness}.

nodes.statement: In every concrete matrix realization, the uniform family \(T_g=(2|\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}|)^{-1}I\) has total mass \((1/2)I\). The dual operator \(Z=2I\) dominates the identity and satisfies \(Z-A_g\geq I\), hence \(Z\geq A_g\), for every polynomial \(g\). In the canonical block SDP, the corresponding block matrix is feasible, its slack block is \((1/2)I\), and the canonical dual slack for the same dual witness also dominates the block identity. More generally, dual feasibility implies positivity of \(Z\), since the averaged point operators \(A_g\) are positive semidefinite.

Lean isolates the saturated canonical optimal-pair output required from strong duality: a feasible canonical primal matrix, a dual-feasible operator with equal objective value, canonical complementary slackness, and vanishing of the extra canonical slack block. This datum gives the matrix-level slackness-carrying SDP statement, whose witness is already a complete matrix measurement, and is then transported to the abstract Section~9 statement without assuming \(I \le Z\). The displayed measurement witness is read directly from that abstract statement. The canonical saturation datum is now the only matrix-level input used to pass from strong duality to the abstract SDP statement. The paper-facing self-improvement helper consumes the resulting abstract SDP statement.

nodes.statement: Rewrite~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} in canonical block form. Let $r$ be the dimension of the space on which~$A$ acts, let $M = |\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}|$, and fix an ordering $g_1,\ldots,g_M$ of the polynomials. Consider \begin{align} \sup &\quad \Tr(C^\dagger X) \\ \text{s.t.} &\quad \Tr(D_{ij}^\dagger X) = b_{ij} \qquad\forall i,j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}, \notag\\ &\quad X \geq 0, \notag \end{align} where \[ C = \sum_{i = 1}^M \ket{i}\bra{i} \ot A_{g_i}, \] and, for $i,j \in \{1,\ldots,r\}$, \[ D_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \ket{k}\bra{k} \ot \ket{i}\bra{j}, \qquad b_{ij} = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if } i = j,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \] Writing $X=\sum_{i,j=1}^{M+1}\ket{i}\bra{j}\ot X_{ij}$, the constraints say precisely that $\sum_{i=1}^{M+1} X_{ii}=I$, hence $\sum_{i=1}^{M}X_{ii}\le I$, and the objective is \[ \Tr(C^\dagger X)=\sum_{i=1}^M \Tr(A_{g_i}\cdot X_{ii}). \] Thus~\eqref{eq:primal-canonical} is equivalent to~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} under the identification $T_{g_i}=X_{ii}$. The canonical dual is \begin{align} \inf &\quad \sum_i\, z_{ij} b_{ij} \\ \text{s.t.} &\quad \sum_{i,j} \,z_{ij} D_{ij} \geq C. \end{align} Since \[ \sum_{i,j=1}^r z_{ij} D_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \ket{k}\bra{k} \ot \left(\sum_{i,j=1}^r z_{ij}\ket{i}\bra{j}\right) =: \sum_{k=1}^{M+1}\ket{k}\bra{k} \ot Z, \] the constraint~\eqref{eq:dual-canonical-constraint} is exactly $Z\ge A_{g_i}$ for every $i$, and the objective is $\Tr(Z)$. In Lean, the latter statement is recorded as the trace-pairing identity \[ \Re\Tr(D(Z)X)=\Re\Tr(Z) \] for every feasible canonical primal matrix \(X\), where \(D(Z)\) denotes the block-diagonal canonical dual operator. Consequently the canonical primal-dual gap is the real trace pairing of \(X\) with the canonical dual slack \(D(Z)-C\). Since the real trace pairing of positive semidefinite operators is nonnegative, Lean also records the resulting weak-duality inequality for any feasible canonical primal and dual pair. Hence~\eqref{eq:dual-canonical} is equivalent to~\eqref{eq:dual-objective}. Slater's condition holds because \[ T_g = \frac{1}{2M}\cdot I \qquad\forall g\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}, \qquad Z = 2I \] are strictly feasible for the primal and dual respectively. Therefore strong duality holds. For an optimal pair $(X,(z_{ij}))$ in canonical form, complementary slackness gives \begin{equation} X\Big( \sum_{i,j} \,z_{ij} D_{ij} - C \Big) \,=\, 0. \end{equation} We may assume that $X$ is block diagonal. Translating~\eqref{eq:complementary-slackness} back to the variables $\{T_g\}$ and~$Z$ yields $T_g(Z-A_g)=0$ for every~$g$ and \(S Z=0\), where \(S=I-\sum_gT_g\) is the slack block. The paper then treats this as forcing \(S=0\). The Lean development records this saturation as part of the canonical optimal-pair datum for the block SDP. The canonical calculation still uses the auxiliary expression \texttt{matrixSdpComplementarySlacknessDefect} to read off the polynomial blocks of \eqref{eq:complementary-slackness}. The matrix optimal-witness interface, however, stores the displayed equation \(T_gZ=T_gA_g\) directly; \texttt{MatrixSdpOptimalWitness.primalMeasurement} expresses \(\sum_g T_g=I\) as a complete measurement. The statement \texttt{MatrixSdpStatementWithSlackness} records this matrix-level strong-duality output and the abstract theorem \texttt{sdp\_statement\_with\_slackness} specializes it to the paper's self-improvement setting. The explicit Slater witnesses used above are isolated in Lemma~\ref{lem:sdp-matrix-feasible-bounds} and separately recorded by \texttt{matrixSdpStrictPrimalSubmeasurement}, \texttt{matrixSdpStrictDualWitness}, and \texttt{matrixSdpFeasibleBounds\_canonical}; the dual feasibility of \(2I\) follows from \texttt{matrixAveragedPointOperator\_le\_one}. The block-diagonal reduction is also recorded for arbitrary feasible canonical matrices: extracting the diagonal blocks preserves the objective and transfers canonical complementary slackness to the extracted paper primal submeasurement.

nodes.statement:
We begin by expanding  egin{align} \E_{u} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi} M^{u}_o \ot H_h \ket{\psi} &= \E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi} M^{u}_o \ot H^{v}_h \ket{\psi} 
otag\ &= \E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi} M^{u}_o \ot  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ket{\psi}. \end{align} We claim that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:expand-that-H} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot M^{u}_o igr) \ot  igl(T_h \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference:  egin{multline} \Big|\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \ot I - I \ot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \cdot  igl(M^{u}_o \ot (T_h \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)}) igr)\ket{\psi}\Big|\ \leq \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \ot I - I \ot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \cdot (M^{u}_o \ot T_h) \cdot  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \ot I - I \ot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ket{\psi}}\ \cdot \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi} M^{u}_o \ot  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot T_h\cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline} The first factor is controlled by summing over the value $a = h(v)$:  egin{align*} &\E_{u,v} \sum_{a \in \F_q}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^v_a \ot I - I \ot A^v_a igr) \cdot \Bigl(\sum_{(o,h)\in S_u,\, h(v)=a} M^u_o \ot T_h\Bigr) \cdot  igl(A^v_a \ot I - I \ot A^v_a igr)\ket{\psi} \ &\le \E_{u,v} \sum_{a \in \F_q}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^v_a \ot I - I \ot A^v_a igr)^2 \ket{\psi}, \end{align*} where the inequality uses that $M^u$ and $T$ are submeasurements. By Lemma~ef{prop:simeq-to-approx} and the self-consistency of~$A$, this is at most $2\delta$. The second factor is \[ \E_{u,v} \sum_{(o,h)\in S_u}  ra{\psi} M^u_o \ot H^v_h \ket{\psi}, \] which is at most~$1$ because $M^u$ and $H^v$ are submeasurements. Next, we claim that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:move-first-point-projector} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot M^{u}_o \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Again, we bound the magnitude of the difference:  egin{align} &\Big|\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl((A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot M^{u}_o) \ot T_h igr) \cdot  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \ot I - I \ot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ket{\psi}\Big| 
otag\ &\leq \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot M^{u}_o \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}} \ &\qquad\cdot \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \ot I - I \ot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \cdot (M^{u}_o \ot T_h) \cdot  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \ot I - I \ot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ket{\psi}}. 
otag \end{align} The first factor is bounded by  egin{align*} &\E_{u,v} \sum_h  ra{\psi} \Bigl(A^v_{h(v)} \cdot \sum_{o:(o,h)\in S_u} M^u_o \cdot A^v_{h(v)}\Bigr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \ &\le \E_{u,v} \sum_h  ra{\psi} (A^v_{h(v)})^2 \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \le \E_{u,v} \sum_h  ra{\psi} I \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \le 1, \end{align*} using first that $M$ is a submeasurement, then that $A^v_{h(v)} \le I$, and finally that $T$ is a submeasurement ($\sum_g T_g \le I$). The second factor is exactly the same expression as in~\eqref{eq:move-first-point-projector-cauchy-schwarz}, hence at most $\sqrt{2\delta}$. Having moved both copies of~$A$ to the left-hand side, we next show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:move-second-point-projector} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot M^{u}_o \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} The difference is bounded by  egin{multline} \Big|\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl((A^{v}_{h(v)} - A^{u}_{h(u)}) \cdot M^{u}_o \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\ \leq \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl((A^{v}_{h(v)} - A^{u}_{h(u)}) \cdot M^{u}_o \cdot (A^{v}_{h(v)} - A^{u}_{h(u)}) igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}}\ \cdot \sqrt{\E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{v}_{h(v)} \cdot M^{u}_o \cdot A^{v}_{h(v)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline} The first factor can be rewritten as  egin{align*} &\E_{u,v} \sum_h  ra{\psi} \Bigl((A^v_{h(v)} - A^u_{h(u)}) \cdot \sum_{o:(o,h)\in S_u} M^u_o \cdot (A^v_{h(v)} - A^u_{h(u)})\Bigr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi} \ &\le \E_{u,v} \sum_h  ra{\psi} (A^v_{h(v)} - A^u_{h(u)})^2 \ot T_h \ket{\psi}, \end{align*} because $M^u$ is a submeasurement. Lemma~ef{lem:global-variance-of-points} bounds this by~$\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$ since $T \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$. The second factor is exactly the first factor from~\eqref{eq:move-second-point-projector-cauchy-schwarz}, so it is at most~$1$. Finally, we show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:replace-left-point-conditioner} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \E_{u,v} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{u}}  ra{\psi}  igl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot M^{u}_o \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)} igr) \ot T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} The same Cauchy--Schwarz estimate as in~\eqref{eq:replace-left-point-conditioner-cauchy-schwarz}, with the final copy of $A^v_{h(v)}$ replaced by $A^u_{h(u)}$, gives the same bound $\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}$. Indeed, the factor containing $A^u_{h(u)} \cdot M^u_o \cdot A^u_{h(u)}$ is bounded by~$1$ by the same submeasurement argument as above, while the factor containing $(A^v_{h(v)} - A^u_{h(u)})^2$ is unchanged. Summing the four transports gives an error of $2\sqrt{2\delta} + 2\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}$, and the lemma follows from $2\delta \leq \zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.

nodes.statement: Several auxiliary results are used to prove Theorem~\ref{thm:self-improvement} from the helper output and the orthonormalization theorem. They record local intermediate estimates and final-field assembly lemmas. The former orthonormalization spectral-transport record has been retired; the spectral-truncation part of the construction is now represented directly by \texttt{spectralTruncationStatement\_of\_sourceAlmostProjective}. nodes.statement: Let $G \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ be a measurement with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $u \sim \F_q^{m}$, \[ A^{u}_a \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G_{[g(u)=a]}. \] \end{enumerate} Let \[ \zeta = 3000m\cdot \Big(\eps^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big). \] Then there exists a projective submeasurement $H \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Completeness): If $H = \sum_h H_h$, then \[ \bra{\psi} H \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\nu)-\zeta. \] \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $u \sim \F_q^m$, \[ A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\zeta} I \ot H_{[h(u) = a]}. \] \item (Strong self-consistency): \[ H_h \ot I \approx_{\zeta} I \ot H_h. \] \item (Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z$ such that \[ \bra{\psi} Z \ot (I - H) \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta \] and for each $h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \[ Z \geq \left(\E_{u} A^{u}_{h(u)}\right). \] \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: By Definition~\ref{def:restricted-diagonal-lines-test}, the strategy passes the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma m$. Hence \[ A_a^u \otimes I \simeq_{\gamma m} I \otimes L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]} \] on average over uniformly random $u \sim \F_q^m$ and a uniformly random line $\ell$ in $\F_q^m$ containing $u$. By \ref{prop:simeq-to-approx}, \begin{equation} A_a^u \otimes I \approx_{2\gamma m} I \otimes L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]}. \end{equation} Let $u$ and $v$ be independent uniformly random points in $\F_q^m$, and let $\ell$ be a uniformly random line containing both points. The marginal distribution on $(u,\ell)$ and on $(v,\ell)$ is the same as above, so \begin{align*} (A_a^u A_b^v) \ot I & \approx_{2\gamma m} A_a^u \otimes L^\ell_{[f(v)=b]} \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \\ & \approx_{2\gamma m} I \otimes \bigl(L^\ell_{[f(v)=b]} L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]}\bigr) \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \\ & = I \otimes \bigl(L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]} L^\ell_{[f(v)=b]}\bigr) \tag{because~$L$ is projective} \\ & \approx_{2\gamma m} A_b^v \otimes L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]} \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \\ & \approx_{2\gamma m} (A_b^v A_a^u) \ot I. \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \end{align*} The theorem follows from \ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}.

nodes.statement:
Conditioning the low individual degree test on the last coordinate direction gives, on average over $(u,x) \sim \F_q^{m+1}$,
\[
	A_a^{u,x} \ot I \simeq_{(m+1)\eps} I \ot B^u_{[f(x)=a]}.
\]
Hence \ref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and $(m+1)\le 2m$ imply
\[
	A_a^{u,x} \ot I \approx_{4m\eps} I \ot B^u_{[f(x)=a]}.
\]
Using also the $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-goodness assumption and \ref{prop:simeq-to-approx},
\[
	I \ot A_a^{u,x} \approx_{2\delta} A_a^{u,x} \ot I \approx_{4m\eps} I \ot B^u_{[f(x)=a]}.
\]
Therefore \ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta} yields
\begin{equation} I \ot A_a^{u,x} \approx_{8m\eps+4\delta} I \ot B^u_{[f(x)=a]}.
\end{equation}
Applying \ref{prop:triangle-sub} to \ref{item:ld-pasting-consistency} and \ref{eq:ld-abcon} gives
\begin{equation} G^x_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I \simeq_{\nu_1} I \ot B^u_{[f(x)=a]},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation} \nu_1 = \zeta + \sqrt{8m\eps+4\delta}.
\end{equation}
Finally, \ref{thm:com-main} gives
\begin{equation} G_g^x G_h^y \ot I \approx_{\nu_{\mathrm{com}}} G_h^y G_g^x \ot I,
\end{equation}
where
\[
	\nu_{\mathrm{com}} = 30m\left(\gamma^{1/4}+\zeta^{1/4}+(d/q)^{1/4}\right).
\]

nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item \textbf{Head--tail split identities.} For every $k \ge 0$, point tuple $\bx = (x_1,\dots,x_{k+1})$, and outcome tuple $\bg = (g_1,\dots,g_{k+1})$, \[ \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1}\cdots \widehat G^{x_{k+1}}_{g_{k+1}} = \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \bigl( \widehat G^{x_2}_{g_2}\cdots \widehat G^{x_{k+1}}_{g_{k+1}} \bigr), \] and the right half-sandwich analogously rotates the head to the tail. \item \textbf{Sum-of-adjoint-products bounds.} For every $r\ge 0$ and $\bx = (x_1,\dots,x_r) \in \F_q^r$, \[ \sum_{g_1,\dots,g_r} \bigl(\widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\bigr)^\dagger \bigl(\widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\bigr) \;\le\; I, \] and the same bound holds for the reverse-order product family. \item \textbf{Generic tensor contraction.} If families~$\{A_a\}_a$ and~$\{B_b\}_b$ satisfy $\sum_a A_a^\dagger A_a \le I$ and $\sum_b B_b^\dagger B_b \le I$, then \[ \sum_{a,b} (A_a \ot B_b)^\dagger (A_a \ot B_b) \le I. \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.name: Completed sandwich normalization
nodes.statement_short: Head--tail split identities, normalization of completed product families, and tensor contraction bound.
nodes.label: lem:completed-sandwich-normalization

nodes.statement: The split identities follow from the completed-outcome equivalences. The normalization inequalities are the corresponding submeasurement bounds for the left and right half-products after reindexing the sums.
nodes.name: Completed-outcome equivalences and submeasurement bounds after reindexing.
nodes.statement_short: Completed-outcome equivalences and submeasurement bounds after reindexing.

nodes.statement: Given the completed-measurement self-consistency and commutation estimates from Corollary~\ref{cor:G-hat-facts}, the following one-step estimates hold. \begin{enumerate} \item \textbf{Self-consistency step.} For every~$r\ge 0$, \[ \E_{x,y,z}\E_{x_1,\dots,x_r} \sum_{g} \bigl\| \bigl(\widehat G^{z}_g \ot I - I \ot \widehat G^{z}_g\bigr) \ket{\psi} \bigr\|^2 \;\le\; 2\zeta. \] \item \textbf{Commutation step.} For every~$r\ge 0$, \[ \E_{x,y}\E_{x_1,\dots,x_r} \sum_{g,h}\sum_{g_1,\dots,g_r} \bigl\| \bigl( \widehat G^{x}_g \widehat G^{y}_h \ot \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\cdots \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} - \widehat G^{y}_h \widehat G^{x}_g \ot \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\cdots \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \bigr) \ket{\psi} \bigr\|^2 \;\le\; \nu_3. \] \item \textbf{Two-factor base case.} For $k=2$, the commutation chain reduces to the same tensor-placement convention with the reverse tail product equal to the identity, hence to the pairwise estimate~$\nu_3$. \item \textbf{Split equivalences.} The half-sandwich families are equivalent, under the head--tail reindexing of Lemma~\ref{lem:completed-sandwich-normalization}, to the chain-families used in the move estimates above, with ordered products on the first tensor factor and reverse products on the second tensor factor where these appear in the commutation step. \end{enumerate} These are the elementary building blocks assembled by the recursive chain construction in the following lemma.
nodes.name: One-step completed sandwich commutation
nodes.statement_short: One-step self-consistency and commutation estimates for completed sandwiches.
nodes.label: lem:one-step-completed-sandwich-commutation

nodes.statement: For the one-step commutation move, rewrite the relevant head--tail split, apply the self-consistency and commutation estimates for~$\widehat G$, and assemble the resulting comparison by the triangle inequality for~$\approx_\delta$.
nodes.name: Rewrite the split, apply $\widehat G$ estimates, triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the split, apply $\widehat G$ estimates, triangle inequality.

nodes.statement: For every $k \ge 2$, \[ \widehat G_{g_1}^{x_1}\widehat G_{g_2}^{x_2}\cdots \widehat G_{g_k}^{x_k} \ot I \approx_{\nu_4} \widehat G_{g_2}^{x_2}\cdots \widehat G_{g_k}^{x_k}\widehat G_{g_1}^{x_1} \ot I, \] where \[ \nu_4 = 426k^2m\left(\gamma^{1/16}+\zeta^{1/16}+(d/q)^{1/16}\right). \]
nodes.name: Commuting past multiple completed measurements
nodes.statement_short: Moving the leftmost completed factor past $k-1$ others costs $\nu_4=426k^2m(\cdot)$.
nodes.label: lem:commute-g-half-sandwich

nodes.statement: Repeatedly move the leftmost factor across the remaining product, using \ref{eq:g-hat-self-consistency} and \ref{eq:g-hat-commutativity} at each step and summing the resulting errors with \ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}. The paper's calculation gives \[ 3k\bigl(4k\zeta + k\nu_3\bigr) \le 426k^2m\left(\gamma^{1/16}+\zeta^{1/16}+(d/q)^{1/16}\right). \]
nodes.name: Repeatedly move the leftmost factor using self-consistency and commutation, summ
nodes.statement_short: Repeatedly move the leftmost factor using self-consistency and commutation, summing errors.

nodes.statement: If the tuple of completed slices does not interpolate to the sampled vertical-line value, then some active coordinate witnesses a line-value mismatch. Concretely, for every direction $u$ and injective tuple $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_k)$, let $\widehat{H}^{\mathbf{x}}\rvert_u$ be the vertical-line restriction of the pasted interpolation family. Then \[ \operatorname{Defect}_\psi\bigl( \widehat{H}^{\mathbf{x}}\rvert_u,\, B^u\bigr) \;\le\; \operatorname{Bad}(\psi;u,\mathbf{x}) \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^k \operatorname{Defect}_\psi\bigl( \widehat{H}^{(i)}(u,\mathbf{x}),\, B^{(i)}(u,\mathbf{x})\bigr), \] where $\operatorname{Defect}_\psi(A,B)$ denotes the bipartite consistency defect $\max\bigl(0,\, \bra{\psi} A_{\mathrm{tot}}\ot B_{\mathrm{tot}}\ket{\psi} - \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a\ot B_a\ket{\psi}\bigr)$, \[ \operatorname{Bad}(\psi;u,\mathbf{x}) = \sum_f \bra{\psi} \Bigl(\sum_{\substack{g_1,\dots,g_k\\ \exists i:\, g_i\ne\bot,\ g_i(u)\ne f(x_i)}} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{\mathbf{x}} \Bigr) \ot B_f^u \ket{\psi}, \] and $\widehat{H}^{(i)},B^{(i)}$ are the one-point line comparison families (Lemma~\ref{lem:ld-sandwich-line-one-point}) restricted to coordinate $i$, and $\operatorname{Bad}(\psi;u,\mathbf{x})\le 1$.
nodes.name: Line-interpolation mismatch estimates
nodes.statement_short: Failed vertical-line interpolation is witnessed by some coordinate's line mismatch, bounded by a sum of one-point defects.
nodes.label: lem:line-interpolation-mismatch-estimates

nodes.statement: The proof first identifies a failed vertical-line interpolation with a particular active coordinate whose slice value disagrees with the line answer. The operator sum over all such failures is then bounded by the sum of the corresponding one-coordinate line defects, using the vertical restriction identities above.
nodes.name: Identify a failed interpolation with a mismatched coordinate and sum one-coordin
nodes.statement_short: Identify a failed interpolation with a mismatched coordinate and sum one-coordinate defects.

nodes.statement: Let $H$ be any polynomial-valued submeasurement. Suppose that the strategy is good, that $\gamma,\zeta \ge 0$, that $k \ge 1$, and that the restriction of $H$ to every vertical line is consistent with the vertical-line measurement with error $\nu_6$. Then the pointwise evaluations of $H$ are consistent with Alice's point measurement with error $\nu$.
nodes.name: Point consistency from vertical-line consistency
assumptions: Let $H$ be any polynomial-valued submeasurement.
the strategy is good, that $\gamma,\zeta \ge 0$, that $k \ge 1$, and that the restriction of $H$ to every vertical line is consistent with the vertical-line measurement with error $\nu_6$
conclusions: Then the pointwise evaluations of $H$ are consistent with Alice's point measurement with error $\nu$.
nodes.label: lem:h-a-consistency-from-line-consistency

nodes.statement: The proof transports the vertical-line consistency estimate to point evaluations and combines it with the good-strategy point-to-line comparison. The displayed numerical assumptions are used only to absorb the intermediate errors into the final parameter~$\nu$.
nodes.name: Transport line consistency to points and absorb errors.
nodes.statement_short: Transport line consistency to points and absorb errors.

nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:remove-the-restriction} - \eqref{eq:sum-restricted-to-global-polynomial} & = \E_{y_1,\dots,y_k} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_\tau(y)}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{y_1,\dots,y_k} \ot I \ket{\psi}\nonumber \\ & = \E_u \E_{y_1,\dots,y_k} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_\tau(y)}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{y_1,\dots,y_k} \ot B_f^u \ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Insert line measurement resolution
nodes.label: eq:insert-line-measurement-resolution

nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:insert-line-measurement-resolution} \approx_{\frac{k^2}{q}+k\nu_5} \E_u \E_{y_1,\dots,y_k} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_\tau(y)}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{y_1,\dots,y_k} \ot B_f^u \ket{\psi} \cdot \bone[\forall i\in\tau,\ f(y_i)=g_i(u)].
nodes.name: Insert line consistency indicator
nodes.label: eq:insert-line-consistency-indicator

nodes.statement: \E_u \E_{y_1,\dots,y_k} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_\tau(y)}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{y_1,\dots,y_k} \ot B_f^u \ket{\psi} \cdot \bone[\exists i\in\tau,\ f(y_i)\ne g_i(u)],
nodes.name: Discarded line inconsistency term
nodes.label: eq:discarded-line-inconsistency-term

nodes.statement: & \E_u \E_{y_1,\dots,y_k} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_\tau(y)}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{y_1,\dots,y_k} \ot I \ket{\psi} \cdot \bone[\mathsf{Consistent}_\tau(g,y,u)]\nonumber \\ ={} & \E_{y_1,\dots,y_k} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_\tau(y)}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{y_1,\dots,y_k} \ot I \ket{\psi} \cdot \Pr_u[\mathsf{Consistent}_\tau(g,y,u)].
nodes.name: Consistent indicator
nodes.label: eq:consistent-indicator

nodes.statement: For $1 \le \ell \le k+1$ and a tail type $\tau_{\ge \ell} \in \{0,1\}^{k-\ell+1}$, define \[ S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} = \sum_{\tau_{<\ell}\,:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} G^{|\tau_{<\ell}|}(I-G)^{(\ell-1)-|\tau_{<\ell}|}. \] This records the contribution of all prefixes that can still be completed to total weight at least $d+1$ once the tail $\tau_{\ge \ell}$ is fixed.
nodes.name: Truncated type sums
nodes.label: def:truncated-type-sums

nodes.statement: Each $S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}$ is Hermitian, positive semidefinite, and bounded by $I$. Moreover, if $\tau_{>\ell}$ is a tail type of length $k-\ell$, then \[ S_{\tau_{>\ell}} = \sum_{\tau_\ell \in \{0,1\}} S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} G^{\tau_\ell}(I-G)^{1-\tau_\ell}. \]
nodes.name: Recurrence for truncated type sums
nodes.statement_short: $S_{\tau_{\ge\ell}}$ is PSD, at most $I$, and satisfies a one-bit recurrence.
nodes.label: lem:truncated-type-sum-recurrence

nodes.statement: Every summand is a polynomial in the commuting positive operators $G$ and $I-G$, so $S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}$ is Hermitian and positive semidefinite. Summing over all prefixes gives \[ S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \le (G+(I-G))^{\ell-1}=I. \] Splitting the next type bit according to whether $\tau_\ell=1$ or $\tau_\ell=0$ gives the stated recurrence.
nodes.name: Polynomials in commuting $G,I-G$; binomial sum gives $\le I$; split the next bit
nodes.statement_short: Polynomials in commuting $G,I-G$; binomial sum gives $\le I$; split the next bit.

nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi_{\mathrm{bi}}}$ be a bipartite state on $\iota \otimes \iota$. If $x_1,\dots,x_k$ are sampled independently and uniformly from $\F_q$, then \[ \E_{x_1,\dots,x_k} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \mathsf{Outcomes}_\tau} \bra{\psi_{\mathrm{bi}}} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{x_1,\dots,x_k} \ot I \ket{\psi_{\mathrm{bi}}} \approx_{\nu_8} \sum_{r=d+1}^k \binom{k}{r} \bra{\psi_{\mathrm{bi}}} G^r(I-G)^{k-r} \ot I \ket{\psi_{\mathrm{bi}}}, \] where \[ \nu_8 = 46k^2m\left(\gamma^{1/32}+\zeta^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right). \]
nodes.name: From the pasted sum to a polynomial in $G$
nodes.statement_short: The averaged pasted sum is $\nu_8$-close to the Bernoulli polynomial $\sum_{r>d}\binom kr G^r(I-G)^{k-r}$.
nodes.label: lem:from-H-to-G

nodes.name: Peel one coordinate at a time: move $\widehat G_{g_\ell}$ to the second register
nodes.statement_short: Peel one coordinate at a time: move $\widehat G_{g_\ell}$ to the second register via self-consistency and commutation, and use the truncated type sum recurrence. The key stage estimate costs $2\sqrt{2\zeta}+2\sqrt{\nu_4}$ per coordinate.

nodes.statement: \widehat G_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} = \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}},
nodes.name: G recurrence
nodes.label: eq:G-recurrence

nodes.statement: \widehat H_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} = \widehat G_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} \bigl(\widehat G_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}}\bigr)^\dagger.
nodes.name: Split H into two Gs
nodes.label: eq:split-H-into-two-Gs

nodes.statement: & \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_{g_{\ge \ell}\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} \ot \bigl(G^{|\tau_{<\ell}|}(I-G)^{(\ell-1)-|\tau_{<\ell}|}\bigr)\ket{\psi}\nonumber \\ \approx_{2\sqrt{2\zeta}+2\sqrt{\nu_4}}{} & \E_{x_{>\ell}} \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \sum_{g_{>\ell}\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{>\ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}} \ot \bigl(G^{|\tau_{\le \ell}|}(I-G)^{\ell-|\tau_{\le \ell}|}\bigr)\ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Bernoulli tail stage reduction
nodes.label: eq:bernoulli-tail-stage-reduction

nodes.statement: S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} = \sum_{\tau_{<\ell}\,:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} G^{|\tau_{<\ell}|}(I-G)^{(\ell-1)-|\tau_{<\ell}|}.
nodes.name: S def
nodes.label: eq:S-def

nodes.statement: & \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{g_{\ge \ell}\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} \ot S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \ket{\psi}\nonumber \\ \approx_{2\sqrt{2\zeta}+2\sqrt{\nu_4}}{} & \E_{x_{>\ell}} \sum_{\tau_{>\ell}} \sum_{g_{>\ell}\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{>\ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}} \ot S_{\tau_{>\ell}} \ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Bernoulli tail stage reduction expanded
nodes.label: eq:bernoulli-tail-stage-reduction-expanded

nodes.statement: In Lean, the type-restricted averaged submeasurement, the per-tail operator/mass, the aggregated stage quantity, and the final Bernoulli-tail scalar from this proof are recorded by the declarations above. Their indexing is shifted to the repository's 0-based convention: Lean stage $\ell$ is the paper's stage $\ell+1$.
nodes.name: Lean proof-stage notation

nodes.statement: S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} & = \sum_{\tau_{<\ell}\,:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} G^{|\tau_{<\ell}|}(I-G)^{(\ell-1)-|\tau_{<\ell}|}\nonumber \\ & \le \sum_{\tau_{<\ell}} G^{|\tau_{<\ell}|}(I-G)^{(\ell-1)-|\tau_{<\ell}|}\nonumber \\ & = (G+(I-G))^{\ell-1} = I.
nodes.name: S bound
nodes.label: eq:S-bound

nodes.statement: \E_{x_\ell} \sum_{g_\ell \in \mathsf O_{\tau_\ell}} \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell} = G^{\tau_\ell}(I-G)^{1-\tau_\ell}.
nodes.name: Explicit formula for G expectation
nodes.label: eq:explicit-formula-for-G-expectation

nodes.statement: \sum_{\tau_\ell} S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \cdot \Bigl(\E_{x_\ell} \sum_{g_\ell \in \mathsf O_{\tau_\ell}} \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\Bigr) & = \sum_{\tau_\ell} S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} G^{\tau_\ell}(I-G)^{1-\tau_\ell}\nonumber \\ & = S_{\tau_{>\ell}}.
nodes.name: S recurrence
nodes.label: eq:S-recurrence

nodes.statement: S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \cdot \Bigl(\E_{x_\ell} \sum_{g_\ell \in \mathsf O_{\tau_\ell}} \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\Bigr) \cdot S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \le \E_{x_\ell} \sum_{g_\ell \in \mathsf O_{\tau_\ell}} \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell},
nodes.name: S sandwich
nodes.label: eq:S-sandwich

nodes.statement: & \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} \ot S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\ket{\psi}\nonumber \\ ={} & \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \bigl(\widehat G_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} (\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr) \ot S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\ket{\psi}\nonumber \\ \approx_{\sqrt{2\zeta}}{} & \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \bigl(\widehat G_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} (\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger\bigr) \ot \bigl(S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr)\ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Move rightmost g to second factor
nodes.label: eq:move-rightmost-g-to-second-factor

nodes.statement: \Bigl| \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} (\widehat G_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} \ot S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}) \bigl((\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger \ot I\bigr) (\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\ot I - I \ot \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}) \ket{\psi} \Bigr|\\ \le \sqrt{ \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{\ge \ell}}^{x_{\ge \ell}} \ot (S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}})^2 \ket{\psi} } \cdot \sqrt{ \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} (\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\ot I - I \ot \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}) (\widehat H_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}} \ot I) (\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\ot I - I \ot \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}) \ket{\psi} }.
nodes.name: First cauchy schwarz bound
nodes.label: eq:first-cauchy-schwarz-bound

nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:move-rightmost-g-to-second-factor} & = \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \bigl(\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}}(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger\bigr) \ot \bigl(S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr)\ket{\psi}\nonumber \\ & \approx_{\sqrt{\nu_4}} \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \bigl(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger\bigr) \ot \bigl(S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr)\ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Commute g part one
nodes.label: eq:commute-g-part-one

nodes.statement: \Bigl| \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \bigl([\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}},\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}] \ot I\bigr) \bigl((\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger \ot (S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell})\bigr) \ket{\psi} \Bigr|\\ \le \sqrt{ \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} [\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}},\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}] [\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}},\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}]^\dagger \ot I \ket{\psi} } \cdot \sqrt{ \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}} \ot \bigl(\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}(S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}})^2\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr) \ket{\psi} }.
nodes.name: Adjoint commutator cauchy schwarz
nodes.label: eq:adjoint-commutator-cauchy-schwarz

nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:commute-g-part-one} \approx_{\sqrt{\nu_4}} \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \bigl(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}}(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger \widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr) \ot \bigl(S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr)\ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Commute g part two
nodes.label: eq:commute-g-part-two

nodes.statement: \Bigl| \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \bigl(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}} \ot (S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell})\bigr) \bigl([(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger,\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}] \ot I\bigr) \ket{\psi} \Bigr|\\ \le \sqrt{ \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}} \ot \bigl(S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\bigr) \ket{\psi} } \cdot \sqrt{ \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} [(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger,\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}]^\dagger [(\widehat G_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}})^\dagger,\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}] \ot I \ket{\psi} }.
nodes.name: Second cauchy schwarz bound
nodes.label: eq:second-cauchy-schwarz-bound

nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:commute-g-part-two} \approx_{\sqrt{2\zeta}} \E_{x_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \sum_{(g_\ell,g_{>\ell})\in \mathsf O_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_{>\ell}}^{x_{>\ell}} \ot \bigl(S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\widehat G_{g_\ell}^{x_\ell}\bigr) \ket{\psi}.
nodes.name: Remaining g on second factor
nodes.label: eq:remaining-g-on-second-factor

nodes.statement: The nontrivial-regime pasting context specializes the consistency of $H$ with $A$ and the conversion from the pasted sum to the polynomial in $G$ to the parameters and error bounds fixed in Definition~\ref{def:ld-pasting-context}.
nodes.name: Context specializations for the pasted measurement
nodes.label: lem:pasting-context-specializations

nodes.statement: These are direct specializations of the two preceding construction theorems to the notation and numerical hypotheses packaged in the nontrivial-regime pasting context.
nodes.name: Direct specializations to the context notation.
nodes.statement_short: Direct specializations to the context notation.

nodes.statement: Let $0<\theta<1$ and integers $k,d>0$ with $k \ge 2d/\theta$. Define \[ F(X) = \sum_{r=d+1}^k \binom{k}{r} X^r (I-X)^{k-r}. \] If $X$ is Hermitian, $0 \le X \le I$, and $\bra{\psi} X \ot I \ket{\psi} \ge 1-\kappa$, then \[ \bra{\psi} F(X) \ot I \ket{\psi} \ge 1 - \frac{\kappa}{1-\theta} - e^{-\theta^2 k/2}. \]
nodes.name: Matrix Chernoff bound for the Bernoulli polynomial
nodes.statement_short: If $\langle X\rangle\ge1-\kappa$ then the Bernoulli tail polynomial $F(X)$ has expectation $\ge1-\kappa/(1-\theta)-e^{-\theta^2k/2}$.
assumptions: Let $0<\theta<1$ and integers $k,d>0$ with $k \ge 2d/\theta$.
$X$ is Hermitian, $0 \le X \le I$, and $\bra{\psi} X \ot I \ket{\psi} \ge 1-\kappa$
nodes.label: lem:chernoff-bernoulli-matrix

nodes.name: Spectral decomposition, Markov's inequality for spectral mass above $\theta$, an
nodes.statement_short: Spectral decomposition, Markov's inequality for spectral mass above $\theta$, and the scalar Chernoff bound eigenvalue-by-eigenvalue.

nodes.statement: \Pr_{i\sim\mu}[\lambda_i > \theta] \ge 1-\frac{\kappa}{1-\theta}.
nodes.name: Spectral mass threshold
nodes.label: eq:spectral-mass-threshold

nodes.statement: F(p) \ge 1-\exp\Bigl(-2\Bigl(p-\frac{d}{k}\Bigr)^2k\Bigr).
nodes.name: Bernoulli tail chernoff
nodes.label: eq:bernoulli-tail-chernoff

nodes.name: Bernoulli polynomial spectral lower bound
nodes.label: eq:bernoulli-polynomial-spectral-lower-bound

nodes.statement: If $k \ge 400md$, then \[ \bra{\psi} H \ot I \ket{\psi} \ge 1 - \kappa\left(1+\frac{1}{100m}\right) - \nu - e^{-k/(80000m^2)}. \]
nodes.name: Completeness of the pasted submeasurement
assumptions: $k \ge 400md$
nodes.label: cor:ld-pasting-N-completeness

nodes.statement:
Lemma~ef{lem:over-all-outcomes} gives \[  ra{\psi} H \ot I \ket{\psi} \approx_{
u_7} \E_{x_1,\dots,x_k} \sum_{	au:\,|	au|\ge d+1} \sum_{(g_1,\dots,g_k)\in \mathsf{Outcomes}_	au}  ra{\psi} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{x_1,\dots,x_k} \ot I \ket{\psi}. \] Lemma~ef{lem:from-H-to-G} turns the right-hand side into \[ \sum_{r=d+1}^k  inom{k}{r}  ra{\psi} G^r(I-G)^{k-r} \ot I \ket{\psi} \] up to error $

nodes.name: Chain: completeness to outcome sum, to Bernoulli polynomial, then matrix Chernof
nodes.statement_short: Chain: completeness to outcome sum, to Bernoulli polynomial, then matrix Chernoff with $\theta=1/(200m)$.

nodes.statement: For $x \in \F_q$, let $\operatorname{append}_x(\ell)$ be the line in $\F_q^{m+1}$ obtained by appending the coordinate $x$ to every point of a line $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$. If $f \colon \ell \to \F_q$, let $\operatorname{append}_x(f)$ be the polynomial on $\operatorname{append}_x(\ell)$ defined by $\operatorname{append}_x(f)(u,x)=f(u)$.
nodes.name: Appending a line at height $x$
nodes.label: def:append-x

nodes.statement: Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ low individual degree test. For each $x \in \F_q$, the $x$-restricted strategy $(\psi,A^x,B^x,L^x)$ for the $(m,q,d)$ test is defined by \[ (A^x)_a^u = A_a^{u,x}, \qquad (B^x)_f^\ell = B_{\operatorname{append}_x(f)}^{\operatorname{append}_x(\ell)}, \qquad (L^x)_f^\ell = L_{\operatorname{append}_x(f)}^{\operatorname{append}_x(\ell)}. \]
nodes.name: $x$-restricted strategy
nodes.label: def:restricted-strategy

nodes.statement: Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ test. For each $x \in \F_q$, let $(\psi,A^x,B^x,L^x)$ be the restricted strategy and let $\eps_x,\delta_x,\gamma_x$ be its three failure probabilities. Then \[ \E_x \eps_x \le \frac{m+1}{m}\eps, \qquad \E_x \delta_x \le \delta, \qquad \E_x \gamma_x \le \frac{m+1}{m}\gamma. \]
nodes.name: Restricted success probabilities
assumptions: Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ test.
nodes.label: lem:restricted-probabilities

nodes.statement: The self-consistency test restricts exactly to the slice at height $x$. For the axis-parallel and diagonal-line tests, conditioning on the sampled line not being parallel to the last coordinate identifies the test with the corresponding restricted game.
nodes.name: Self-consistency restricts exactly; line tests conditioned on non-vertical lines
nodes.statement_short: Self-consistency restricts exactly; line tests conditioned on non-vertical lines.

nodes.statement: The average restricted errors are the expectations over $x \in \F_q$ of the axis-parallel, self-consistency, and restricted diagonal-line failure probabilities of the $x$-restricted strategies.
nodes.name: Average restricted errors
nodes.label: def:average-restricted-errors

nodes.statement: The weighted bounds from Lemma~\ref{lem:restricted-probabilities} imply the restricted-probability data used in the successor step.
nodes.name: Weighted restricted-probability bounds
nodes.label: lem:weighted-restricted-probability-bounds

nodes.statement: The weighted axis-parallel and diagonal-line estimates are divided by the transverse-direction weight, while the self-consistency estimate is exactly the average restricted self-consistency probability. These three estimates form the restricted-probability record used in the successor step.
nodes.name: Divide weighted estimates by the transverse weight.
nodes.statement_short: Divide weighted estimates by the transverse weight.

nodes.statement: The Lean declaration for Theorem~\ref{thm:self-improvement-in-induction-section} has the paper hypotheses, in particular that \(G\) is a complete polynomial measurement. The labelled theorem in \texttt{references/ldt-paper/inductive\_step.tex:249--286} states the input as a submeasurement, while the proved form in \texttt{references/ldt-paper/self\_improvement.tex:635--671} states it as a measurement. The blueprint and Lean follow the proved measurement-valued form, which is also the form used at the point where the theorem is applied in \texttt{references/ldt-paper/inductive\_step.tex:461--485}. The proof applies \texttt{SelfImprovement.selfImprovement} to \(G\), then uses \texttt{selfImprovementInInductionSectionConclusion\_ofSelfImprovementConclusion} to transport the fields. The Section~\ref{chap:self-improvement} SDP slackness input is supplied by the formalized theorem \texttt{sdp\_statement\_with\_slackness}; it is not an additional hypothesis of the induction-section theorem.
nodes.name: Lean realization of induction self-improvement
nodes.label: rem:self-improvement-in-induction-section-realization

nodes.statement: The Lean declaration linked to Theorem~\ref{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section} is now the unrestricted source-facing restatement. It calls the formal Section~\ref{chap:pasting} theorem \texttt{Pasting.ldPasting} and therefore carries exactly the source hypotheses displayed above, together with the faithful formal boundary hypotheses needed to interpret the objects in Lean. The nontrivial-regime proof reduction remains represented in the Chapter~9 declaration \texttt{Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial}. That helper assumes \[ \gamma \le 1,\qquad \zeta \le 1,\qquad d \le q,\qquad 0<d,\qquad 1\le k. \] These inequalities are not hypotheses of the paper theorem: in \texttt{references/ldt-paper/ld-pasting.tex}, lines 12--50 state the unrestricted result, while lines 52--55 use the inequalities only to reduce the proof to the nontrivial regime. The formal theorem linked from the blueprint has already incorporated the complementary cases through \texttt{Pasting.ldPasting}.
nodes.name: Unrestricted Lean form of induction-section pasting
nodes.label: rem:ld-pasting-induction-unrestricted-lean-form

nodes.statement: The successor step records the slice-wise self-improvement output in \texttt{SelfImprovementData}, and the answer-valued route records the analogous output in \texttt{AnswerSelfImprovementData}. Their constructors call \texttt{selfImprovementInInductionSection}; they no longer carry a separate bundle of Section~\ref{chap:self-improvement} proof-stage data as an input. The \texttt{SliceStrategyTransport} structures are narrow formal interfaces: they assume concrete per-slice symmetric strategies and measurement-transport data, while averaged point-operator compatibility is derived structurally from point-measurement transport. They then convert the remaining data into the ordinary or answer-valued self-improvement output.

nodes.statement: The successor step forms the pasting input by combining the restricted probability estimates with the slice-wise self-improvement data. The Lean construction applies the unrestricted induction-section pasting theorem directly, and the small-error constructor supplies the scalar side conditions \(\gamma\le 1\), \(\zeta\le 1\), and \(d\le q\) internally. Thus the successor proof can call the small-error pasting constructor without carrying \(0<d\), \(1\le k\), \(\gamma\le 1\), \(\zeta\le 1\), or \(d\le q\) as separate proof inputs. The answer-valued small-error assembly then converts the answer-valued slice data to this pasting interface and applies the checked stage-data theorem.

nodes.statement: This is the nontrivial successor branch in the corrected large-\(k\) induction interface. The ordinary successor theorem now reduces to the internal answer-valued induction theorem. That theorem supplies the predecessor induction argument for the restricted slices by a genuine strong induction on the dimension. The answer-valued pasting invocation is recorded in Proposition~\ref{prop:main-induction-successor-answer-valued-pasting}, and the answer-valued self-improvement construction is checked by Proposition~\ref{prop:main-induction-successor-answer-slice-realization}. This is a construction internal to the proof, not an assumption of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-induction}. The recursive slice route applies also when \(d=0\); the successor reduction no longer needs a separate degree-zero family construction.

nodes.statement: In the small-error successor branch, the proof must apply the induction hypothesis in dimension \(m\) to the restricted strategies indexed by \(x\in\mathbb F_q\), with the same integer \(k\). The successor large-\(k\) hypothesis implies the predecessor large-\(k\) side condition in the corrected formal interface, and the nontrivial small-error branch supplies \(k\ge1\). This is the genuine recursive use of the theorem; it is not an additional hypothesis on the successor strategy. The answer-valued restriction map for an answer-valued successor strategy is now explicit in Lean; it preserves the full function-valued diagonal answer on the slice, so it does not use the ordinary low-degree realization that is unavailable for arbitrary answer-valued diagonal measurements. The corresponding restricted-probability theorem for answer-valued successor strategies is also checked: the axis-parallel and diagonal slice averages are derived from the ambient answer-valued goodness assumptions, and the diagonal calculation uses the full function-valued answer rather than an ordinary polynomial-valued realization. Lean now also checks the recursive application itself: after these restricted probabilities are constructed, the predecessor answer-valued induction hypothesis gives the main-induction conclusion for every answer-valued restricted slice. The theorem \texttt{answerMainInduction} now supplies this predecessor hypothesis by strong induction on the dimension. Thus the predecessor induction argument is a checked internal construction, not an additional theorem hypothesis.

nodes.statement: The restricted slice strategy is represented in Lean by an answer-valued strategy. The slice self-improvement data are constructed directly: replace only the diagonal part by an inert ordinary covariant measurement and apply the induction-section self-improvement theorem in the form whose hypotheses are the axis-parallel and point self-consistency estimates. Since the Section~9 conclusion is independent of the diagonal-line error parameter, no low-degree support theorem for the answer-valued diagonal outcomes is needed for this step. Such a support theorem would still be necessary for the stronger route which realizes the answer-valued diagonal measurement as an ordinary polynomial-valued covariant measurement, but that realization is not used here.

The diagonal component of the carrier is a fixed covariant projective measurement; the hypotheses consumed by self-improvement are the axis-parallel and point self-consistency estimates of the answer-valued restricted slice.

nodes.statement: After the recursive answer-valued slice measurements and the slice-wise self-improvement outputs have been averaged, Lean has a polynomial family which is complete, point-consistent with the actual answer-valued point measurement, strongly self-consistent, and bounded by the witnesses obtained from self-improvement. The boundedness input is presently typed through the point-equivalent ordinary carrier, because the existing boundedness interface for pasting is an ordinary-strategy interface. The final induction-section pasting invocation is proved by first deriving the answer-valued Section~10 point-commutativity estimate from the answer-valued diagonal-line verifier relation, then invoking the Section~11 scalar chain in the form which assumes this point-commutativity estimate. The proof does not replace the answer-valued strategy by the ordinary carrier for the diagonal-line test; the carrier is used only for the ordinary boundedness interface. This construction is therefore a Lean-only internal construction for the simultaneous successor proof, not a new hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-induction} and not a replacement for Theorem~\ref{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section}.

nodes.statement:
We may assume $\eps,\delta,\gamma,d/q \le 1$, since otherwise $\nu \ge 1$ and the bound is trivial.

	The proof is by induction on $m$. The base case $m=1$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:main-induction-base}.

	For the step from $m$ to $m+1$, let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ test, and let $k \ge 400(m+1)d$. For each $x \in \F_q$, let $(\psi,A^x,B^x,L^x)$ be the $x$-restricted strategy, with failure parameters $\eps_x,\delta_x,\gamma_x$. Apply the induction hypothesis to each restricted strategy with the same integer $k$ and define
	\[
		\nu_x = 1000k^2m^2\left(\eps_x^{1/1024}+\delta_x^{1/1024}+\gamma_x^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}\right),
		\qquad
		\sigma_x = m^2\left(\nu_x + e^{-k/(80000m^2)}\right).
	\]
	This yields a measurement $G^x \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ such that
	\[
		(A^x)_a^u \ot I \simeq_{\sigma_x} I \ot G_{[g(u)=a]}^x.
	\]

	Next define
	\[
		\zeta_x = 3000m\left(\eps_x^{1/32}+\delta_x^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right).
	\]
	Theorem~\ref{thm:self-improvement-in-induction-section} produces a projective submeasurement $\widehat G^x \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ such that, for each $x$:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item if $\widehat G^x=\sum_g \widehat G_g^x$, then
		      \[
			      \bra{\psi} \widehat G^x \ot I \ket{\psi} \ge (1-\sigma_x)-\zeta_x;
		      \]
		\item on average over $u \sim \F_q^m$,
		      \[
			      (A^x)_a^u \ot I \simeq_{\zeta_x} I \ot \widehat G_{[g(u)=a]}^x;
		      \]
		\item
		      \[
			      \widehat G_g^x \ot I \approx_{\zeta_x} I \ot \widehat G_g^x;
		      \]
		\item there exists a positive semidefinite operator $Z^x$ such that
		      \[
			      \bra{\psi} Z^x \ot (I-\widehat G^x) \ket{\psi} \le \zeta_x
		      \]
		      and for each $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$,
		      \[
			      Z^x \ge \E_u (A^x)_{g(u)}^u.
		      \]
	\end{enumerate}

	We now average the slice-dependent parameters. By concavity of $\alpha \mapsto \alpha^c$ for $c \le 1$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:restricted-probabilities},
	\begin{align*}
		\E_x \nu_x
		 & \le 1000k^2m^2\left((\E_x \eps_x)^{1/1024}+(\E_x \delta_x)^{1/1024}+(\E_x \gamma_x)^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}\right)                          \\
		 & \le 1000k^2m^2\left(\left(\frac{m+1}{m}\eps\right)^{1/1024}+\delta^{1/1024}+\left(\frac{m+1}{m}\gamma\right)^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}\right) \\
		 & \le 1000k^2(m+1)^2\left(\eps^{1/1024}+\delta^{1/1024}+\gamma^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}\right).
	\end{align*}
	Call this final quantity $\nu$. Then, defining
	\[
		\sigma = m^2\left(\nu + e^{-k/(80000m^2)}\right),
	\]
	we have
	\[
		\sigma \ge \E_x \sigma_x.
	\]
	Similarly,
	\begin{align*}
		\E_x \zeta_x
		 & \le 3000m\left((\E_x \eps_x)^{1/32}+(\E_x \delta_x)^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right)         \\
		 & \le 3000m\left(\left(\frac{m+1}{m}\eps\right)^{1/32}+\delta^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right) \\
		 & \le 3000(m+1)\left(\eps^{1/32}+\delta^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right).
	\end{align*}
	Call this last quantity $\zeta$. For later use,
	\begin{align}
		\zeta
		 & = 3000(m+1)\left(\eps^{1/32}+\delta^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right) \notag                              \\
		 & \le 1000k^2(m+1)^2\left(\eps^{1/32}+\delta^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right) \notag                       \\
		 & \le 1000k^2(m+1)^2\left(\eps^{1/1024}+\delta^{1/1024}+\gamma^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}\right) \notag \\
		 & = \nu. \end{align}

	The averaged slice family $\{\widehat G^x\}_{x \in \F_q}$ therefore satisfies the four hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section} with completeness parameter $\kappa=\sigma+\zeta$. To verify the new $\nu$ bound in that theorem, observe that $(3000)^{1/32} \le 2$, so
	\[
		\zeta^{1/32} \le 2(m+1)\left(\eps^{1/1024}+\delta^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}\right),
	\]
	and hence
	\begin{align*}
		 & 100k^2m\left(\eps^{1/32}+\delta^{1/32}+\gamma^{1/32}+\zeta^{1/32}+(d/q)^{1/32}\right)       \\
		 & \le 1000k^2(m+1)^2\left(\eps^{1/1024}+\delta^{1/1024}+\gamma^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}\right) \\
		 & = \nu.
	\end{align*}
	Therefore Theorem~\ref{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section} gives a pasted measurement $H \in \polymeas{m+1}{q}{d}$ such that, on average over $u \sim \F_q^{m+1}$,
	\[
		A_a^u \ot I \simeq_{\sigma^*} I \ot H_{[h(u)=a]},
	\]
	where
	\[
		\sigma^* = (\sigma+\zeta)\left(1+\frac{1}{100m}\right) + 2\nu + e^{-k/(80000m^2)}.
	\]
	It remains to compare $\sigma^*$ with the next-stage target. The pasting
	parameter in Theorem~\ref{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section} is bounded by
	$\nu/5$ in this regime. Using this sharper estimate and
	\eqref{eq:zeta-smaller-than-nu}, we get
	\begin{align*}
		\sigma^*
		 & \le \left(m^2\left(\nu+e^{-k/(80000m^2)}\right)+\nu\right)
		      \left(1+\frac{1}{100m}\right) + \frac{2}{5}\nu
		      + e^{-k/(80000m^2)} \\
		 & = \left((m^2+1)\left(1+\frac{1}{100m}\right)+\frac{2}{5}\right)\nu
		     + \left(m^2\left(1+\frac{1}{100m}\right)+1\right)e^{-k/(80000m^2)}.
	\end{align*}
	For every $m\ge 1$,
	\[
		(m^2+1)\left(1+\frac{1}{100m}\right)+\frac{2}{5}\le (m+1)^2,
		\qquad
		m^2\left(1+\frac{1}{100m}\right)+1\le (m+1)^2.
	\]
	Therefore
	\[
		\sigma^* \le (m+1)^2\left(\nu+e^{-k/(80000m^2)}\right)
		\le (m+1)^2\left(\nu+e^{-k/(80000(m+1)^2)}\right),
	\]
	which is exactly the bound required for dimension $m+1$.

nodes.statement_short: Induction on $m$: restrict to slices, apply the induction hypothesis and self-improvement on each slice, average parameters, then paste. The key step bounds the pasting error $\sigma^*$ by $(m+1)^2(\nu+e^{-k/(80000m^2)})$.

		corrected large-\(k\) theorem \texttt{MainInductionStep.mainInduction} to
		the role-register symmetrization.  The final source-route theorem then
		carries this measurement through the two unsymmetrized point-consistency
		relations, the Step~5 self-consistency calculation, the step making
		measurements projective, completion, and the final point-evaluation
		transport.  These targets are proof-complete for the corrected large-\(k\)
		interface and are not added hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal}.

nodes.statement: Lean now isolates the Step~3 extraction from \texttt{inductive\_step.tex} lines 84--108. In the same-space route, the principal-block map \texttt{extractRoleBlock} turns a role-register POVM \(G\) into the two POVMs \(G^{\mathrm A}\) and \(G^{\mathrm B}\) on the original prover space and proves that point-evaluation postprocessing commutes with this extraction. In the heterogeneous two-space route, the corresponding principal-block maps \texttt{extractRoleRegisterAlice} and \texttt{extractRoleRegisterBob} extract the occupied \((\mathrm A,\mathrm{inl})\) and \((\mathrm B,\mathrm{inr})\) blocks of a measurement on \(\{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}\times(\mathcal H_{\mathrm A}\oplus\mathcal H_{\mathrm B})\). Lean proves the trace-level factor-two identities for arbitrary role-register measurements in \texttt{qBipartiteConsDefect\_roleRegisterProjMeas\_arbitrary\_eq\_average} and its two factor-two consequences. No projectivity of arbitrary principal blocks is claimed, matching the paper's later step making measurements projective.

nodes.statement: Assume $q > 0$, $k \ge 1$, $m \ge 1$, $0 \le \eps \le 1$, and $d \le q$. Fix an incoming error parameter $\nu$. Define \[ \sigma = m^2\left(\nu + e^{-k/(80000m^2)}\right), \qquad \zeta_1 = 2\sigma + 2\sqrt{3\eps+2\sigma} + md/q, \] \[ \zeta_2 = 200\zeta_1^{1/4} + 42\zeta_1^{1/8}, \qquad \zeta_3 = 6\zeta_1 + 6\zeta_2, \qquad \zeta_4 = 2\sigma + 2\sqrt{\zeta_1+\zeta_3/2}. \] The coefficient $42$ is the Lean cascade scalar; it widens the paper's printed coefficient $40$ so that the completion theorem's extra $2\zeta_1$ term is absorbed while preserving the final error envelope.

nodes.statement: The following Lean declarations are bookkeeping infrastructure for the final assembly witness: They split off the vacuous branch where the theorem error is at least $1$, derive the Step~8 scalar hypotheses in the non-vacuous branch, and isolate the role-register Section~6 measurement behind a concrete role-witness record. The role-register measurement is now obtained directly from the \texttt{mainInduction} theorem by \texttt{roleRegisterSymmStrategy\_sourceMainInduction}; the successor case is handled by the checked Section~6 theorem, so it is not a separate boundary hypothesis in Section~3. Lean also records that every non-base parameter choice has a predecessor via \texttt{Parameters.successorDecompositionOfNeOne}, and it retains the explicit transport helpers for the strategy and passing proof across that predecessor equality. The older branch-witness records, which assembled ordinary or answer-valued successor data from recursive slice witnesses and supplied self-improvement inputs, have been removed. The current completion witness carries the concrete role witness obtained from the Section~6 theorem rather than a separate decorative branch witness. Once the role-measurement record is obtained, Lean proves the two factor-two unsymmetrization links from its symmetrized consistency estimate. The subsequent proved lemmas use the proved Section~5 Schwartz--Zippel theorem to convert evaluated pre-projective consistency to full-polynomial consistency at $\zeta_1$, prove the paper line-116 triangle step, and reconstruct the line-156 $\approx_{\zeta_3}$ relation obtained while making measurements projective from pre-projective consistency plus left/right completion closeness at $\zeta_2$. Lean also derives the evaluated line-164 projective consistency. The error-parametric lemmas \texttt{pointAConsistency\_ofLine169Consistency} and \texttt{pointBConsistency\_ofLine169Consistency} show that a polynomial line-169 estimate with error $\eta$ yields the final point error \[ 2\sigma + 2\sqrt{\eta+\zeta_3/2}. \] The active formal route specializes this with the repaired value $\eta=\zeta_1+10\zeta_1^{1/8}$. The existing \texttt{pointAConsistency} and \texttt{pointBConsistency} declarations are the corresponding repaired specializations. After the \#869 right-register completion transport, the remaining active post-role witness asks only for Alice's line-146 completion closeness, Bob's right-register completion closeness, and the two repaired polynomial line-169 links. Lean reconstructs pre-projective full-polynomial consistency from the concrete role witness, uses those repaired line-169 links together with the evaluated line-164 projective consistency, and converts directly to the projective completion witness used by the final assembly. It no longer asks for an arbitrary role-measurement record or an arbitrary Section~6 witness as an independent field. It also no longer asks for stored factor-two role-block estimates, a stored Section~6 consistency input, or a duplicated pre-projective consistency field; those are rebuilt from the concrete role-register measurement and \texttt{hpass}. Lean then applies the projective converse of \texttt{simeq-to-approx} inside the two-space source route. As stated in \texttt{preliminaries.tex}, \texttt{prop:triangle-sub} gives a $\delta+\sqrt{\epsilon}$ loss, so applying it directly to $G^{\mathrm A}\simeq_{\zeta_1}G^{\mathrm B}$ and $G^{\mathrm A}\approx_{\zeta_2}Q^{\mathrm A}$ yields $Q^{\mathrm A}\simeq_{\zeta_1+\sqrt{\zeta_2}}G^{\mathrm B}$, not the printed $\zeta_1$ estimate. The generic corrected route would degrade the final point error to scale $t^{1/65536}$, outside the current \texttt{mainFormalError} envelope. The sharper local pre-completion repair from Remark~\ref{rem:lean-line169-projectivization-match-mass} avoids that widening. Its completion step uses only the formal monotonicity helper \texttt{ProjectivizationMatchMassMonotonicity.completeAtOutcomeProj\_left\_matchMass\_ge}, not a separate exact match-mass witness route. For the corrected boundary assumptions \(k \ge 400md\) and \(k>0\), the source theorem now has a checked proof-level route.
