nodes.statement:
Let \[ (\psi,A^{\mathrm A},B^{\mathrm A},L^{\mathrm A},A^{\mathrm B},B^{\mathrm B},L^{\mathrm B}) \] be a projective strategy passing the $(m,q,d)$ low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Since the three subtests occur with probability $1/3$, this strategy is $(3\eps,3\eps,3\eps)$-good. Introduce a two-dimensional role register on each side and define the symmetrized state \[ \ket{\psi_{\mathrm{sym}}} =  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left( \ket{0}_{\mathrm{A}'}\ket{1}_{\mathrm{B}'}\ket{\psi}_{\mathrm{AB}} + \ket{1}_{\mathrm{A}'}\ket{0}_{\mathrm{B}'}\ket{\psi_{\mathrm{swap}}}_{\mathrm{AB}} ight). \] Define the symmetrized point measurement by \[ (A_{\mathrm{sym}})_a^u = \ket{0} ra{0} \ot A_a^{\mathrm A,u} + \ket{1} ra{1} \ot A_a^{\mathrm B,u}, \] and similarly for $B_{\mathrm{sym}}$ and $L_{\mathrm{sym}}$. This yields a symmetric $(3\eps,3\eps,3\eps)$-good strategy. Set \[ 
u = 10000k^2m^2\left(\eps^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}ight), \qquad \sigma = m^2\left(
u+e^{-k/(80000m^2)}ight). \] Theorem~ef{thm:main-induction} applied to the symmetrized strategy produces a measurement $G=\{G_g\} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ such that  egin{equation} (A_{\mathrm{sym}})_a^u \ot I \simeq_\sigma I \ot G_{[g(u)=a]}, \qquad G_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I \simeq_\sigma I \ot (A_{\mathrm{sym}})_a^u. \end{equation} Now unsymmetrize by defining \[ G_g^{\mathrm A} = ( ra{0} \ot I)\, G_g\, (\ket{0} \ot I), \qquad G_g^{\mathrm B} = ( ra{1} \ot I)\, G_g\, (\ket{1} \ot I). \] These are POVMs on the original prover space. Since $A_{\mathrm{sym}}$ is a convex combination of $(\ket{0} ra{0} \ot I)$ and $(\ket{1} ra{1} \ot I)$ weighted by the test probabilities, the cross-terms $ ra{0} \cdot A_{\mathrm{sym}} \cdot \ket{1}$ vanish. Expanding the consistency of $G$ gives  egin{gather} G_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_{2\sigma} I \ot A_a^{\mathrm B,u}, \ I \ot G_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm B} \simeq_{2\sigma} A_a^{\mathrm A,u} \ot I. \end{gather} Since the original strategy is $(3\eps,3\eps,3\eps)$-good, \[ A_a^{\mathrm A,u} \ot I \simeq_{3\eps} I \ot A_a^{\mathrm B,u}. \] Therefore Lemma~ef{prop:simeq-triangle-inequality} yields \[ G_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_{2\sigma + 2\sqrt{3\eps+2\sigma}} I \ot G_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm B}. \] Expanding this consistency relation and applying Lemma~ef{lem:schwartz-zippel-individual} to replace point evaluations by polynomial evaluations (at cost $md/q$) gives  egin{equation} G_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_{\zeta_1} I \ot G_g^{\mathrm B}, \end{equation} where \[ \zeta_1 = 2\sigma + 2\sqrt{3\eps+2\sigma} +  rac{md}{q}. \] The Lean Step~5 theorem formalizes this expansion/reindexing step and combines it with the proved Schwartz--Zippel tensor bound . The Lean statement is now formulated for a bipartite state on \(H_A\otimes H_B\), so this particular Schwartz--Zippel loss is no longer a same-space restriction in the source-theorem route. Apply Lemma~ef{lem:orthonormalization-main-lemma} to ef{eq:G-self-consistency}. This gives projective submeasurements $P^{\mathrm A},P^{\mathrm B} \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ with \[ G_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I \approx_{100\zeta_1^{1/4}} P_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I, \qquad I \ot G_g^{\mathrm B} \approx_{100\zeta_1^{1/4}} I \ot P_g^{\mathrm B}. \] Completing them by Lemma~ef{prop:completing-to-measurement} yields projective measurements $Q^{\mathrm A},Q^{\mathrm B} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ such that  egin{align} G_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I & \approx_{\zeta_2} Q_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I, \ I \ot G_g^{\mathrm B} & \approx_{\zeta_2} I \ot Q_g^{\mathrm B}, 
otag \end{align} where \[ \zeta_2 = 200\zeta_1^{1/4} + 42\zeta_1^{1/8}. \] The paper prints the coefficient $40$ in this display. The formal Lean cascade uses the widened coefficient $42$ to absorb the literal completion error $2\cdot(100\zeta_1^{1/4})+4\sqrt{100\zeta_1^{1/4}}+2\zeta_1$: under the non-vacuous scalar regime $0 \le \zeta_1 \le 1$, the extra term $2\zeta_1$ is bounded by $2\zeta_1^{1/8}$. By ef{eq:G-self-consistency} and Lemma~ef{prop:simeq-to-approx}, \[ G_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I \approx_{2\zeta_1} I \ot G_g^{\mathrm B}. \] Hence Lemma~ef{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta} gives \[ Q_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I \approx_{\zeta_3} I \ot Q_g^{\mathrm B}, \] where \[ \zeta_3 = 6\zeta_1 + 6\zeta_2. \] Because both measurements are projective, Lemma~ef{prop:simeq-to-approx} converts this to  egin{equation} Q_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_{\zeta_3/2} I \ot Q_g^{\mathrm B}. \end{equation} By data processing,  egin{equation} Q_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_{\zeta_3/2} I \ot Q_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm B}. \end{equation} Next, Lemma~ef{prop:triangle-sub}, applied to ef{eq:G-self-consistency} and ef{eq:G-with-Q-A}, implies \[ Q_g^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_{\zeta_1} I \ot G_g^{\mathrm B}. \] Data processing then gives  egin{equation} Q_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm A} \ot I \simeq_{\zeta_1} I \ot G_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm B}. \end{equation} Applying Lemma~ef{prop:simeq-triangle-inequality} to ef{eq:cons-b}, ef{eq:left-completed-point-with-original-polynomial}, and ef{eq:point-evaluation-data-processing} yields  egin{equation} A_a^{\mathrm A,u} \ot I \simeq_{\zeta_4} I \ot Q_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm B}, \end{equation} where \[ \zeta_4 = 2\sigma + 2\sqrt{\zeta_1+\zeta_3/2}. \] The same argument with the roles reversed gives  egin{equation} I \ot A_a^{\mathrm B,u} \simeq_{\zeta_4} Q_{[g(u)=a]}^{\mathrm A} \ot I. \end{equation} Remark~ef{rem:main-formal-lean-witness-records} records the Lean witness structures that separate the scalar cascade and the Step~5 Schwartz--Zippel handoff from the remaining projective-stage transport work. The scalar side discharges the paper's line~71--73 coarsening and the Step~8 hypotheses in the non-vacuous branch; the Step~5 theorem now turns the evaluated estimate at line~116 into full-polynomial consistency at $\zeta_1$. The remaining Lean witness is the completion-and-line-169 construction: supply the actual role-register measurement, Alice's line-146 completion estimate, Bob's left-register completion estimate, and the two exact polynomial-level $\zeta_1$ links. Lean transports the Bob-side completion estimate to the line-147 right-register form, reconstructs the duplicated Step~6 pre-projective consistency field from these inputs and 	exttt{hpass}, then data-processes the line-169 links to line~172 and derives the two $\zeta_4$ point goals and the $\zeta_3/2$ self-consistency target. With $E$ as in Definition~ef{def:main-formal-envelope}, the quantities $\sigma,\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\zeta_3,\zeta_4$ form the cascade of Definition~ef{def:main-formal-error-cascade}. Theorem~ef{thm:sigma-bound-main-formal} and Theorem~ef{thm:zeta-bounds-main-formal} give the final inflation to the scale $100000k^2m^4 E$. The underlying estimates, with the formal widened $\zeta_2$, are: \[ \sigma \le 10000k^2m^4\left(\eps^{1/1024}+(d/q)^{1/1024}+e^{-k/(80000m^2)}ight). \] Then \[ \zeta_1 \le 20204k^2m^4\left(\eps^{1/2048}+(d/q)^{1/2048}+e^{-k/(160000m^2)}ight), \] and \[ \zeta_2 \le 2568km\left(\eps^{1/16384}+(d/q)^{1/16384}+e^{-k/(1280000m^2)}ight). \] Consequently, \[ \zeta_3 \le 150000k^2m^4\left(\eps^{1/16384}+(d/q)^{1/16384}+e^{-k/(1280000m^2)}ight), \] and \[ \zeta_4 \le 40000k^2m^4\left(\eps^{1/32768}+(d/q)^{1/32768}+e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}ight). \] Both $\zeta_3/2$ and $\zeta_4$ are therefore bounded by \[ 100000k^2m^4\left(\eps^{1/40000}+(d/q)^{1/40000}+e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}ight). \] Hence ef{eq:final-left-point-consistency}, ef{eq:final-right-point-consistency}, and ef{eq:completed-polynomial-consistency} give the three claimed conclusions, with $Q^{\mathrm A}$ and $Q^{\mathrm B}$ renamed as the theorem's $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$.

nodes.name: Case $a=0$: average is 1
nodes.statement: If $a=0$, then $\tr[\bx\cdot a]=0$ for every $\bx$, so the average is $1$.

nodes.name: Case $a\ne0$: pick $y$ with nonzero trace and name the average $C$
nodes.statement:
If $a\neq 0$, choose $y \in \F_q$ such that $\tr[a\cdot y]\neq 0$, and set
	\[
		C=\E_{\bx \sim \F_q} \omega^{\tr[\bx \cdot a]}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Case $a\ne0$: pick $y$ with nonzero trace and name the average $C$.

nodes.name: Translation invariance gives $C=C\omega^{\tr[ya]}$
nodes.statement:
Translation invariance of the uniform distribution gives
	\[
		C=\E_{\bx \sim \F_q} \omega^{\tr[(\bx+y)\cdot a]}
		= C \cdot \omega^{\tr[y\cdot a]}.
	\]

nodes.name: Conclude $C=0$
nodes.statement: Since $\omega^{\tr[y\cdot a]}\neq 1$, it follows that $C=0$.

nodes.name: Write the difference as one expectation
nodes.statement:
To prove \eqref{eq:closeness3}, write the difference as
	\[
		\E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Big(\sum_b C^\bx_{a,b}\Big) (A^\bx_a-B^\bx_a) \ket{\psi}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Write the difference as one expectation.

nodes.name: Cauchy--Schwarz with the two hypotheses bounds it by $\sqrt\gamma$
nodes.statement:
Cauchy--Schwarz bounds its magnitude by
	\[
		\Big( \E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Big(\sum_b C^{\bx}_{a,b}\Big)\Big(\sum_b C^{\bx}_{a,b}\Big)^\dagger \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2}
		\Big( \E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\bx}_a - B^{\bx}_a)^\dagger (A^{\bx}_a - B^{\bx}_a) \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2},
	\]
	and the two hypotheses bound these factors by $1$ and $\sqrt{\gamma}$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy--Schwarz with the two hypotheses bounds it by $\sqrt\gamma$.

nodes.name: Adjoint version follows from the first
nodes.statement:
For \eqref{eq:closeness4}, rewrite the difference as
	\[
		\E_{\bx} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} (C^{\bx}_{a,b})^\dagger \big((A^{\bx}_a)^\dagger-(B^{\bx}_a)^\dagger\big) \ket{\psi},
	\]
	and apply \eqref{eq:closeness3} to the adjoint families.
nodes.statement_short: Adjoint version follows from the first.

nodes.name: Express the difference
nodes.statement:
The difference has magnitude
	\[
		\Big| \E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\bx}_a - B^{\bx}_a) C^{\bx}_a \ket{\psi}\Big|.
	\]

nodes.name: Cauchy--Schwarz split
nodes.statement:
By Cauchy--Schwarz this is at most
	\[
		\Big(\E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\bx}_a - B^{\bx}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}\Big)^{1/2}
		\Big(\E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (C^{\bx}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}\Big)^{1/2}.
	\]

nodes.name: Bound each factor
nodes.statement: The first factor is at most $\sqrt{\delta}$ by hypothesis, and the second is at most $1$ because $C$ is a submeasurement.

nodes.name: First approximation bounded by inconsistency
nodes.statement:
For the first approximation in \eqref{eq:closeness5}, bound
	\[
		\E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \bigl(A^{\bx}_a \ot (I-B^{\bx}_a)\bigr)^2 \ket{\psi}
	\]
	by the inconsistency between $A$ and $B$.

nodes.name: Second approximation similarly
nodes.statement:
The second approximation is identical, applied to
	\[
		\E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \bigl((A^\bx-A^\bx_a)\ot B^\bx_a\bigr)^2 \ket{\psi}.
	\]

nodes.name: Compose by triangle inequality
nodes.statement: Then compose the two bounds with Lemma~\ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}.

nodes.name: Plan: two steps
nodes.statement: We prove the first approximation in \eqref{eq:switch-sandwich} in two steps.

nodes.name: Move the right copy across by Cauchy--Schwarz
nodes.statement_short: Move the right copy across by Cauchy--Schwarz.

nodes.name: Move the left copy; projectivity collapses the sandwich
nodes.statement: For the second step, move the remaining left copy of $A^\bx_a$ across the bipartition in the same way; projectivity then collapses the sandwich and yields the first approximation in \eqref{eq:switch-sandwich}.
nodes.statement_short: Move the left copy; projectivity collapses the sandwich.

nodes.name: Second approximation by the same argument
nodes.statement: The second approximation in \eqref{eq:switch-sandwich} is the same argument with the rightmost factor $A_a^\bx$ omitted.
nodes.statement_short: Second approximation by the same argument.

nodes.name: Expand the squared norm
Bound by $2\delta$
nodes.statement: The strong self-consistency bound controls the last line by $2\delta$.

nodes.name: Projective case gives equality, hence converse
nodes.statement: If $A$ is projective, then \eqref{eq:here's-where-projectivity-would-help} is an equality, which gives the converse.
nodes.statement_short: Projective case gives equality, hence converse.

nodes.name: State the intermediate cross-side bound
Expand the squared norm
Bound first and third terms
nodes.statement: Proposition~\ref{prop:completeness-transfer-projective-P} bounds the first term by $\bra{\psi} A \ot I \ket{\psi}+2\sqrt{\eps}$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:easy-approx-from-approx-delta} together with strong self-consistency bounds the third term below by $\bra{\psi} A \ot I \ket{\psi}-\delta-\sqrt{\eps}$.

nodes.name: Substitute to get the intermediate bound
nodes.statement: Substituting into \eqref{eq:gonna-handle-third-term} yields \eqref{eq:what-we-want-to-prove-but-on-wrong-side}.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute to get the intermediate bound.

nodes.name: Combine with post-processed self-consistency by triangle inequality
nodes.statement:
Now combine \eqref{eq:what-we-want-to-prove-but-on-wrong-side} with
	\[
		A^x_{[f(a)=b]} \ot I \approx_{2\delta} I \ot A^x_{[f(a)=b]}
	\]
	from Lemma~\ref{prop:two-notions-of-self-consistency-after-evaluation}, and conclude by Lemma~\ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with post-processed self-consistency by triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Squared triangle inequality reduces to the residual
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-vectors-squared},
	\[
		\sum_a \lVert(A_a-C_a)\ot I \ket{\psi} \rVert^2
		\leq 2\delta + 2 \cdot \lVert(I-B)\ot I \ket{\psi}\rVert^2.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Squared triangle inequality reduces to the residual.

nodes.name: Reduce to bounding the residual
nodes.statement: It remains to bound the residual term.

nodes.name: Residual at most $1-\sum B_a^2$
Replace $B^2$ by $AB$ then $A^2$
Same-side square lemma lower-bounds $\sum A_a^2$
nodes.statement:
Proposition~\ref{prop:cool-prop} gives
	\[
		\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a^2\ot I \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} A \ot I \ket{\psi} - \zeta = 1-\zeta.
	\]

nodes.name: Residual $\le 2\sqrt\delta+\zeta$
nodes.statement:
Hence \eqref{eq:to-return-later-whatevs} implies
	\[
		\lVert(I-B) \ot I \ket{\psi}\rVert^2 \le 2\sqrt\delta + \zeta.
	\]

nodes.name: Substitute to conclude
nodes.statement: Substituting this into the first bound proves the claim.

nodes.name: Dilate each question's measurement with the helper lemma
nodes.statement:
For each question $x$, choose a local auxiliary state
	$\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm A,x}}$ of dimension one larger than the number of
	outcomes of $A^x$, and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper} to obtain a
	projective sub-measurement $\widetilde A^x$. Do the same for each question $y$
	on Bob's side, obtaining auxiliary states $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm B,y}}$
	and projective sub-measurements $\widetilde B^y$.
nodes.statement_short: Dilate each question's measurement with the helper lemma.

nodes.name: Define the product auxiliary state and dilated operators
nodes.statement:
Let
	\[
		\ket{\mathsf{aux}}
		=
		\Big(\bigotimes_x \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm A,x}}\Big)
		\ot
		\Big(\bigotimes_y \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm B,y}}\Big),
		\qquad
		\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}},
	\]
	and let $\widehat A^x_a$ and $\widehat B^y_b$ be obtained by letting
	$\widetilde A^x_a$ or $\widetilde B^y_b$ act on the relevant auxiliary factor
	and the identity act on every other auxiliary factor.
nodes.statement_short: Define the product auxiliary state and dilated operators.

nodes.name: Correlations reduce to the helper's compression identity
nodes.statement:
Because the auxiliary
	state is a product state and the two dilations act on disjoint tensor factors,
	the correlation for fixed $(x,y)$ reduces to the compression identity from
	Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper} on the $x$- and $y$-registers.
nodes.statement_short: Correlations reduce to the helper's compression identity.

nodes.name: Conclude correlation preservation
nodes.statement:
Hence
	\[
		\bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat A^x_a \ot \widehat B^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}
		=
		\bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}.
	\]

nodes.name: Fix a basis and a dilating unitary $U$
nodes.statement:
Consider an orthonormal basis for $\C^{k+1}$ consisting of vectors $\ket{a}$ for $a \in \mathcal A$ and the vector $\ket{\bot}$. Let $U$ be any unitary such that for each vector $\ket{\phi}$,
	\[
		U \cdot (\ket{\phi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
		=
		\sum_{a \in \mathcal A} ((A_a)^{1/2}\ket{\phi}) \ot \ket{a}
		+
		((I-A)^{1/2}\ket{\phi}) \ot \ket{\bot},
	\]
	where $A=\sum_a A_a$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a basis and a dilating unitary $U$.

nodes.name: Compute $U(I\otimes|aux\rangle)$ and its components
nodes.statement:
Then
	\[
		U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
		=
		\sum_{a \in \mathcal A} (A_a)^{1/2} \ot \ket{a}
		+
		(I-A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot},
	\]
	so for any $a \in \mathcal A$,
	\[
		(I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
		=
		(A_a)^{1/2}.
	\]

nodes.name: Define $\widehat A_a$ and verify projectivity and compression
nodes.statement:
Define
	\[
		\widehat{A}_a = U^\dagger \cdot (I \ot \ket{a}\bra{a}) \cdot U.
	\]
	Each $\widehat{A}_a$ is a projector, and
	\begin{align*}
		(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}}) \cdot \widehat{A}_a \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
		 & =
		(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}}) \cdot U^\dagger \cdot (I \ot \ket{a}) \cdot (I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) \\
		 & =
		(A_a)^{1/2} \cdot (A_a)^{1/2}
		=
		A_a.
	\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $\widehat A_a$ and verify projectivity and compression.

nodes.name: Self-consistency defect equals consistency defect with itself
nodes.statement:
Since \(A\) is complete, the self-consistency defect is the consistency
	defect of \(A\) with itself.
nodes.statement_short: Self-consistency defect equals consistency defect with itself.

nodes.name: Apply the consistency corollary with $B=A$
nodes.statement:
The proof therefore applies the consistency
	corollary with \(B=A\).

nodes.name: No extra witnesses assumed
nodes.statement:
No spectral-truncation witness or repair witness is
	assumed at this interface.

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency bounds $\langle A\otimes(I-A)\rangle$
nodes.statement:
Write \(A=\sum_a A_a\).  The strong self-consistency assumption implies
	\[
		\bra{\psi} A \ot A \ket{\psi}
		\geq
		\bra{\psi} A \ot I \ket{\psi} - \zeta,
	\]
	so
	\[
		\bra{\psi} A \ot (I-A) \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta.
	\]

nodes.name: Same inequality for $I-A$
nodes.statement:
Rearranging once more gives
	\[
		\bra{\psi} (I-A) \ot (I-A) \ket{\psi}
		\geq
		\bra{\psi} (I-A) \ot I \ket{\psi} - \zeta.
	\]

nodes.name: Complete $A$ with outcome $\bot$
nodes.statement:
Complete \(A\) to the measurement
	\(\widehat A=\{\widehat A_a\}_{a \in \widehat{\mathcal A}}\) on
	\(\widehat{\mathcal A}=\mathcal A \cup \{\bot\}\) by setting
	\(\widehat A_a=A_a\) for \(a \in \mathcal A\) and
	\(\widehat A_{\bot}=I-A\).

nodes.name: Completion is $2\zeta$-strongly self-consistent
nodes.statement:
Adding the two preceding inequalities shows
	that \(\widehat A\) is \(2\zeta\)-strongly self-consistent.

nodes.name: Get the almost-projective estimate $4\zeta$
nodes.statement:
By
	\ref{prop:other-two-notions-of-self-consistency}, this gives the source
	almost-projective estimate
	\[
		\sum_a \bra{\psi}
		\bigl((\widehat A_a\ot I)-(\widehat A_a\ot I)^2\bigr)
		\ket{\psi}
		\le 4\zeta.
	\]

nodes.name: Projectivize the completion
nodes.statement:
Apply \ref{lem:locality-preserving-projectivization} to obtain a projective
	sub-measurement \(\widehat P\) such that
	\[
		\widehat A_a \ot I \approx_{84(4\zeta)^{1/4}} \widehat P_a \ot I.
	\]

nodes.name: Drop $\bot$
nodes.statement:
Discard the extra outcome and set \(P_a=\widehat P_a\) for
	\(a \in \mathcal A\).

nodes.name: Constant $84\cdot4^{1/4}\le120$
nodes.statement:
Then
	\[
		A_a \ot I \approx_{84(4\zeta)^{1/4}} P_a \ot I,
	\]
	and \(84 \cdot 4^{1/4} \leq 120\), so the completion-route bound follows.

nodes.name: WLOG $\zeta\le1/4$
Consistency gives overlap $\ge1-\zeta$
nodes.statement:
By \ref{prop:simeq-for-measurements},
	\[
		\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \ot B_a \ket{\psi} \geq 1-\zeta.
	\]

nodes.name: Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\sum A_a^2\ge1-2\zeta$
nodes.statement:
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to
	\[
		\sum_a \bra{\psi} (A_a \ot I)\cdot(I \ot B_a)\ket{\psi}
	\]
	to obtain
	\[
		\sum_a \bra{\psi} (A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\zeta)^2 \geq 1-2\zeta.
	\]

nodes.name: Almost-projectivity of $A$
Inner lemmas: truncation, rounding, averaging, rank reduction
nodes.statement:
\begin{lemma} For any $x \in [0, 1]$,
		\begin{equation*}
			(x - \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2 \leq \frac{1}{\delta} \cdot (x - x^2).
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		If $x \geq 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$. Since $\delta \leq 1/2$ below, one also has $x \geq \delta$, so
		\[
			(x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2
			=
			(1-x)^2
			\leq
			(1-x)\frac{x}{\delta}
			=
			\frac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2).
		\]
		If $x < 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=0$, and similarly
		\[
			(x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2
			=
			x^2
			\leq
			x\frac{1-x}{\delta}
			=
			\frac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2).
		\]
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[Rounding to projectors] There exists a set of projective matrices $\{R_a\}$ such that
		\begin{equation*}
			A_a \ot I \approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta}} R_a \ot I.
		\end{equation*}
		and
		\begin{equation*}
			R:= \sum_a R_a \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \cdot I.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		Write the eigendecomposition of $A_a$ as
		\[
			A_a = \sum_i \lambda_{a,i}\ket{u_{a,i}}\bra{u_{a,i}}.
		\]
		Choose
		\begin{equation} 0 < \delta \leq 1/2,
		\end{equation}
		define $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta:[0,1] \to \{0,1\}$ by $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$ when $x \geq 1-\delta$ and $0$ otherwise, and set
		\[
			R_a = \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(A_a)
			=
			\sum_i \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(\lambda_{a,i}) \ket{u_{a,i}}\bra{u_{a,i}}.
		\]
		By \ref{lem:trunc-inequality},
		\[
			(A_a-R_a)^2
			\leq
			\frac{1}{\delta}(A_a-(A_a)^2).
		\]
		Summing expectations and using \ref{eq:A-looks-projective} gives
		\[
			\sum_a \Vert (A_a-R_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2
			\leq
			\frac{2\zeta}{\delta},
		\]
		so $A_a \ot I \approx_{2\zeta/\delta} R_a \ot I$.

		For every $x \in [0,1]$, one has $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x) \leq x/(1-\delta)$, hence
		\[
			R_a \leq \frac{1}{1-\delta} A_a.
		\]
		Summing over $a$ and using that $A$ is a measurement,
		\[
			R = \sum_a R_a \leq \frac{1}{1-\delta} I \leq (1+2\delta)I,
		\]
		where the last estimate uses $\delta \leq 1/2$. Setting $\delta=\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives the claim, and \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta} ensures $\delta \leq 1/2$.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{remark}[Lean auxiliary declarations for rounding to projectors] The source-facing Lean declarations for
		Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-non-measurement} are the proposition
		\texttt{projectiveNonMeasurement} and the construction theorem
		\texttt{projectiveNonMeasurement\_of\_sourceAlmostProjective\_full}.
		The declarations listed here are the endpoint and regime splits, the
		\texttt{AlmostProjMeasStatement} witness forms, and the spectral-truncation
		statement conversions used by later Section~5 arguments.  They are not additional
		hypotheses in the paper statement of
		Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-non-measurement}.
	\end{remark}

	\begin{lemma}[Combinatorial averaging for the $r > d$ branch] Let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function on a finite index set $\alpha$ with
		$|\alpha| = r$, and let $L \subseteq \alpha$ with $|L| = d$ and $d < r$. Write
		$S = L^\complement$ and assume $f(s) \leq f(l)$ for every $s \in S$ and $l \in L$.
		Then the pairwise double-counting inequality
		\[
			|L|\, \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\, \sum_{l \in L} f(l)
		\]
		holds, and hence also
		\[
			r\, \sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\, \sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x).
		\]
		If in addition $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})\,d$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq
		1 + 2\sqrt{\zeta}$, and $0 \leq \zeta \leq 1/4$, then
		\[
			\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}.
		\]
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		Choose $L$ to be a set of $d$ indices on which the sum of $f$ is maximal. If some $s \in S$ and $l \in L$ satisfied $f(l) < f(s)$, replacing $l$ by $s$ would increase this sum, so every small index is bounded by every large index. Summing the inequalities $f(s) \leq f(l)$ over all pairs $(s,l) \in S \times L$ gives
		\[
			|L|\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{l \in L} f(l).
		\]
		Since $\alpha$ is the disjoint union of $L$ and $S$, adding $|S|\sum_{s \in S} f(s)$ to both sides yields
		\[
			r\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x).
		\]
		The hypotheses $|L|=d$ and $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d$ imply $|S|/r \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Dividing by $r$ and using $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives
		\[
			\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}).
		\]
		Finally, $\zeta \leq 1/4$ implies $\sqrt{\zeta} \leq 1/2$, and hence $2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}$.
	\end{proof}


	\begin{lemma}[Rank reduction] There exists a set of projection matrices $\{Q_a\}$ such that
		\begin{equation*}
			A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I.
		\end{equation*}
		and
		\begin{equation*}
			Q:= \sum_a Q_a \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \cdot I.
		\end{equation*}
		Furthermore,
		\begin{equation*}
			\sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a) \leq d.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		
		
		
		
		Let $\{R_a\}$ be given by \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement}. Write $r_a=\mathrm{rank}(R_a)$ and $r=\sum_a r_a$. If $r \leq d$, take $Q_a=R_a$. Otherwise,
		\begin{equation} r
			=
			\sum_a r_a
			=
			\sum_a \Tr(R_a)
			=
			\Tr(R)
			\leq
			(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d.
		\end{equation}
		Let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,r_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $R_a$, so
		\[
			R_a = \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\]
		Define the overlaps
		\[
			o_{a,i} = \bra{\psi} (\ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}} \ot I)\ket{\psi}.
		\]
		Their total satisfies
		\begin{equation} \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} o_{a,i}
			=
			\bra{\psi} R \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\leq
			1+2\sqrt{\zeta}.
		\end{equation}
		Let $\mathsf{Large}$ be the set of the $d$ largest overlaps $o_{a,i}$, breaking ties arbitrarily, and let $\mathsf{Small}$ be the complement. Then
		\begin{equation} |\mathsf{Small}|
			=
			r-d
			\leq
			2\sqrt{\zeta}\,d
			\leq
			2\sqrt{\zeta}\,r,
		\end{equation}
		by \ref{eq:bound-on-r}. Averaging the overlaps over the $r$ indices gives
		\begin{equation} \sum_{(a,i)\in \mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i}
			\leq
			\frac{|\mathsf{Small}|}{r}\sum_{a,i} o_{a,i}
			\leq
			4\sqrt{\zeta},
		\end{equation}
		using \ref{eq:size-of-small-is-small}, \ref{eq:total-overlap}, and \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta}.

		For each $a$, let $\mathsf{Large}_a=\{i : (a,i)\in \mathsf{Large}\}$ and define
		\[
			Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Large}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\]
		Then $\sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a)=|\mathsf{Large}| \leq d$, and $Q_a \leq R_a$ for every $a$, so
		\[
			Q = \sum_a Q_a \leq \sum_a R_a = R \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I.
		\]
		Also,
		\[
			R_a-Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Small}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}
		\]
		is a projector, hence
		\[
			\sum_a \Vert (R_a-Q_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2
			=
			\sum_{(a,i)\in\mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i}
			\leq
			4\sqrt{\zeta}
		\]
		by \ref{eq:small-overlaps}. Therefore $R_a \ot I \approx_{4\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I$. Combining this with \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement} and the triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ gives
		\[
			A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I.
		\]
	\end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Inner lemmas: truncation, rounding, averaging, rank reduction.

nodes.name: Fix $Q$ from rank reduction
nodes.statement: Henceforth let $Q=\{Q_a\}$ be the family given by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}.

nodes.name: Inner lemmas: completeness, $Q/X/\widehat X/P$ algebra, $P\approx Q$
nodes.statement:
\begin{lemma}[Completeness of~$Q$] \begin{equation*}
			\bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\geq
			1 - 11 \zeta^{1/4}.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		Since each $Q_a$ is projective,
		\begin{equation} \bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\approx_{5\zeta^{1/4}}
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}.
		\end{equation}
		By Cauchy--Schwarz,
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}
			\quad\text{and}\quad
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 12\sqrt{\zeta}
		\]
		from \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}.
		A second Cauchy--Schwarz estimate yields
		\begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a \cdot A_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}
			\approx_{4\zeta^{1/4}}
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}.
		\end{equation}
		Combining \ref{eq:Q-for-an-A} and \ref{eq:another-Q-for-A} with \ref{eq:A-looks-projective} gives
		\[
			\bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\geq
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \ot I \ket{\psi} - 2\zeta - 9\zeta^{1/4}
			=
			1 - 11\zeta^{1/4},
		\]
		since $\zeta \leq \zeta^{1/4}$ under \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta}.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[Completeness of~$\sqrt{Q}$] \begin{equation*}
			\bra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\geq
			1 - 12 \zeta^{1/4}.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		Diagonalize $Q=\sum_i \nu_i \ket{u_i}\bra{u_i}$. Because $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, each $\nu_i$ is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Therefore
		\[
			\sqrt{Q}
			=
			\sum_i \sqrt{\nu_i}\ket{u_i}\bra{u_i}
			\geq
			\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} Q.
		\]
		The scalar estimate
		\[
			\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} \geq 1-\sqrt{\zeta}
		\]
		gives $\sqrt{Q} \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})Q$. Hence \ref{lem:Q-completeness} implies
		\[
			\bra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\geq
			(1-\sqrt{\zeta})(1-11\zeta^{1/4})
			\geq
			1-12\zeta^{1/4}.
		\]
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[$Q$ is almost projective] \begin{equation*}
			\sum_a (Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta} \cdot I.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		Since $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum},
		\begin{align*}
			\sum_a Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a
			 & \leq
			(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \sum_a Q_a \cdot I \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a \\
			 & =
			(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})Q - Q                                      \\
			 & =
			2\sqrt{\zeta}\,Q                                            \\
			 & \leq
			2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I                             \\
			 & \leq
			4\sqrt{\zeta}\,I,
		\end{align*}
		using \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta} in the last step.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{definition}[Matrix decomposition of~$Q_a$] For each $a$, let
		\[
			m_a = \mathrm{rank}(Q_a),
		\]
		and let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,m_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $Q_a$, so that
		\[
			Q_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\]
		Let
		\[
			m = \sum_a m_a,
		\]
		and let $\{\ket{a,i}\}$ be an orthonormal basis of $\C^m$, indexed by all $a$ and all
		$1 \leq i \leq m_a$. For each $a$, define
		\[
			X_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{v_{a,i}},
			\qquad
			T_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{a,i},
		\]
		and define
		\begin{equation} X = \sum_a X_a = \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\end{equation}
		Let $T = \{T_a\}$. Then $T$ is a projective measurement on $\C^m$.
	\end{definition}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		
		Choose an orthonormal basis of the range of each projector \(Q_a\).
		The rank-one expansion gives the displayed decomposition, and the
		orthogonality of the labelled basis vectors makes the family \(T\)
		a projective measurement.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{definition}[SVD of~$X$] The paper presents this step by choosing a singular value decomposition
		\[
			X = U \cdot \Sigma_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger.
		\]
		The formalization has two closely related auxiliary declarations.  The reduced
		datum records the downstream consequences of the choice: the matrices $X$
		and $\widehat X$, the identities $X^\dagger X=Q$,
		$\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$, and $X^\dagger\widehat X=\sqrt Q$,
		together with the $Q_a=X^\dagger T_aX$ restatement.  The rectangular-SVD
		lemmas take explicit matrices $U,V,\Sigma,I_{m\times d}$ and derive the
		two stored $\widehat X$ identities from the matrix calculation below.
	\end{definition}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		
		Apply the finite-dimensional singular value decomposition to \(X\) and
		record exactly the consequences used later: the identities for
		\(X^\dagger X\), \(\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger\),
		\(X^\dagger\widehat X\), and the restatement of the \(Q_a\)'s.  The
		unitary-group constructors are the same rectangular-SVD calculation, with
		the square factors taken as elements of the relevant unitary groups
		rather than as matrices accompanied by separate unitarity equations.  In
		the sigma-range specialization, the auxiliary row space is the lifted
		finite-enumeration carrier associated to the ranks of the \(Q_a\)'s, which
		is definitionally the carrier of the canonical sigma-range \(Q\)-layer.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{remark}[Formalization support for orthogonal projector families] If the family $\{Q_a\}$ were a projective measurement, then the vectors
		$\ket{v_{a,i}}$, over all $a$ and all $1 \leq i \leq m_a$, would be orthonormal.
		Then \eqref{eq:looks-like-singular-value-decomposition} would already be a singular value
		decomposition of $X$, with $\Sigma = I_{m \times d}$. Equivalently,
		\[
			X = U \cdot I_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger.
		\]
		This motivates replacing $\Sigma$ by $I$ in the definition of $\widehat X$ and $P$.
	\end{remark}

	\begin{definition}[Definition of~$P$] The paper defines
		\[
			\widehat{X} = U \cdot I_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger.
		\]
		We take $\widehat X$ to be the reduced matrix supplied by the stored datum.
		For each $a$, define
		\[
			\widehat{X}_a = T_a \cdot \widehat{X},
			\qquad
			P_a = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a.
		\]
	\end{definition}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		
		The definition is the formal \(Q/X/\widehat X/P\) construction: once
		\(\widehat X\) is chosen from the stored singular-value data, each
		\(P_a\) is defined as the positive operator
		\(\widehat X_a^\dagger\widehat X_a\).
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma} For each $a$,
		\[
			X_a = T_a \cdot X.
		\]
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		Multiply the definition of $X$ by $T_a$ on the left and use that $T_a$ selects exactly the basis vectors $\ket{a,i}$:
		\[
			T_a \cdot X
			=
			\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{a,i}\Big)
			\Big(\sum_b \sum_{j=1}^{m_b} \ket{b,j}\bra{v_{b,j}}\Big)
			=
			\sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \ket{a,i}\bra{v_{a,i}}
			=
			X_a.
		\]
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[$Q_a$ restated] For each $a$,
		\begin{equation*}
			Q_a = X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a = X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = X_a^\dagger \cdot X.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		The identity $X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$ follows by expanding the basis sums. The remaining equalities come from \ref{lem:xa-t} and the projectivity of $T$:
		\[
			X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a
			=
			(X^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot X)
			=
			X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X
			=
			X_a^\dagger \cdot X.
		\]
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[$X$ squared] \begin{equation*}
			X^\dagger \cdot X = Q.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		Use that $T$ is a measurement and then \ref{lem:qa-restated}:
		\[
			X^\dagger \cdot X
			=
			\sum_a X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X
			=
			\sum_a Q_a
			=
			Q.
		\]
		The additional paper identities involving $U,V,\Sigma$ are the usual SVD
		computations.  The Lean development also records the spectral calculation
		which will identify the mixed positive-Gram-image product with
		$\sqrt Q$: the positive eigenvalues give the nonzero columns, while the
		zero eigenspace has zero coefficient in the square-root expansion and is
		killed by $X$.  The conjugate right-eigenvector rows over the positive
		spectrum are also orthonormal.  Equivalently, any row-space vector
		orthogonal to the positive Gram images is killed by $X^\dagger$.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma} For each $a$,
		\begin{equation*}
			X_a^\dagger \cdot (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2 \cdot X_a
			=
			Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		Expand the square and apply \ref{lem:X-squared} and \ref{lem:qa-restated} term by term:
		\[
			X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a
			=
			Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a,
		\]
		while
		\[
			X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a
			=
			(X_a^\dagger \cdot X)(X^\dagger \cdot X_a)
			=
			Q_a \cdot Q_a
			=
			Q_a,
		\]
		and $X_a^\dagger I_{m \times m} X_a = X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$. Substituting these identities into
		\[
			(X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2
			=
			X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger - 2X \cdot X^\dagger + I_{m \times m}
		\]
		gives the claim.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[$P_a$ restated] For each $a$,
		\begin{equation*}
			P_a = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		Since $T$ is projective,
		\[
			P_a
			=
			\widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a
			=
			(\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot \widehat{X})
			=
			\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X}
			=
			\widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}.
		\]
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[$\widehat{X}$ squared] \begin{equation*}
			\widehat{X} \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger = I_{m \times m}.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		The paper proves this by multiplying out
		$\widehat{X}=U\cdot I_{m\times d}\cdot V^\dagger$ and using the unitarity of
		$U$ and $V$.  In Lean, the dimension hypothesis $m\leq d$ already gives a
		rectangular matrix with orthonormal rows on the sigma auxiliary space; the
		chosen matrix \texttt{sigmaFinXHatCoisometry} and its specification record this
		existence result as a hypothesis for the future construction.  The formal lemma
		\texttt{orthonormal\_normalized\_image\_of\_adjoint\_comp\_eigenvectors}
		records the singular-vector normalization calculation, while
		\texttt{normalized\_matrix\_image\_rows\_mul\_conjTranspose} combines the
		corresponding row-coisometry identity, and
		\texttt{positive\_gram\_spectrum\_image\_rows\_transpose\_mixed} records the
		adjoint action $X^\dagger(\lambda^{-1/2}Xv)=\lambda^{1/2}v$ on the positive
		spectral part of the Gram operator.  The formal lemma
		\texttt{exists\_unitaryGroup\_with\_positive\_gram\_spectrum\_rows} records the
		next finite-dimensional step: after choosing distinct row positions for the
		positive spectrum, these normalized image rows extend to a square unitary
		group element on the row space.  The companion lemma
		\texttt{exists\_rectangular\_coisometry\_extending\_orthonormal\_rows}
		records the analogous rectangular completion for prescribed right rows
		when the dimension bound permits it.  The formal lemma
		\texttt{unitaryGroup\_mul\_rectangular\_coisometry} and its right-multiplication
		companion
		\texttt{rectangular\_coisometry\_mul\_conjTranspose\_unitaryGroup} record the
		two unitary-preservation steps in the paper's multiplication.  The formal
		lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_coisometry\_unitaryGroup} applies these
		preservation steps to the rectangular-SVD expression.  The
		unconditional positive-Gram route is
		\texttt{exists\_xHat\_of\_sigmaFinRangeEmbedding\_positiveGram}, which
		constructs $\widehat X$ from the rank-reduction witness and proves
		$\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$ together with the mixed square-root
		identity below.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[$X$ times $\widehat{X}$] \begin{equation*}
			X \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger =
			U \cdot \Sigma_{m \times m} \cdot U^\dagger,
			\quad
			X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} = \sqrt{Q}.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		The paper obtains this from the SVD formula for $X$ and the definition of
		$\widehat X$.  In Lean, the unconditional QXP data first proves that
		$X\widehat X^\dagger$ is Hermitian and positive.  The formal lemma
		\texttt{x\_mul\_xHat\_adjoint\_spectral\_theorem} then applies Mathlib's
		spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, giving the displayed
		$U\Sigma U^\dagger$ form with the Mathlib eigenvector unitary and the
		diagonal matrix of real eigenvalues.  The auxiliary lemma
		\texttt{rectangularSvd\_x\_mul\_xHat\_conjTranspose\_raw} records the same
		calculation under explicit rectangular-SVD data, where the middle factor
		\(S I_{m\times d}^\dagger\) is the formal square matrix
		\(\Sigma_{m\times m}\).  The formal lemma
		\texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_mixed\_of\_sqrtQ\_unitaryGroup} records the
		second matrix calculation in the form whose square-root target is the
		operator $Q$ supplied by the QXP construction.  The formal lemma
		\texttt{rectangularSvd\_middle\_eq\_sqrt\_of\_square} records the spectral
		step: a positive middle factor whose square is $Q$ is the positive square
		root of $Q$.  The reduced datum then records this mixed-product
		identity as a primitive consequence, which is exactly the part needed in
		\ref{lem:squared-difference} and \ref{lem:P-Q-approx}.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{remark}[Lean status for the QXP algebra] The Lean declarations linked in Lemmas~\ref{lem:X-squared},
		\ref{lem:X-hat-squared}, and~\ref{lem:X-times-X-hat} expose the
		corresponding matrix identities as construction theorems.  These
		declarations prove the identities from the \(Q\)-layer, the sigma-range
		realization, and the positive-Gram spectral construction, with the
		rectangular-SVD calculation retained as an auxiliary comparison.  Thus the
		local \(X/\widehat X/P\) algebra is formalized; the remaining chapter-level
		work is to compose this construction with the preceding orthonormalization
		step from the paper hypotheses.
	\end{remark}

	\begin{lemma}[Squared difference] \begin{equation*}
			(X - \widehat{X}) \cdot (X - \widehat{X})^\dagger \leq (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		The paper diagonalizes the positive operator $X\widehat X^\dagger$ using the
		SVD notation.  The formal proof avoids storing that SVD explicitly: set
		$Y=X\widehat X^\dagger$.  The primitive identities imply that $Y$ is
		hermitian, nonnegative, and satisfies $Y^2=XX^\dagger$.  Hence
		$(X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger=(Y-I)^2$, and positivity of $Y$ gives
		$(Y-I)^2\leq(Y^2-I)^2=(XX^\dagger-I)^2$.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[Projectivity of~$P$] $P = \{P_a\}$ forms a projective sub-measurement.
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		For outcomes $a,b$,
		\begin{align*}
			P_a \cdot P_b
			 & =
			(\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X})
			(\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X})                              \\
			 & =
			\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot I_{m \times m} \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X} \\
			 & =
			\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot \bone[a=b]               \\
			 & =
			P_a \cdot \bone[a=b],
		\end{align*}
		where the second line uses \ref{lem:X-hat-squared}, the third uses that $T$ is projective, and the last uses \ref{lem:pa-restated}. Summing over $a$ shows $\sum_a P_a \leq I$, so $P$ is a projective sub-measurement.  The formalization also records the sharper identity
		\[
			\sum_a P_a=\widehat X^\dagger\widehat X,
		\]
		and the resulting total-domination estimates used later in the monotone-total self-improvement route.
	\end{proof}

	\begin{lemma}[$P$ is close to~$Q$] \begin{equation*}
			Q_a \ot I \approx_{30\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I.
		\end{equation*}
	\end{lemma}
	\begin{proof}
		
		
		The formal proof follows this argument directly from the primitive
		$X$, $\widehat X$, and $P$ identities; the $30\zeta^{1/4}$ estimate is
		derived here rather than stored as part of the reduced datum.  The
		unitary-group rectangular-SVD lemma combines the same estimate with the
		positive-square identification of the middle factor from
		\ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}; the square unitary factors are again carried as
		elements of the relevant unitary groups.  The
		positive-Gram sigma-space lemma also records the coisometry
		\(X X^\dagger=I\) for the original sigma embedding when the projective
		\(Q\)-family is subnormalized; this is the construction-level hypothesis
		later used to obtain the QXP-internal fresh-outcome comparison
		\(Q_{\mathrm{none}} \leq P_{\mathrm{none}}\).  An additional
		source-to-\(Q\) comparison is still needed for source-facing residual
		domination.
		The quantity to bound is
		\begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi}
			+
			\bra{\psi} P \ot I \ket{\psi}
			-
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}
			-
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi},
		\end{equation}
		using the projectivity of $Q$ and $P$. The first term is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, and the second is at most $1$ because $P$ is a sub-measurement.

		For the last two terms,
		\begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}
			+
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} P_aQ_a \ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			2 \cdot \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big).
		\end{equation}
		By \ref{lem:qa-restated},
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a) \ot I \ket{\psi}.
		\]
		The main estimate is
		\begin{equation} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}
			\approx_{2\zeta^{1/4}}
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}.
		\end{equation}
		This follows by Cauchy--Schwarz:
		\[
			\Big|\sum_a \bra{\psi} ((X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)) \ot I)\cdot(P_a \ot I)\ket{\psi}\Big|
		\]
		is bounded by the square root of
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} \big(X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger \cdot X_a\big)\ot I \ket{\psi},
		\]
		times the square root of $\sum_a \bra{\psi}(P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1$. The first factor is at most $4\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:squared-difference}, \ref{lem:X-expression-to-Q-expression}, and \ref{lem:q-almost-projective}, so the total error is at most $2\zeta^{1/4}$.

		The right-hand side of \ref{eq:add-a-hat} is real, because
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\bra{\psi} (X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}) \ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\bra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi},
		\]
		where the first equality uses \ref{lem:xa-t}, \ref{lem:pa-restated}, and \ref{lem:X-hat-squared} and that $T$ is a measurement, and the second uses \ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}. Hence \ref{lem:sqrt-Q-completeness} and \ref{eq:add-a-hat} imply
		\[
			\mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big)
			\geq
			1-14\zeta^{1/4}.
		\]
		Substituting this into \ref{eq:complex-conjugates} and then into \ref{eq:P-Q-thing-to-bound} gives
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\leq
			(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) + 1 - 2(1-14\zeta^{1/4})
			=
			2\sqrt{\zeta} + 28\zeta^{1/4}
			\leq
			30\zeta^{1/4}.
		\]
	\end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Inner lemmas: completeness, $Q/X/\widehat X/P$ algebra, $P\approx Q$.

nodes.name: Combine $A\approx Q$ and $Q\approx P$
nodes.statement:
Finally, \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum} gives
	\[
		A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I,
	\]
	and \ref{lem:P-Q-approx} gives
	\[
		Q_a \ot I \approx_{30\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I.
	\]

nodes.name: Triangle inequality gives $84\zeta^{1/4}$
nodes.statement:
The triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ yields
	\[
		A_a \ot I \approx_{84\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \ot I.
	\]

nodes.name: Case $x\ge1-\delta$: truncation is 1
nodes.statement:
If $x \geq 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$. Since $\delta \leq 1/2$ below, one also has $x \geq \delta$, so
		\[
			(x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2
			=
			(1-x)^2
			\leq
			(1-x)\frac{x}{\delta}
			=
			\frac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2).
		\]

nodes.name: Case $x<1-\delta$: truncation is 0
nodes.statement:
If $x < 1-\delta$, then $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=0$, and similarly
		\[
			(x-\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x))^2
			=
			x^2
			\leq
			x\frac{1-x}{\delta}
			=
			\frac{1}{\delta}(x-x^2).
		\]

nodes.name: Eigendecompose $A_a$
nodes.statement:
Write the eigendecomposition of $A_a$ as
		\[
			A_a = \sum_i \lambda_{a,i}\ket{u_{a,i}}\bra{u_{a,i}}.
		\]

nodes.name: Define $R_a$ by truncation
nodes.statement:
Choose
		\begin{equation} 0 < \delta \leq 1/2,
		\end{equation}
		define $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta:[0,1] \to \{0,1\}$ by $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x)=1$ when $x \geq 1-\delta$ and $0$ otherwise, and set
		\[
			R_a = \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(A_a)
			=
			\sum_i \mathsf{trunc}_\delta(\lambda_{a,i}) \ket{u_{a,i}}\bra{u_{a,i}}.
		\]

nodes.name: Operator truncation inequality
nodes.statement:
By \ref{lem:trunc-inequality},
		\[
			(A_a-R_a)^2
			\leq
			\frac{1}{\delta}(A_a-(A_a)^2).
		\]

nodes.name: $A\approx_{2\zeta/\delta}R$
nodes.statement:
Summing expectations and using \ref{eq:A-looks-projective} gives
		\[
			\sum_a \Vert (A_a-R_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2
			\leq
			\frac{2\zeta}{\delta},
		\]
		so $A_a \ot I \approx_{2\zeta/\delta} R_a \ot I$.

nodes.name: $R_a\le A_a/(1-\delta)$
nodes.statement:
For every $x \in [0,1]$, one has $\mathsf{trunc}_\delta(x) \leq x/(1-\delta)$, hence
		\[
			R_a \leq \frac{1}{1-\delta} A_a.
		\]

nodes.name: $R\le(1+2\delta)I$
nodes.statement:
Summing over $a$ and using that $A$ is a measurement,
		\[
			R = \sum_a R_a \leq \frac{1}{1-\delta} I \leq (1+2\delta)I,
		\]
		where the last estimate uses $\delta \leq 1/2$.

nodes.name: Choose $\delta=\sqrt\zeta$
nodes.statement: Setting $\delta=\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives the claim, and \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta} ensures $\delta \leq 1/2$.

nodes.name: Take $L$ maximizing the sum
nodes.statement: Choose $L$ to be a set of $d$ indices on which the sum of $f$ is maximal.

nodes.name: Exchange argument: small values below large
nodes.statement: If some $s \in S$ and $l \in L$ satisfied $f(l) < f(s)$, replacing $l$ by $s$ would increase this sum, so every small index is bounded by every large index.
nodes.statement_short: Exchange argument: small values below large.

nodes.name: Double count over $S\times L$
nodes.statement:
Summing the inequalities $f(s) \leq f(l)$ over all pairs $(s,l) \in S \times L$ gives
		\[
			|L|\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{l \in L} f(l).
		\]

nodes.name: Add to both sides
nodes.statement:
Since $\alpha$ is the disjoint union of $L$ and $S$, adding $|S|\sum_{s \in S} f(s)$ to both sides yields
		\[
			r\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq |S|\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x).
		\]

nodes.name: Bound $|S|/r$ and divide
nodes.statement:
The hypotheses $|L|=d$ and $r \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d$ imply $|S|/r \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Dividing by $r$ and using $\sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x) \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ gives
		\[
			\sum_{s \in S} f(s) \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}).
		\]

nodes.name: Use $\sqrt\zeta\le1/2$
nodes.statement: Finally, $\zeta \leq 1/4$ implies $\sqrt{\zeta} \leq 1/2$, and hence $2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}$.

nodes.name: Take $R_a$ from rounding; define ranks
nodes.statement: Let $\{R_a\}$ be given by \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement}. Write $r_a=\mathrm{rank}(R_a)$ and $r=\sum_a r_a$.

nodes.name: Case $r\le d$: $Q=R$
nodes.statement: If $r \leq d$, take $Q_a=R_a$.

nodes.name: Case $r>d$: discard small-overlap directions
nodes.statement:
Otherwise,
		\begin{equation} r
			=
			\sum_a r_a
			=
			\sum_a \Tr(R_a)
			=
			\Tr(R)
			\leq
			(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d.
		\end{equation}
		Let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,r_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $R_a$, so
		\[
			R_a = \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\]
		Define the overlaps
		\[
			o_{a,i} = \bra{\psi} (\ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}} \ot I)\ket{\psi}.
		\]
		Their total satisfies
		\begin{equation} \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} o_{a,i}
			=
			\bra{\psi} R \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\leq
			1+2\sqrt{\zeta}.
		\end{equation}
		Let $\mathsf{Large}$ be the set of the $d$ largest overlaps $o_{a,i}$, breaking ties arbitrarily, and let $\mathsf{Small}$ be the complement. Then
		\begin{equation} |\mathsf{Small}|
			=
			r-d
			\leq
			2\sqrt{\zeta}\,d
			\leq
			2\sqrt{\zeta}\,r,
		\end{equation}
		by \ref{eq:bound-on-r}. Averaging the overlaps over the $r$ indices gives
		\begin{equation} \sum_{(a,i)\in \mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i}
			\leq
			\frac{|\mathsf{Small}|}{r}\sum_{a,i} o_{a,i}
			\leq
			4\sqrt{\zeta},
		\end{equation}
		using \ref{eq:size-of-small-is-small}, \ref{eq:total-overlap}, and \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta}.

		For each $a$, let $\mathsf{Large}_a=\{i : (a,i)\in \mathsf{Large}\}$ and define
		\[
			Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Large}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\]
		Then $\sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a)=|\mathsf{Large}| \leq d$, and $Q_a \leq R_a$ for every $a$, so
		\[
			Q = \sum_a Q_a \leq \sum_a R_a = R \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I.
		\]
		Also,
		\[
			R_a-Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Small}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}
		\]
		is a projector, hence
		\[
			\sum_a \Vert (R_a-Q_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2
			=
			\sum_{(a,i)\in\mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i}
			\leq
			4\sqrt{\zeta}
		\]
		by \ref{eq:small-overlaps}. Therefore $R_a \ot I \approx_{4\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I$. Combining this with \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement} and the triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ gives
		\[
			A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I.
		\]

nodes.name: Bound $r\le(1+2\sqrt\zeta)d$
nodes.statement:
Otherwise,
		\begin{equation} r
			=
			\sum_a r_a
			=
			\sum_a \Tr(R_a)
			=
			\Tr(R)
			\leq
			(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})d.
		\end{equation}

nodes.name: Orthonormal basis of ranges
nodes.statement:
Let $\ket{v_{a,1}},\ldots,\ket{v_{a,r_a}}$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $R_a$, so
		\[
			R_a = \sum_{i=1}^{r_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\]

nodes.name: Define overlaps $o_{a,i}$
nodes.statement:
Define the overlaps
		\[
			o_{a,i} = \bra{\psi} (\ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}} \ot I)\ket{\psi}.
		\]

nodes.name: Total overlap bound
Split into Large and Small
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathsf{Large}$ be the set of the $d$ largest overlaps $o_{a,i}$, breaking ties arbitrarily, and let $\mathsf{Small}$ be the complement. Then
		\begin{equation} |\mathsf{Small}|
			=
			r-d
			\leq
			2\sqrt{\zeta}\,d
			\leq
			2\sqrt{\zeta}\,r,
		\end{equation}
		by \ref{eq:bound-on-r}.

nodes.name: Small overlaps total $\le4\sqrt\zeta$
Define $Q_a$ from Large
nodes.statement:
For each $a$, let $\mathsf{Large}_a=\{i : (a,i)\in \mathsf{Large}\}$ and define
		\[
			Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Large}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}.
		\]

nodes.name: Rank and norm bounds for $Q$
nodes.statement:
Then $\sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a)=|\mathsf{Large}| \leq d$, and $Q_a \leq R_a$ for every $a$, so
		\[
			Q = \sum_a Q_a \leq \sum_a R_a = R \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I.
		\]

nodes.name: $R\approx_{4\sqrt\zeta}Q$
nodes.statement:
Also,
		\[
			R_a-Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Small}_a} \ket{v_{a,i}}\bra{v_{a,i}}
		\]
		is a projector, hence
		\[
			\sum_a \Vert (R_a-Q_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2
			=
			\sum_{(a,i)\in\mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i}
			\leq
			4\sqrt{\zeta}
		\]
		by \ref{eq:small-overlaps}. Therefore $R_a \ot I \approx_{4\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality gives $12\sqrt\zeta$
nodes.statement:
Combining this with \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement} and the triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ gives
		\[
			A_a \ot I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \ot I.
		\]

nodes.name: Rewrite and compare with $Q_aA_a$
Norm bounds from rank reduction
nodes.statement:
By Cauchy--Schwarz,
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta}
			\quad\text{and}\quad
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-A_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 12\sqrt{\zeta}
		\]
		from \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}.

nodes.name: Compare $Q_aA_a$ with $A_a^2$
Combine to get $1-11\zeta^{1/4}$
nodes.statement:
Combining \ref{eq:Q-for-an-A} and \ref{eq:another-Q-for-A} with \ref{eq:A-looks-projective} gives
		\[
			\bra{\psi} Q \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\geq
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \ot I \ket{\psi} - 2\zeta - 9\zeta^{1/4}
			=
			1 - 11\zeta^{1/4},
		\]
		since $\zeta \leq \zeta^{1/4}$ under \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta}.

nodes.name: Diagonalize $Q$
nodes.statement: Diagonalize $Q=\sum_i \nu_i \ket{u_i}\bra{u_i}$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue bound gives $\sqrt Q\ge Q/\sqrt{1+2\sqrt\zeta}$
nodes.statement:
Because $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, each $\nu_i$ is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Therefore
		\[
			\sqrt{Q}
			=
			\sum_i \sqrt{\nu_i}\ket{u_i}\bra{u_i}
			\geq
			\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} Q.
		\]

nodes.name: Scalar estimate
nodes.statement:
The scalar estimate
		\[
			\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} \geq 1-\sqrt{\zeta}
		\]
		gives $\sqrt{Q} \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})Q$.

nodes.name: Apply completeness of $Q$
nodes.statement:
Hence \ref{lem:Q-completeness} implies
		\[
			\bra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\geq
			(1-\sqrt{\zeta})(1-11\zeta^{1/4})
			\geq
			1-12\zeta^{1/4}.
		\]

nodes.name: Apply finite-dimensional SVD
nodes.statement:
Apply the finite-dimensional singular value decomposition to \(X\) and
		record exactly the consequences used later: the identities for
		\(X^\dagger X\), \(\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger\),
		\(X^\dagger\widehat X\), and the restatement of the \(Q_a\)'s.

nodes.name: Unitary-group variant is the same calculation
nodes.statement:
The
		unitary-group constructors are the same rectangular-SVD calculation, with
		the square factors taken as elements of the relevant unitary groups
		rather than as matrices accompanied by separate unitarity equations.
nodes.statement_short: Unitary-group variant is the same calculation.

nodes.name: Sigma-range carrier identification
nodes.statement:
In
		the sigma-range specialization, the auxiliary row space is the lifted
		finite-enumeration carrier associated to the ranks of the \(Q_a\)'s, which
		is definitionally the carrier of the canonical sigma-range \(Q\)-layer.

nodes.name: Sum the restated $Q_a$
nodes.statement:
Use that $T$ is a measurement and then \ref{lem:qa-restated}:
		\[
			X^\dagger \cdot X
			=
			\sum_a X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X
			=
			\sum_a Q_a
			=
			Q.
		\]

nodes.name: Other SVD identities are standard
nodes.statement:
The additional paper identities involving $U,V,\Sigma$ are the usual SVD
		computations.

nodes.name: Lean spectral side-facts
nodes.statement:
The Lean development also records the spectral calculation
		which will identify the mixed positive-Gram-image product with
		$\sqrt Q$: the positive eigenvalues give the nonzero columns, while the
		zero eigenspace has zero coefficient in the square-root expansion and is
		killed by $X$.  The conjugate right-eigenvector rows over the positive
		spectrum are also orthonormal.  Equivalently, any row-space vector
		orthogonal to the positive Gram images is killed by $X^\dagger$.

nodes.name: Paper proof via unitarity
nodes.statement:
The paper proves this by multiplying out
		$\widehat{X}=U\cdot I_{m\times d}\cdot V^\dagger$ and using the unitarity of
		$U$ and $V$.

nodes.name: Lean: coisometry from dimension bound
nodes.statement:
In Lean, the dimension hypothesis $m\leq d$ already gives a
		rectangular matrix with orthonormal rows on the sigma auxiliary space; the
		chosen matrix \texttt{sigmaFinXHatCoisometry} and its specification record this
		existence result as a hypothesis for the future construction.

nodes.name: Normalization and row-coisometry lemmas
nodes.statement:
The formal lemma
		\texttt{orthonormal\_normalized\_image\_of\_adjoint\_comp\_eigenvectors}
		records the singular-vector normalization calculation, while
		\texttt{normalized\_matrix\_image\_rows\_mul\_conjTranspose} combines the
		corresponding row-coisometry identity, and
		\texttt{positive\_gram\_spectrum\_image\_rows\_transpose\_mixed} records the
		adjoint action $X^\dagger(\lambda^{-1/2}Xv)=\lambda^{1/2}v$ on the positive
		spectral part of the Gram operator.

nodes.name: Extend rows to a unitary
nodes.statement:
The formal lemma
		\texttt{exists\_unitaryGroup\_with\_positive\_gram\_spectrum\_rows} records the
		next finite-dimensional step: after choosing distinct row positions for the
		positive spectrum, these normalized image rows extend to a square unitary
		group element on the row space.

nodes.name: Rectangular completion
nodes.statement:
The companion lemma
		\texttt{exists\_rectangular\_coisometry\_extending\_orthonormal\_rows}
		records the analogous rectangular completion for prescribed right rows
		when the dimension bound permits it.

nodes.name: Unitary-preservation steps
nodes.statement:
The formal lemma
		\texttt{unitaryGroup\_mul\_rectangular\_coisometry} and its right-multiplication
		companion
		\texttt{rectangular\_coisometry\_mul\_conjTranspose\_unitaryGroup} record the
		two unitary-preservation steps in the paper's multiplication.  The formal
		lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_coisometry\_unitaryGroup} applies these
		preservation steps to the rectangular-SVD expression.

nodes.name: Unconditional construction of $\widehat X$
nodes.statement:
The
		unconditional positive-Gram route is
		\texttt{exists\_xHat\_of\_sigmaFinRangeEmbedding\_positiveGram}, which
		constructs $\widehat X$ from the rank-reduction witness and proves
		$\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$ together with the mixed square-root
		identity below.

nodes.name: Paper derivation from SVD
nodes.statement:
The paper obtains this from the SVD formula for $X$ and the definition of
		$\widehat X$.

nodes.name: $X\widehat X^\dagger$ is Hermitian positive
nodes.statement:
In Lean, the unconditional QXP data first proves that
		$X\widehat X^\dagger$ is Hermitian and positive.

nodes.name: Spectral theorem gives $U\Sigma U^\dagger$
nodes.statement:
The formal lemma
		\texttt{x\_mul\_xHat\_adjoint\_spectral\_theorem} then applies Mathlib's
		spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, giving the displayed
		$U\Sigma U^\dagger$ form with the Mathlib eigenvector unitary and the
		diagonal matrix of real eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Same under explicit SVD data
nodes.statement:
The auxiliary lemma
		\texttt{rectangularSvd\_x\_mul\_xHat\_conjTranspose\_raw} records the same
		calculation under explicit rectangular-SVD data, where the middle factor
		\(S I_{m\times d}^\dagger\) is the formal square matrix
		\(\Sigma_{m\times m}\).

nodes.name: Mixed product equals $\sqrt Q$
nodes.statement:
The formal lemma
		\texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_mixed\_of\_sqrtQ\_unitaryGroup} records the
		second matrix calculation in the form whose square-root target is the
		operator $Q$ supplied by the QXP construction.  The formal lemma
		\texttt{rectangularSvd\_middle\_eq\_sqrt\_of\_square} records the spectral
		step: a positive middle factor whose square is $Q$ is the positive square
		root of $Q$.

nodes.name: Recorded as primitive consequence
nodes.statement:
The reduced datum then records this mixed-product
		identity as a primitive consequence, which is exactly the part needed in
		\ref{lem:squared-difference} and \ref{lem:P-Q-approx}.

nodes.name: Paper uses SVD diagonalization
nodes.statement:
The paper diagonalizes the positive operator $X\widehat X^\dagger$ using the
		SVD notation.

nodes.name: Set $Y=X\widehat X^\dagger$
nodes.statement:
The formal proof avoids storing that SVD explicitly: set
		$Y=X\widehat X^\dagger$.

nodes.name: $Y$ Hermitian, nonnegative, $Y^2=XX^\dagger$
nodes.statement:
The primitive identities imply that $Y$ is
		hermitian, nonnegative, and satisfies $Y^2=XX^\dagger$.

nodes.name: Positivity gives the inequality
nodes.statement:
Hence
		$(X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger=(Y-I)^2$, and positivity of $Y$ gives
		$(Y-I)^2\leq(Y^2-I)^2=(XX^\dagger-I)^2$.

nodes.name: $P_aP_b=\delta_{ab}P_a$
nodes.statement:
For outcomes $a,b$,
		\begin{align*}
			P_a \cdot P_b
			 & =
			(\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X})
			(\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X})                              \\
			 & =
			\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot I_{m \times m} \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X} \\
			 & =
			\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot \bone[a=b]               \\
			 & =
			P_a \cdot \bone[a=b],
		\end{align*}
		where the second line uses \ref{lem:X-hat-squared}, the third uses that $T$ is projective, and the last uses \ref{lem:pa-restated}.

nodes.name: Sum is at most $I$
nodes.statement: Summing over $a$ shows $\sum_a P_a \leq I$, so $P$ is a projective sub-measurement.

nodes.name: Sharper total identity recorded
nodes.statement:
The formalization also records the sharper identity
		\[
			\sum_a P_a=\widehat X^\dagger\widehat X,
		\]
		and the resulting total-domination estimates used later in the monotone-total self-improvement route.

nodes.name: Lean bookkeeping notes
nodes.statement:
The formal proof follows this argument directly from the primitive
		$X$, $\widehat X$, and $P$ identities; the $30\zeta^{1/4}$ estimate is
		derived here rather than stored as part of the reduced datum.  The
		unitary-group rectangular-SVD lemma combines the same estimate with the
		positive-square identification of the middle factor from
		\ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}; the square unitary factors are again carried as
		elements of the relevant unitary groups.  The
		positive-Gram sigma-space lemma also records the coisometry
		\(X X^\dagger=I\) for the original sigma embedding when the projective
		\(Q\)-family is subnormalized; this is the construction-level hypothesis
		later used to obtain the QXP-internal fresh-outcome comparison
		\(Q_{\mathrm{none}} \leq P_{\mathrm{none}}\).  An additional
		source-to-\(Q\) comparison is still needed for source-facing residual
		domination.

nodes.name: Expand the squared difference
Bound the mass terms
nodes.statement: The first term is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, and the second is at most $1$ because $P$ is a sub-measurement.

nodes.name: Cross terms are $2\Re$
Rewrite via $X_a^\dagger X$
nodes.statement:
By \ref{lem:qa-restated},
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a) \ot I \ket{\psi}.
		\]

nodes.name: Replace $X$ by $\widehat X$
Cauchy--Schwarz split
nodes.statement:
This follows by Cauchy--Schwarz:
		\[
			\Big|\sum_a \bra{\psi} ((X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)) \ot I)\cdot(P_a \ot I)\ket{\psi}\Big|
		\]
		is bounded by the square root of
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} \big(X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger \cdot X_a\big)\ot I \ket{\psi},
		\]
		times the square root of $\sum_a \bra{\psi}(P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi} \leq 1$.

nodes.name: First factor $\le4\sqrt\zeta$
nodes.statement: The first factor is at most $4\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:squared-difference}, \ref{lem:X-expression-to-Q-expression}, and \ref{lem:q-almost-projective}, so the total error is at most $2\zeta^{1/4}$.

nodes.name: It equals $\langle\sqrt Q\rangle$
nodes.statement:
The right-hand side of \ref{eq:add-a-hat} is real, because
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\bra{\psi} (X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}) \ot I \ket{\psi}
			=
			\bra{\psi} \sqrt{Q} \ot I \ket{\psi},
		\]
		where the first equality uses \ref{lem:xa-t}, \ref{lem:pa-restated}, and \ref{lem:X-hat-squared} and that $T$ is a measurement, and the second uses \ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}.

nodes.name: Real part $\ge1-14\zeta^{1/4}$
nodes.statement:
Hence \ref{lem:sqrt-Q-completeness} and \ref{eq:add-a-hat} imply
		\[
			\mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \bra{\psi} Q_aP_a \ot I \ket{\psi}\Big)
			\geq
			1-14\zeta^{1/4}.
		\]

nodes.name: Total $\le30\zeta^{1/4}$
nodes.statement:
Substituting this into \ref{eq:complex-conjugates} and then into \ref{eq:P-Q-thing-to-bound} gives
		\[
			\sum_a \bra{\psi} (Q_a-P_a)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}
			\leq
			(1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) + 1 - 2(1-14\zeta^{1/4})
			=
			2\sqrt{\zeta} + 28\zeta^{1/4}
			\leq
			30\zeta^{1/4}.
		\]

nodes.name: Orthonormality
Inner products via character orthogonality
Orthonormal basis
nodes.statement: Thus the $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ form an orthonormal basis of $\C^V$.

nodes.name: Eigenvector property
nodes.statement:
Next we prove \ref{item:eigenvector}. For $\alpha \in \F_q^m$,
	\begin{equation}
		\begin{aligned}
			K \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha}
			 & =
			\left(\E_{(u,v)\sim C} \ket{u}\bra{v}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}\right) \\
			 & =
			\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(v\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}.
		\end{aligned} \end{equation}
	By the edge-sampling rule from Definition~\ref{def:hypercube-graph}, we may write $v=u+x e_i$, where $i$ is uniformly random in $\{1,\dots,m\}$ and $x$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$. Therefore
	\[
		\eqref{eq:eigenvector-calculation}
		=
		\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \E_{u,i,x} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}((u+x e_i)\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}
		=
		\left(\E_{i,x}\omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \E_u \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \ket{u}
		=
		\frac{1}{M}\left(\E_{i,x}\omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right) \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha}.
	\]
	Hence $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ is an eigenvector of $K$ with eigenvalue
	\[
		\frac{1}{M} \cdot \E_i \left[\E_x \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right]
		=
		\frac{1}{M} \cdot \E_i \left[\bone[\alpha_i=0]\right]
		=
		\frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-|\alpha|}{m},
	\]
	by Lemma~\ref{lem:character-average-scalar}.

nodes.name: Apply $K$ to $|\varphi_\alpha\rangle$
Substitute $v=u+xe_i$
Eigenvalue via scalar character average
nodes.statement:
Hence $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ is an eigenvector of $K$ with eigenvalue
	\[
		\frac{1}{M} \cdot \E_i \left[\E_x \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right]
		=
		\frac{1}{M} \cdot \E_i \left[\bone[\alpha_i=0]\right]
		=
		\frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-|\alpha|}{m},
	\]
	by Lemma~\ref{lem:character-average-scalar}.

nodes.name: Action of edge differences on $A_{\mathrm{comb}}$
Laplacian rewrite
nodes.statement:
Therefore
	\[
		A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}}
		=
		\frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger \bigl((\ket{u}-\ket{v})(\bra{u}-\bra{v}) \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}\bigr) A_{\mathrm{comb}}
	\]
	by Lemma~\ref{prop:laplacian-rewrite}, and hence
	\[
		A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}}
		=
		\frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} ((A^u-A^v)\ot I)\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}((A^u-A^v)\ot I)
	\]
	by \eqref{eq:edge-difference-action}.

nodes.name: Take trace
nodes.statement:
Taking the trace gives
	\[
		\Tr(A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}})
		=
		\frac12 \E_{(u,v)\sim C} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A^v)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}
		=
		\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi).
	\]

nodes.name: Compute $A_0$
nodes.statement:
We first compute
	\[
		A_0
		=
		(\bra{\varphi_0}\ot I)\cdot A_{\mathrm{comb}}
		=
		\left(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \bra{u}\right) \ot I \cdot \left(\sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \ket{u} \ot A^u \ot I\right)
		=
		\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \F_q^m} A^u \ot I.
	\]

nodes.name: Decompose into average and fluctuation
nodes.statement:
Writing $A_{\mathrm{avg}}=\E_u A^u$, it follows that
	\[
		\ket{\varphi_0}\ot A_0
		=
		\sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \ket{u} \ot A_{\mathrm{avg}} \ot I,
		\qquad
		\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp
		=
		\sum_{u \in \F_q^m} \ket{u} \ot (A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \ot I.
	\]

nodes.name: Trace of orthogonal part
Variance identity
nodes.statement:
Moreover,
	\[
		\E_{u \sim \F_q^m}(A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2
		=
		\E_{u \sim \F_q^m}\bigl((A^u)^2-(A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2\bigr)
		=
		\frac12 \E_{u,v \sim \F_q^m} (A^u-A^v)^2.
	\]

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
Substituting this identity into \eqref{eq:just-took-trace} yields
	\[
		\frac{1}{M} \cdot \Tr((\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(I\ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp))
		=
		\frac12 \E_{u,v \sim \F_q^m} \bra{\psi} (A^u-A^v)^2 \ot I \ket{\psi}
		=
		\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi).
	\]

nodes.name: Laplacian kills $|\varphi_0\rangle$ component
Spectral gap bound
nodes.statement:
Since $\ket{\varphi_\perp}$ is orthogonal to $\ket{\varphi_0}$, Lemma~\ref{cor:laplacian-spectral-gap} gives
	\[
		\bra{\varphi_\perp}L\ket{\varphi_\perp}
		\ge
		\frac{1}{mM} \cdot \braket{\varphi_\perp}{\varphi_\perp}.
	\]

nodes.name: Combine with local and global rewrites
nodes.statement:
Therefore
	\[
		\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi)
		=
		\Tr(A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) A_{\mathrm{comb}})
		=
		\bra{\varphi_\perp}L\ket{\varphi_\perp} \cdot \Tr(A_\perp \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} A_\perp)
	\]
	by Lemma~\ref{lem:local-rewrite} and \eqref{eq:used-0-eigenvector}, so
	\[
		\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi)
		\ge
		\frac{1}{mM} \cdot \Tr((\bra{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp)(I\ot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})(\ket{\varphi_\perp}\ot A_\perp))
		=
		\frac{1}{m}\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi),
	\]
	where the last step is Lemma~\ref{lem:global-rewrite}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with local and global rewrites.

nodes.name: Take optimal SDP primal $T$ and dual $Z$
nodes.statement_short: Take optimal SDP primal $T$ and dual $Z$.

nodes.name: Define $H^u_h$ and $H_h$
nodes.statement:
For each $u \in \F_q^m$, define $H^u=\{H_h^u\}_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}$ by
  \[
    H_h^u := A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)},
  \]
  and let
  \[
    H_h := \E_{u} H_h^u.
  \]

nodes.name: $H$ is a sub-measurement
nodes.statement:
The pointwise family $H^u$ is a submeasurement because
  \[
    \sum_h H_h^u
    = \sum_a A_a^u \cdot \Big(\sum_{h:h(u)=a} T_h\Big)\cdot A_a^u
    \le \sum_a (A_a^u)^2
    = I,
  \]
  where the inequality uses that~$T$ is a measurement and the last identity uses
  that~$A$ is projective. Averaging over~$u$ gives
  \[
    \sum_h H_h
    = \E_{u} \sum_h H_h^u
    \le I,
  \]
  so $H$ is also a submeasurement and therefore lies in~$\polysub{m}{q}{d}$.

nodes.name: Define $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$
nodes.statement:
Set
  \[
    \zeta_{\mathrm{variance}} = 24m\cdot\Big(\eps + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\Big).
  \]

nodes.name: Plan: use add-in-$u$ for all four conclusions
nodes.statement:
Lemma~\ref{lem:add-in-u} below is the technical transfer from the averaged family~$H$ back to the sandwiched operators $A^u_{h(u)}T_hA^u_{h(u)}$. We use it in the completeness, consistency, strong self-consistency, and boundedness estimates that follow.

  We now verify the four conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement-helper}.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: use add-in-$u$ for all four conclusions.

nodes.name: Completeness
Expand completeness
Group by value at $u$

Remove the right copy
nodes.statement:
We next remove the remaining copy of~$A^u_a$ on Bob's side:
  \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:first-point-projector-transport}
    \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}}
    \E_{u} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \bigl(T_{[h(u)=a]} \cdot A^{u}_{a}\bigr) \ot I \ket{\psi}.
  \end{equation}
  The first Cauchy--Schwarz factor is at most~$1$ because the fiber operators form a submeasurement after grouping~$T$ by the value of~$h(u)$.
  
  
  
  Here the second Cauchy--Schwarz factor is
  \[
    \E_{u} \sum_{a\neq b} \bra{\psi} A^u_a \ot A^u_b \ket{\psi},
  \]
  which is at most~$\delta$ because~$A$ is self-consistent and projective.

nodes.statement:
\emph{Proof of \ref{item:self-improvement-A-consistency}.}
  The inconsistency of~$H$ with~$A$ is
  \begin{equation} \E_{u} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{u}_a \ot H_{[h(u) = b]} \ket{\psi}
    = \E_{u} \sum_{a, h: h(u) \neq a} \bra{\psi} A^{u}_a \ot H_h \ket{\psi}.
  \end{equation}

  \[
    \eqref{eq:point-consistency-expansion}
    \approx_{4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}}
    \E_{u} \sum_{a, h: h(u) \neq a} \bra{\psi} \bigl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot A^{u}_a \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)}\bigr)\ot T_h \ket{\psi},
